Title: GravaStar Mercury M2 Wireless Gaming Mouse, 5 Dynamic Lightsync RGB (White)

Category: Video Games,PC,Accessories,Gaming Mice
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "De De", "review_title": "Mercury m2 mouse", "review_text": "Absolutely amazing. Upgrade from razer deathadder v3. Sounds amazing, looks amazing, feels amazing. Best value mouse for its price. Also comes with cable and stickers which is a nice touch. The mouse connects instantly with no setup required, had amazing response, and is build great. 10/10 mouse", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "ana sophia", "review_title": "Yes, it IS worth your money!", "review_text": "Fantastic mouse for gaming and work! Comfortable for smaller hands, and is really beautiful alongside the Mercury K1 keyboard in white. Worth the wait to have a matching set. I notice a huge difference between my ergonomic mouse and this one for responsiveness and DPI settings. As someone who has to use the scroll wheel a lot I find it really satisfying with good haptic feedback. Fully customizable button mapping and rgb settings puts the cherry on top. If you’ve been wondering whether it’s worth splashing out on along with the keyboard, DO IT! They make for such a clean setup, I’ve loved every bit of my Gravastar kit.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "William", "review_title": "Buy under $80 and you get an absolute GEM", "review_text": "Beautiful mouse.
The webby design is beautiful but on the right side for Claw and Fingertip Grips makes for a very awkward seat for the fingers, palm grip is not an issue because there are grated flat surfaces toward the front of each side that is very accommodating for the thumb and fingers but I personally like to grip with my fingertips curled around the side, fingertips sitting vertically in the middle rather than fully straight and riding horizontally along the side. This completely avoids that surface meant for fingers and relies on the webbed design for support which is a little off feeling. By no means does this make it unusable, you just have to get used to it. My ring fingertip generally makes contact with that grated support surface but my pinky sits further back and I have to set it on the skinny web part.
This does not make the mouse unusable I just believe it justifies $60 over $80, this oddity in the design applies to all of GravaStar's mice.
Overall the PAW3395 is the best widespread sensor to date, yes there are better sensors but they are not generational leaps, they're just small improvements and support gimmicks like 4k and 8k polling when there is no proven practical increase over 2K, the specs of this mouse and the quality of the wireless (and bluetooth)- are pretty unbeatable at $60, $80 I'd say if you really want the design of this mouse, go for it, but this thing is always on sale.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Silas Growden", "review_title": "Fantastic Design and Quality, but Too Small", "review_text": "I’m going to give this mouse 5 stars, even though I won’t be using it.
It is exactly what is pictured. The internal LED is very well-diffused and easy to customize with Gravastar’s software. The sensor is extremely accurate. The mouse has negligible latency in both configurations, and is very smooth across my mousepad. The buttons feel excellent, and the ergonomics are pretty good: buttons are where you need them to be without being in the way.
Why won’t I be using it then? The size. It’s too small for me. I was very sad when I gave it a try, and it just didn’t fill my hand as well as my other mouse (Razer DeathAdder V2 X).
Gravastar is a fantastic company that makes quality products with a distinct style. I love their keyboard, their chargers, and their speakers. My wife has the Sakura pink version of this mouse that matches her keyboard, and she LOVES it. So I would recommend this mouse on the basis of its quality and its style to anyone, with the caveat that it’s just not the best fit for larger hands. If you’re used to a smaller mouse like a Logitech, then maybe this would be close to what you’re used to anyway, but for me, I’m more comfortable on my DeathAdder.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Zarina", "review_title": "Great mouse!", "review_text": "I got it as a gift for my sister! She LOVED it! It works great and looks really good.
She wanted a transparent one and it is lightweight, smooth and easy to connect to the laptop.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "casey S", "review_title": "Super beautiful. Low latency. Wish it was Bigger", "review_text": "Ive been using this mouse for about a month now, so far its golding up well! The mouse is beautiful. What I love about Gravastar is their unapologetically futuristic cyberpunk designs. The look of the mouse is beautiful and is exactly what I was looking for when I searched "futuristic mouse".
As far as performance, I've had no issue with it at all. The latency is extremely low (practically non existent in my experience). Both wireless and wired feel very responsive. It's very lightweight also. I haven't used the windows app yet, but from what I've seen. You can customize the rgb a bit and program the 2 side buttons and the top one near the scroll wheel.
2 gripes:
1. The design of the mouse can make it difficult to wipe the inner part of the mouse. If it gets dusty. But I guess that's the trade off for a beautiful design. Not a deal breaker.
2. It's relatively small, I have fairly large hands. So it's easy for it to slip out of my hands when it gets sweaty. They're not abnormally large, but big enough to make my hand cramp up after an hour or 2 of playing.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Kenny", "review_title": "Ok... I like it!", "review_text": "You'll either love or hate the look of this mouse. Definitely a love for me! Glides effortlessly, ergonomics are perfect for me. Haven't tested the battery life yet, but it comes about 50% charged. This is my 1st product from this company so if it holds up, it'll be good vaule for money compared to bigger brands. You can choose to download the software or use their web app. You can changed RGB colors, adjust DPI, etc. Zero issues with tracking so far. Would recommend.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "with_teeth100", "review_title": "I will never use any other from now on", "review_text": "🔥 Review: Mercury M2 Wireless Gaming Mouse 🔥
The Mercury M2 Wireless Gaming Mouse is an absolute weapon in the hands of any serious gamer. From the moment I unboxed it, I could tell this wasn’t just another “me too” peripheral—it’s a precision tool built for dominance.
The wireless response time feels indistinguishable from wired, which is insane considering how most wireless mice still struggle to match that level of speed and accuracy. Every click lands instantly, every flick registers without delay. It’s as if the M2 is reading my mind before my fingers move.
The ergonomic design deserves a standing ovation. It fits the hand like it was carved for it—no awkward angles, no fatigue after hours of gaming. The textured side grips are a small detail, but they make a massive difference during sweaty high-pressure matches.
And the sensor performance? Ruthless. Tracking is flawless, even at absurd DPI ranges. Whether I’m micro-adjusting for a pixel-perfect headshot or whipping across a 4K screen in a split-second, the Mercury M2 never loses its nerve. It’s a beast that adapts to every playstyle.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Reaverz0r", "review_title": "Great mouse!", "review_text": "AMAZING mouse!

Title: Razer Basilisk V3 Customizable RGB Wired Ergonomic Gaming Mouse, Black
Description: ICONIC ERGONOMIC DESIGN WITH THUMB REST — PC gaming mouse favored by millions worldwide with a form factor that perfectly supports the hand while its buttons are optimally positioned for quick and easy access
Category: Electronics,Computers & Accessories,Computer Accessories & Peripherals,Keyboards, Mice & Accessories,Mice
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Yahia B.", "review_title": "Love the switch", "review_text": "I used the Razer Mamba Elite for many years and absolutely loved it, so I was hesitant to switch. This mouse was recommended to me as a replacement, and I have been pleasantly surprised. It feels comfortable in the hand, responds quickly, and the customizable buttons and RGB lighting are excellent. The scroll wheel is especially smooth and versatile. Overall, it has been a great change and I am very happy with it.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Amazon Customer", "review_title": "Yes! Beats the G502 Hero (which I liked) and the G502 X (by a lot)", "review_text": "Good god, what a mouse. I mean, it's not perfect; nothing is. But it's so good.
I came from years of the G502 Hero; the grips on it were wearing out. I first decided to try a G502 X, as it was supposed to be an improved version of the Hero, essentially. For $25 more than the Basilisk, it pretty much sucked in my opinion. The only thing I could imagine picking it over the Basilisk for is weight. But if you care that much about weight, there are much lighter mice on the market.
---
I'll review it as compared to the Hero (and a bit to the X), as that's what I know. They're pretty common, so maybe this will help people out if they're thinking about converting:
Initially I wasn't so sure about the grip and the main mouse buttons. The mouse buttons have a rough texture, and I found with my Hero that when my fingers were slightly tacky/damp, they would stick slightly to the surface of the buttons in the same way a clean basketball shoe does to a court (i.e., not "sticky", but grippy). I liked that. But after using it for a while, I think it's totally fine and maybe even better.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Dallas Barnes", "review_title": "One of my favorite mice and you will love it too", "review_text": "This mouse is just incredibly smooth. Even with its high weight the skates make it super easy to move around and the weight gives it control, resulting in superb aim. The material can make your hands a bit sweaty when death gripping it, but it’s very solid matte surface. You can grip test and throw this mouse across a room without it breaking. The shape this mouse has just fits right in your hand, and the rubber side grips make it super comfortable and easy to use, it’s basically great with any grip type. The skates are super glidey and quiet even when under the weight of this chunker of a mouse. It’s better for bigger hands of course, it’s harder to use with smaller hands but it’s doable. The scroll wheel is the best of any mouse, even the Logitech g502. It has a setting in the software where it can be a tactile scroll wheel when scrolling slowly, but becomes a freely spinning wheel when flicked fast. You can even switch between spinny wheel mode and tactile mode with the click of a button. I loved this mouse so much I upgraded to the wireless version, and I wasn’t sacrificing much leaving wired because the battery life was great on that one. 10/10 mouse.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Louis Barber", "review_title": "Great for the price.", "review_text": "The Razer Basilisk V3 is hands down one of the best gaming mice I've ever used. It's super comfy even during long gaming sessions thanks to its ergonomic design, and the customizable buttons are perfect for both gaming and getting stuff done. The RGB lighting looks awesome, and the HyperScroll wheel is surprisingly handy for switching between precise and fast scrolling.
The sensor is super accurate and responsive, and the mouse just glides across my mousepad. I also love how easy it is to customize everything through Razer Synapse. Whether I'm playing FPS games, MMOs, or just browsing, this mouse works perfectly.
If you want a top-notch gaming mouse with tons of customization and excellent comfort, the Basilisk V3 is totally worth it. Highly recommended!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Noah Schreiber", "review_title": "Good gaming mouse and does what it needs. Just wish it would last longer.", "review_text": "To be honest they don't make mice like they used to. I remember a time where you would buy gaming mice and they would last 5 years minimum. Now a days they last a year if you are lucky. So far this mouse has worked pretty good and seems like it is holding up quite fine. I also want to point out I haven't had this for a very long time and I suspect the build quality of the mouse should last a year if this was anything like my old razor mouse.
The scroll wheel is pretty solid. I like how responsive it is. I have never seen a mouse scroll wheel quite like this. Scrolling speed is pretty good. Was able to do a lot of jagged movements and noticed the mouse handled it very well in minecraft.
Ergonomic of the mouse are probably the best part. I haven't used a non trackball mouse that felt this great in maybe ever. The programmable buttons I haven't used for anything since I literally have nothing to remotely use them for whatsoever.
RGB is decent. Not a selling point for me that is a selling point for some people I guess.
With that said I am not sure if I can recommend this just because it seems pretty good but the way gaming mice have been going I don't see this lasting more than a year. I remember a time where mice would last like a decade now they break if you look at them the wrong way. I will say the big pro to a gaming mouse is the fact it is meant for gaming. Yes you are paying a lot of money for something that will break within a year but you pretty much have no choice just because these mice have a sensor in them that is significantly way better than most mice.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "BearFire", "review_title": "This Mouse Ruined Cheap Mice for Me", "review_text": "I’ve genuinely liked using the Razer Basilisk V3. The first thing I noticed was how comfortable it felt. Some mice are fine for about 20 minutes and then they start feeling like a weirdly shaped brick. This mouse has been much better for longer use, whether I’m gaming or just clicking around online doing whatever nonsense I got distracted by.
What I like most is that it feels like someone actually thought about how a hand works. The buttons are responsive, the movement is smooth, and the scroll wheel feels so nice that it almost made reading comment sections worth it. Almost. While this mouse has not been life changing in a dramatic movie soundtrack kind of way, it has changed my expectations enough that going back to a cheaper mouse would feel like using a shopping cart with one bad wheel.
Oh, and the customization. I am not out here trying to launch a space mission from my desk, but it is nice being able to set things up in a way that actually fits how I use it. Once everything is dialed in, it just feels easy.
Overall, it has been a genuinely solid mouse and one of those upgrades you stop thinking about because it just quietly does its job well. Which, for a mouse, is honestly the dream. It just sits there, minds its business, and makes me slightly more powerful than I probably deserve.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Troy", "review_title": "Excellent & totally worth it.", "review_text": "Best mouse I've ever used. Every surface is comfortable to touch & adds to its controllability. The RMB & LMB are soft & responsive, and have a quick reset. Easy to hold & thumb rest allows for greater control during long use.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Michael", "review_title": "Peak Gaming Mouse Energy", "review_text": "This mouse is basically the “I’m him” of gaming mice. It’s super comfortable, the buttons feel crisp, and the 26K DPI sensor tracks like it’s reading your mind. The RGB lighting goes full rave mode (in a good way), and the HyperScroll wheel is clutch whether you’re swapping weapons or doom‑scrolling.
The 11 programmable buttons give you all the customization you could want, and the whole thing just feels premium. It’s fast, smooth, and honestly makes every other mouse feel a little mid.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "KARIM FAHMY", "review_title": "Excellent", "review_text": "Very good quality", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Michael T Brown", "review_title": "Fantastic mouse for those who like it heavy.", "review_text": "I'm an avid PC user and rarely replace my accessories. My mouse especially was hard to replace, as every top end mouse seems to get lighter and lighter. However, after using the Basilisk V3, I can safely say this mouse has been a perfect upgrade from my 2013 Deathadder. It weighs roughly the same, being on the heavier side for a mouse, and that's perfect for me. It's built great, has a fantastic braided cable which is smooth to the touch, it doesn't catch on corners like the older Razer cables, and the RGB is stellar. I really like the ring of RGB that goes around the base, and it's incredibly easy to edit in Razer Synapse.
The mouse is also extremely comfortable. I didn't expect a thumb rest to do much, but I'll honestly miss it if I ever have to upgrade.
For the price, you really can't go wrong. This mouse is incredible for its price point and well worth investing in if you like to 'feel' your mouse movements.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "uae", "review_title": "perfect", "review_text": "real razer mouse not a scam works perfectly fine and great quality.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Andrew", "review_title": "The greatest strength is it's smoothness of operation.", "review_text": "I've been using this mouse for about a month now.
It's my first gaming mouse.
It's lighter than I expected but that does not impair the use at all.
The greatest strength is it's smoothness of operation. The cursor glides smoothly with small and large gestures.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Raphael Oliveira", "review_title": "ótimo mouse", "review_text": "Mouse ergonômico com encaixe para dedão, tem textura no dedão e nas laterais para um grip melhor, é grande então dá para usar se você tem pegada "garra" ou se pega com a mão inteira, funciona em ambos.
É mais pesado que os outros mouses como li descrito em reviews de sites mas é um peso ideal, mouse leve é meio estranho, na minha opinião.
Vêm com botões de várias funcionalidades, como os 2 botões acima do dedão, assim como o a frente do dedão que serve para diminuir o dpi para jogos tipo FPS, por ex, usar com sniperscope onde você precisa fazer movimentos menores. Para MOBA não serve para nada, mas todos os botões são customizáveis com o app da razer, então dá para configurar para usar algum slot de item, ou skill, etc. O app também tem como fazer macros, e configurar o padrão das cores dos leds.
O cabo tem uma qualidade boa e longo. O scroll é bem macio, e tem um botão para trocar entre modo corrido (rola sem parar) e o scroll normal (com pulos/ticks). E o próprio scroll também serve como 2 botões extras quando vc empurra ele para os lados.", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: Logitech G PRO X2 SUPERSTRIKE Wireless Gaming Mouse - Black/White
Description: Designed With Pros, Engineered to Win: Designed alongside the world’s best esports athletes, the Logitech G PRO X2 SUPERSTRIKE wireless gaming mouse delivers the fastest, fully customizable click
Category: Video Games,PC,Accessories,Gaming Mice
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Sol", "review_title": "huge difference during long gaming sessions", "review_text": "The Logitech PRO X2 SUPERSTRIKE is easily one of the best gaming mice I’ve used. The first thing you notice is how incredibly lightweight it is—it glides effortlessly, which makes a huge difference during long gaming sessions. The responsiveness is top-tier, and the Lightspeed wireless connection feels just as fast and reliable as a wired mouse.
The build quality is excellent, with a clean, minimalist design that looks great on any setup. The clicks feel crisp and precise, and the customizable haptics add a nice touch for those who want to fine-tune their experience. Battery life is also impressive, and the USB-C charging is a welcome upgrade.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Joseanup", "review_title": "The best gaming mouse I’ve ever used", "review_text": "I’ve owned and tested many gaming mice over the years, and the Logitech G Superstrike X2 is, without question, the best one I’ve ever used. I don’t play competitively—I mostly enjoy adventure games, action titles, and other immersive experiences—but this mouse has made every gaming session more enjoyable. It combines incredible comfort, premium build quality, and features that genuinely stand out.
The biggest highlight for me is the haptic switches. They feel amazing, providing a tactile, satisfying click that makes every input feel deliberate and precise. The feedback is unlike anything I’ve experienced on another mouse, adding a level of immersion that you don’t realize you’re missing until you try it. Combined with the outstanding responsiveness, every click feels fast, consistent, and incredibly satisfying.
Another thing I absolutely love is how lightweight it is. It glides effortlessly across the mousepad and never feels fatiguing, even after hours of gaming. The shape is comfortable, the weight is perfectly balanced, and it almost feels like an extension of your hand.

-Packaging:

-Comfortable ergonomic shape for marathon gaming sessions
-PTFE mouse feet for super-smooth glide across mouse pads
-The new optical hybrid switches are incredibly fast compared to the G-Pro's older Omron switches, with a nice crisp click and improved actuation. They will last much longer than conventional mechanical switches and correct double-clicking issues. My last G-Pro's right rear thumb switch suffered from double-clicking issues since they were the old Omron mechanicals that wore out from constant use.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Garrett", "review_title": "Exactly what you would expect from a direct upgrade.", "review_text": "TBH if your looking for a G502/HERO/Lightspeed replacement there is no complaints in my opinion.

Title: Razer Naga V3 Pro Wireless MMO Gaming Mouse with Swappable Side Plates
Description: ADAPT TO ANY GAME GENRE – Customize your setup with 3 swappable magnetic side plates featuring 12, 6, or 2-button layouts, plus 2 quick-access edge buttons and a lockable ring finger button for MMO, MOBA, FPS, and battle royale gaming
Category: Video Games,PC,Accessories,Gaming Mice
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Albert", "review_title": "I don't like Razer, but this mouse slaps", "review_text": "I was really, really contemplating rating this less because of Razer Synapse 4. I couldn't get button remapping to work in any game at the start, it would only work after I closed Synapse entirely. Profile switching also didn't work. The software took so much finagling and trial and error manually deleting Synapse and re-installing more than once--I even tried deleting Synapse data online from my account via the Privacy Center to no avail. Midway through, I almost just resorted to keeping things on onboard memory and manually switching between games. It was brutal.
Thankfully profile switching started working and button remaps followed suit. I don't know how I got it to work, but it works! It handles so well that the pain setting up the software can be forgiven. This is everything I wanted out of my old Logitech G600s, of which I've had several and daily drove for the better part of a decade. I'd always try but ultimately return other MMO mice because I'd always miss ring-finger button. I know I'm not the only one that felt this!
It seems like Razer heard our cries and implemented it on this new Naga V3 Pro, even adding the two additional buttons by the left-click button like on the V2 Hyperspeed. My only gripes are that the side buttons aren't as pronounced and contoured as the G600, and the left- and right-mouse clicks are just obnoxiously loud. Travel distance and weight per click as well I'd say aren't great either--maybe better for older MMOs where each click needed to be more deliberate, but a lighter switch would be better for modern MMOs. I guess I'll get used to them.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "REM", "review_title": "I loved my Logitech. This is a viable replacement!", "review_text": "I am a user, and fond lover, of the G502 and G600. When I saw V3 Pro and the feature set, I really wanted to take a dive into the Razer ecosystem and give it a whirl. This one mouse had the features and potential to replace both the G600 and G502 on my desk.
While using and trying the mouse, I can say that it does replace both and works as expected. The form may cause other pause, but it comes down to preference and usability. The G502 is a great mouse but was causing wrist issues despite the perfect for. The Naga V3 Pro is slightly smaller than the V2, but it has given me the form of the G600 which tends to be usable longer for me, with the features of the G600 and G502.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Randy", "review_title": "Good MMO Mouse", "review_text": "Been using an MMO mouse for over 10 years now and this is an upgrade from my very used Trinity. Feels great in the hand but only negative is the high-pitched "ting" sound coming from Gen-4 optical switches left click.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Charlie Gerkin", "review_title": "Excellent Multi-mode mouse", "review_text": "Works great with 2, 6, or 12 side buttons. Razer Synapse customizes it with up to twice as many functions. Button on ring finger rest acts as trigger for second set on all Razer devices. Replaced my V2 with it.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Rafael Ospino", "review_title": "Advanced features through Synapse Not supported in MAC", "review_text": "Synapse 4 currently does not support Razer Naga V3 Pro for MAC. This is ridiculous, and should be specified for buyers.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jonny Quest", "review_title": "Sounds good on paper, BUT...", "review_text": "Pros: Swappable sides. Ring finger button (that you can disable when not needed!). Free spin mousewheel.
Cons: Oddly positioned two buttons added to left click side. Ring finger button/rest is insanely uncomfortable. Loud, tingy clicks. Plastic feels loose and cheap on the main click buttons.
I used the V2 and G600 for years. This seemed to be the best of both, but it didnt cut it for me. The clicks are intolerable. They have an annoying ting to them. After using this mouse for a couple of hours, the ring finger rest started to hurt. I noticed it's a very sharp design, that I just couldn't do. I still have my G600 and it's so much more comfortable. I really liked the free spin wheel. But, the V2 would let you actually adjust the mouse wheel to your liking instead of just 3 presets. Seems like a downgrade. Then there's the two new buttons that my fingers cant reach well, so what's the point? The plastic just also feels cheap and "creaky", which I never noticed on the V2. This ended up going back the next day. Bummer.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Adam", "review_title": "The New Hotness", "review_text": "Feels pretty much identical to the V2 Pro but it's far and away in my opinion the best MMO mouse available. The switches do feel ever so slightly better and the added buttons will be really nice for some users. Would recommend!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Cole", "review_title": "Good mouse design but questionable quality", "review_text": "The buttons on the 12 button MMO panel wobble and creak. They are not sturdy. The buttons on the bottom right of the panel are impossible to use without fat fingering an extra key.
I like the scroll wheel and the third click. The scroll wheel is three extra buttons on its own. The third click should probably be used infrequently as it is an unnatural hand gesture.
I’m coming from an old razer naga x with keys that don’t jiggle, more solid construction, all for a lower price. Doesn’t seem like there’s an equivalent to it these days. I wish they would make another dedicated 12 button and stop giving the mmo players this junk three panel nonsense.", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: Razer Viper V4 Pro Wireless Esports Gaming Mouse, 49g,180Hr Battery, Black
Description: 49G ULTRA LIGHTWEIGHT ESPORTS MOUSE — Built with input from competitive pro players, this wireless mouse is 9% lighter than the previous gen and delivers faster, more agile control for PC gaming
Category: Video Games,PC,Accessories,Gaming Mice
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Amazon Customer", "review_title": "The Ultimate Ambidextrous Endgame! 45 Days of Heavy Gaming and Pure Perfection", "review_text": "I am coming back to write this review after putting this mouse through its paces for a solid 45 days. After upgrading my desktop with a premium 8K magnetic keyboard, I knew my mouse setup had to match that elite level of performance. That is why I pulled the trigger on the latest Razer Viper V4 Pro, and after a month and a half of intense daily use, it has completely redefined my gaming experience. If you are looking for the absolute pinnacle of symmetrical gaming mice, this is the endgame.
First, let us talk about the design because there is a lot of confusion out there. This Viper V4 Pro is a flawless, perfectly symmetrical shape. It is a completely different beast compared to the older, bulky, asymmetrical right-handed design of the DeathAdder V4 Pro. As someone who prefers a claw/fingertip grip for high-precision micro-adjustments, this symmetrical shell melts into my hand perfectly, giving my thumb and fingers ultimate control.
At a mind-blowing 49 grams, the weight distribution is pure wizardry. Combined with the native 8000Hz polling rate and the 50K DPI sensor, the tracking feels like an extension of my own nervous system. In high-APM gaming sessions and chaotic shooters like World War Z or CS2, swapping targets is instantaneous with zero initial drag. Furthermore, it is an absolute dream for massive open-world action games like Where Winds Meet. During high-stakes martial arts combat, dodging, executing flawless parries, and rapidly controlling the 3D camera feels incredibly smooth and responsive. There is absolutely no pixel-skipping or camera stutter, giving me perfect situational awareness.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Krenzzler", "review_title": "This is just one of my favorite mice now", "review_text": "TLDR: This is the mouse I keep coming back to. Long story short, I want nothing more when using this mouse.
I'm one of those that just collects mice. I have my favorites, and I have some that I have just used once and put away. This is one that I keep bringing out. Simply put, the latest Viper and Deathadder are just some of my favorite mice period. They are built very solid, light weight, and flawless sensors. They have an instant wake up, fantastic battery life, satisfying clicks, great scroll wheel, and great side buttons. They are pricey, but quality-wise, it really doesn't get better than Razer now. And I'm comparing to Zowie, Logitech, G-wolves, Finalmouse, Pulsar, etc etc... Every one of those other brands has something I don't like in the quality alone, a creak, spongy click, or something keeps me from wanting to use those brands since I've used the Viper. Obviously, the shape is subjective, so if you've used the Viper V3 and didn't like the shape, you're not gonna like this. But I love the size shape, and weight. I can't wait to see the next Deathadder shed some weight to around 49g, and maybe implement some analog switches like the Logitech Superstrike. If they ever did that, I just hope they do weight balancing better because the superstrike is pretty front heavy, but I'm perfectly happy with Razer's optical switches because they just feel sooooo good. But I think the haptic analog switches would be very interesting in the Deathadder shape. I really don't know how they could improve on this other than finding more ways to lighten the weight even more. Razer might've perfected the Viper with this iteration.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Dylan", "review_title": "Great Gaming Mouse for 2026", "review_text": "This is the best gaming mouse as someone who upgraded from a regular stock mouse. The weight, the functionality, and the design of the mouse is perfect. In fact, this mouse, and it features had further fine-tuned my already decent aim. After using this mouse for a while, I have observed my aim became a natural aim bot, where I was even accused of potentially exploiting in a match of BF1.
The mouse itself is light, and as someone who came from a heavier mouse it felt a bit weird at first. However, if you can manage it, then it becomes a benefit. It allows you to flick quickly, and track targets consistently, which is where my claim of "natural aim bot" came from. It's not too light where you might find yourself tensing up too much to keep it in place, but if you came from a heavier mouse, then you might overflick your target a few times.
The features the mouse offered through Razer's Synapse software such as the DPI and mappings are very useful. You can set different profiles for different games, so there are different DPI's for each game. In addition, you can change the mouse's buttons to be mapped to keys on your keyboard. For example, you can have the side button mapped to 'R', so you can reload through the side button. You can also have the same side buttons run a macro, so if you're playing Helldivers 2, you can instantly input a stratagem through your side button. There are also features like letting the side buttons launch a program.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Kayne P", "review_title": "The perfect mouse?", "review_text": "I don’t typically write reviews, but this mouse is hands down the best I’ve ever had the pleasure of using, so I feel like I must. The moment my hand gripped the mouse, I knew it was the one. The build quality is fantastic. Everything. From the clicks to the sensor, the scroll wheel and the side buttons. Everything is perfect. The coating on the mouse is high quality and the dongle that comes with it is nicely weighted so it doesn’t slip around on your desk. The stock skates are also wonderful and glide around on my Artisan Zero Soft so smoothly. The size and shape is perfect for my grip style (relaxed claw) so I can handle it comfortably. I recently just bought a GPX Superlight 2 as well as an X2 Crazylight Medium and neither felt quite right. So I decided to try this mouse and it did everything for me the other two couldn’t. Since I bought the Razer Viper V4 Pro, I’ve seen a massive improvement in my gameplay. And for that reason I can confidently justify the price of this product. 5 Stars. Genuinely amazing product across the board. Dare I say perfect. 👍 ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Anthony", "review_title": "Left me Surprised in a Good Way", "review_text": "This mouse took me by surprise.
Coming from the Basilisk V3 Pro, this one is just so lightweight that I almost mistook it for a toy. I seriously can't believe how light this is.
The battery life is phenomenal, and the controls are astoundingly tight. The buttons on my Basilisk always felt cheap and mushy, but every button on this Viper V4 Pro is snappy and solid.
Getting to the part people care about most, this is probably the most fluid mouse I've ever used. The 50K sensor is a marketing ploy, as I don't use anything over 6400DPI, but you can turn on the 8K polling with a high refresh rate monitor and you won't see any dragging of your cursor across your screen as you will with lower refresh rates, and the higher polling rate shows your mouse's location on the screen more times per second than traditional 1K polling rates. My eyes can see the difference, but only if I strain to see it.
I run the mouse at 1K polling rate for optimal battery life and because most games are using that rate the most effectively. It's a sweet spot.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Charles myers", "review_title": "Is it worth the upgrade?", "review_text": "The Razer Viper V4 Pro is a flagship-level esports mouse that doubles down on performance rather than reinventing the formula. It features an ultra-lightweight ambidextrous design at around 49–50g, paired with Razer’s Focus Pro 50K optical sensor capable of 50,000 DPI, 930 IPS tracking, and 90G acceleration. It also introduces Gen-4 optical switches, improved wireless performance with an upgraded dongle, and up to 180 hours of battery life. On paper, it’s one of the most technically refined mice available fast, consistent, and clearly built for competitive play.
That said, if you already own the Razer Viper V3 Pro, there’s honestly no real reason to upgrade. The improvements here are incremental slightly better battery life, marginally upgraded switches, and small refinements that you’re not going to feel in-game. The V3 Pro is already insanely lightweight, responsive, and accurate, so the V4 Pro ends up feeling more like a spec bump than a meaningful evolution. Unless you’re chasing absolute top-end specs for the sake of it, you’re better off sticking with the V3 Pro. As a stand alone mouse, I give it 4 stars. As a "upgrade" to the previous generation I'd give it one star.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Marco", "review_title": "New main. Excellent mouse with a ridiculous battery life", "review_text": "The box didn't have much protection, but it arrived in great condition. As for the mouse itself, it is amazing.
I won't talk much about shape because that's highly subjective (I'll just say it fits my hand size and grip style), but everything else is excellent: coating is smooth and grippy, very nice to the touch; main clicks are light and tactile, tho they could have a little less post travel; side buttons are well tensioned and positioned; the wheel might be the weakest aspect, because the scrolling feels a bit off, but it's totally functional; M3 click is very tactile; skates are smooth and fast; build quality is perfect, solid as a rock; performance is top tier, no complaints; and finally, the battery is absolutely insane. I have been using the mouse for 12 days at 1000hz (sometimes 8000, but only for a couple of Apex matches) and it has only gone down to 60%.
On top of all of that, Razer has finally made a web software. That means 2 things: 1) you don't have to deal with the bloatware that is Synapse (except for firmware updates); and 2) you can change your settings on Linux, which has been a game changer for me (I dual boot Windows 11 and Bazzite).", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Nick", "review_title": "Worthy of the praise", "review_text": "I have been using it a full week now, and I think it's worth all the praise. It's a safe shape that will work for everyone except if your hands are on the smaller side. Switches, side buttons, scroll wheel, and sensor all feel perfect. My honest favorite thing about this mouse is the battery life is otherworldly good compared to anything I have used. I likely won't have to charge it until about 5-6 weeks of moderate to heavy use at 1000Hz, which is huge when I need to charge my other mice practically after a weekend.
The first negative is the price is steep, especially when you could get the V3 Pro Se for like have the price. Two, the M1/M2 switches are on the loud side, but you won't notice them with headphones. You will annoy anyone around you though if they have to listen to you click. Three, the black version is a bit of an oil magnet, but the coating at least feels good. Might be worth using either Razer's provided grips or another brands for long-term use.
Overall, it's a very good mouse if it's within your price range, and your hands are moderately large in size. Maybe it's placebo, but I also dropped my first nuke in Call of Duty on keyboard and mouse using it. That might be influencing might personal opinion of it, but I promise it's a great mouse.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Ramz1333", "review_title": "ممتاز جداً", "review_text": "رهيبه بس صوت الازرار عالي جداً", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Sebin jose", "review_title": "Best mouse for competitive games", "review_text": "Best in the market. As always razerr", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Luca Preda", "review_title": "Great all around mouse", "review_text": "I would argue this mouse is better than the superstrike 2 in the way a porsche 911 drives, it just does what you want. I’ve had zero issues, just a lightweight, easy to use mouse that works well on both cloth and glass mousepads. 49g seems like the perfect weight before getting too light for me, and it suits all three grip types well. Battery is genuinely insane, I can charge it fully and leave it at 2000hz polling rate for a month and a half of daily use (multiple hours) before I need to charge it again. The web software is reasonably clear and has good features too, letting you change things like liftoff distance, mouse tilt angle and so on.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Saleh Gharaibeh", "review_title": "Perfect.", "review_text": "Lightweight, responsive, all you can ask from a gaming mouse. Title: Razer Viper V3 Pro Wireless Esports Gaming Mouse, 54g Lightweight, Black
Description: 54 G ULTRA LIGHTWEIGHT DESIGN — Designed in collaboration with world-class esports pros, the Viper V3 Pro’s perfectly balanced ultra lightweight design allows gamers to make swift, precise flicks that match every intention
Category: Video Games,PC,Accessories,Gaming Mice
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Chanly Duong", "review_title": "my review of the razor viper v3 pro", "review_text": "now for my background, i play r6 and csgo, and occasionally roblox shooters. i went from originally a 60g razer orochi v2 using a fingertip grip, and i went to this mouse with a traditional claw. i’ve had this mouse for a few months and i can say that this is a very good and universal shape for all sorts of grips. i have a medium size hand and i can comfortably fingertip and claw this mouse.
the coating is lovely and the best i’ve personally felt on a mouse, and i tried the grips but they eventually wear out over time so i don’t recommend using those (the actual mouse texture is better than the grips anyway). now i know this sounds a little ridiculous but moving from a 60g small mouse not even including the batteries, i played a LOT better with this bigger one after adjusting and i’m honestly happy with my purchase (even though it cost quite a bit). it feels light in the hand for the size and the weight is flawlessly distributed. the skates are solid for being stock but you can always upgrade, the scroll wheel is pretty normal and has distinctive bumps per scroll but personally i like more smoother ones (i am probably just being nitpicky). the main clicks are lovely to hear and the little dongle included doesn’t take up too much space, i’d say only the actual cable itself does but this isn’t actually an issue. the dongle can also support up to 8k hz which isn’t necessary but it’s a “nice to have” feature and i use 2k hz myself to save battery life;", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "CyndiCat", "review_title": "Highly recommend for competitive gamers.", "review_text": "(Review from my 15 year old son)
Honestly this mouse felt SO much lighter than I thought it would. I just upgraded from the Glorious Model O- Wireless Gaming Mouse, and let me say... the upgrade was WORTH it for sure. I pretty much only play Fortnite on Keyboard and Mouse, and I was having issues with my side buttons on my old mouse. I decided it was time to upgrade since I can't have those issues happening mid-game. The Razer Viper V3 Pro, is definitely a solid upgrade. The side buttons are so much more solid than the side buttons on my old mouse. Not to mention, the response time of the clicks was faster, and the accuracy of my aim with the better sensor was so much better. The scroll wheel is also very responsive and fast which is important for Fortnite. (I was able to easily quad edit in Fortnite when using this new mouse)
The wireless connectivity isn't even noticeable at all. The response time is insane for a wireless mouse, and it surprised me a lot. I don't have a lot to say about the battery life yet, as this is my first day using it. I will say though, I charged the mouse to 68%, used it for an hour in Fortnite, and the battery was only 67% afterwards.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "yandre", "review_title": "Expensive, but great mouse.", "review_text": "The Razer Viper V3 has been an excellent mouse for both gaming and everyday use. It feels very lightweight and comfortable in hand, making long sessions easy with no fatigue. The shape is simple but very ergonomic, and it works well for both claw and fingertip grip styles.
Performance wise, the sensor is extremely accurate and responsive. Tracking is smooth, clicks feel crisp, and there is no noticeable delay. The wireless connection is stable and reliable, with no lag or dropouts. Battery life has also been great, lasting several days of heavy use without needing frequent charging.
Build quality feels solid, and the mouse buttons and scroll wheel all feel well made. Overall, the Viper V3 delivers excellent performance, comfort, and reliability. It is a great choice for anyone looking for a high quality lightweight gaming mouse.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Danny", "review_title": "Good claw grip mouse", "review_text": "I had a Logitech superlight and moved to the Viper v3 pro. It was the best decision that I have ever made. The mouse sensor in my opinion is more accurate the Logitech mice. The feel and texture and material of the mouse feels very nice especially the white coating option is phenomenal and has really good grip for a very low amount of weight gain. The size definitely favors mid-big hands and excels in the Claw grip. It isn't the lightest mouse on the market but it still in my opinion is more than light enough for most. The scroll wheel actually feels quite nice and i prefer it over the Logitech one. Though this mouse supports 8k polling I rarely find myself using it as it drains battery too fast, I would just use 4000/2000 if you want a high enough speed with a very long battery life. If you are looking for a high quality claw grip mouse then this is the mouse for you, if you don't have a claw grip I would recommend looking at other mice that might be for you.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "The Lovely Lyss", "review_title": "Most satisfying mouse I have ever used; full stop.", "review_text": "As someone who loves the Superlight and has been jamming out with version 2 of it along with a Logitech Pro X TKL paired with it, it's been nice to swap back to my Black Widow V4 along with the Viper Pro 3.
Right out of the box, and I am someone with medium to large hands, this mouse is just a pure delight to hold; it's not often I can say that my hands feel like they disappear when using a peripheral, but this mouse and the Superlight from Logi are the two mice that achieve that for me. Razer knew what they were doing here and it shows in the product; this will be my go-to mouse and I will alternate my Razer setup back to the Logitech set up as the mood strikes me to change things up week by week.
When it comes time for the Wooting 80HE to arrive, I will most likely be pairing the Viper Pro 3 with that board due to just how consistently good it feels; I am 3 hours deep into a play session and the battery is down to 98% and I'm using the 4K polling rate; not going to bother with 8K just yet.
It's hard to put into words here just how good the slight ergo shape of this mouse feels; I really have tried a number of different mice and this could be "the one"; I don't say this in a hyperbolic fashion either. It's rare that you use a gaming device where you just forget what you're using because it seamlessly blends into the play session.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "ludy", "review_title": "Best Gaming Mouse for Claw and Fingertip grip", "review_text": "TLDR:
Good mouse, great quality for price, beautiful designs, 10/10
The Razer Viper V3 Pro is probably the best gaming mouse hands down. It’s ultra lightweight, feels amazing to move around, and extremely responsive.
The clicks are a little on the louder side, the material is smooth and not particularly grippy, so if you prefer grippier mice, there are those grip stickers that you can put on.
I have an average adult male sized hand. In terms of what type of grip you use (claw, palm, etc..) this mouse is definitely a claw or fingertip type of mouse. Palm grip doesn’t feel amazing on this mouse since it’s a little small in my opinion. There’s also no “ergonomic” shape like the razer deathadder, so if you’re a claw or fingertip type grip person, this is probably the best mouse on the market you can get. (Please do check measurements to compare with your own hand size)
I got the faker edition due to his iconic style, and it’s a beautiful red with a stunning demon art design.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Steven", "review_title": "Light with great battery life", "review_text": "I have had this mouse for about a year now and use it as my daily driver, and I love it.
It is really light and glides across the mouse pad. The mouse wheel is not noisy at all and neither is the clicking of the mouse buttons imo. The battery life is good lasting more than a few all day play sessions, and a couple of weeks of light use.
It comes with some little adhesive pads that you can place on the mouse which I would recommend using as the mouse is very smooth.
My complaints are that the mouse gets clammy feeling after a while. Not a huge deal, but I have thought of buying another adhesive pad to go over the emblem because it gets to feel gross. I do clean it, but this is the only mouse I have ever had this issue with. Also the dongle is kind of a pain if you have OCD, it is hard to get it to lay flat down.
Overall I love the mouse and think it is worth the money. I would just recommend buying an adhesive patch (I'm not sure what they are really called) to go over the razer emblem as that part can start to feel gross.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "R", "review_title": "Surprisingly lightweight, good polling rate and no wifi-interference!", "review_text": "So far so good. I was impressed on how light this mouse felt when I used it for the first time. You can definitely feel the extra accuracy when you aim, by that I mean every small movement you make on your mousepad translates exactly as you would expect on the screen. My router and modem are right under my desk and I don't get any interference. I don't open the program that comes with it (synapse) because I used a wired headset with it (razer blackshark v2 X) and I don't want synapse messing the audio settings of my headset since the default option is pretty good. The battery works for a long time; I used it for like 3 consecutive days and when I open synapse to check battery is about 70% (I use 2k polling rate). Clicking sounds satisfying as you would expect from an expensive mouse. Your forearm gets considerably less tired. The side buttons and click buttons have not collected any dust or grime from my hands, unlike my old mouse did.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Oswar", "review_title": "Very nice", "review_text": "Very nice", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Rodrigo Guimarães de Souza", "review_title": "Recomendo", "review_text": "Produto original! Novo! Produto chegou com mais de 15 dias de antecedência da previsão inicial!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Mohammad aljasir", "review_title": "Super comfortable", "review_text": "Light and feel nice", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Mauricio", "review_title": "Recomendado", "review_text": "Extremadamente ligero y con bateria duradera, muy buen mouse… super recomendado", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Amazon Customer", "review_title": "Highly recommend great mouse", "review_text": "Great mouse but higher polling rates affect fps depending on your pc", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: Logitech G PRO X Superlight 2 Wireless Gaming Mouse - Black
Description: Better Performance: The Logitech Superlight 2, our championship winning wireless mouse gaming is now even better; with 8 kHz polling, USB-C charging, 95-hour battery life and POWERPLAY compatibility at 60 g
Category: Video Games,PC,Accessories,Gaming Mice
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Iggy Gonzalez", "review_title": "Lightweight, Fast, and Worth It", "review_text": "The G PRO X Superlight 2 is an excellent gaming mouse. It’s incredibly lightweight, tracks flawlessly, and feels very responsive in fast-paced games. The battery life is great, the shape is comfortable for long sessions, and the build quality feels premium. It’s expensive, but if you’re serious about gaming, it’s absolutely worth the investment.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Julia", "review_title": "Crazy light and perfect for gaming", "review_text": "I have been using this mouse for a couple weeks now and honestly it has been amazing. The first thing you notice is how light it is. It almost feels like nothing in your hand which made a huge difference for me in FPS games and even just normal computer use. My aim feels smoother and my wrist does not get tired after long sessions. As someone who games in the mornings before studying or rotations, it has been a really nice upgrade.
The clicks feel super crisp and responsive and the wireless connection has been flawless so far. No lag, no random disconnects, and the battery life has been better than I expected. The shape is comfortable even after hours of use and it fits well for both claw and palm grip. Setup was simple and the software was easy to use to adjust DPI and buttons.
Overall this is easily one of the best mice I have owned. It feels premium, performs great, and actually made gaming more enjoyable for me. If you are thinking about upgrading your mouse, especially for competitive games, I would definitely recommend this one.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Will Miles", "review_title": "Excellent Mouse for Competitive Gaming", "review_text": "The Superlight 2 has easily become one of my favorite gaming mice. The first thing you notice is how light it is. At around 60g, movements feel incredibly quick and effortless, which has been especially noticeable for me in FPS games where fast flicks and precise adjustments matter.
Tracking feels extremely accurate and consistent, and wireless performance has been flawless. I haven’t noticed any input delay compared to a wired mouse. Battery life is also excellent—I can use it for long gaming sessions without constantly thinking about charging it.
I also really like the shape. It’s simple, comfortable, and doesn’t try to do anything weird ergonomically, so it works well for both gaming and everyday PC use. The white version looks especially clean paired with a white setup.
It’s definitely expensive for a mouse, but you’re paying for the extremely low weight, excellent sensor, reliable wireless connection, and overall refinement. If competitive FPS games are a big part of what you play, the Superlight 2 absolutely lives up to its reputation.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Damian Pizarro", "review_title": "Crisp, Precise, and Worth Every Dollar!!", "review_text": "The Logitech G Pro X Superlight 2 is easily one of the best mice I’ve used. It’s extremely light without feeling cheap, and the sensor performance is outstanding. When paired with a glass mouse pad, the glide is insanely smooth and tracking feels incredibly clean and precise.
Because I have larger hands, I added grip tape and highly recommend it for anyone in the same boat. Without grip tape I had to grip the mouse tighter than I liked, but with it, control and comfort improved immediately. Combined with the crisp clicks, reliable wireless performance, and long battery life, this mouse delivers exactly what it promises. Pricey, but well worth it.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Why do you need to know ts?", "review_title": "Really Good All Around", "review_text": "Good ergonomics, nice and light, glides well, good software, battery lasts a long time.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Star", "review_title": "Lightweight gaming mouse. Mouse size is decent for small hands.", "review_text": "Been using this mouse for about 6 months for work, school, and gaming. The mouse size is alright. I have small hands, and my hand doesn't get sore or strained using it for several hours. It has decent ergonomics. The clicks are much quieter than a Razer Viper V3 Pro. The sound clicks are as "loud" as linear switches (which are fairly quiet) if noise level is a concern for you. I prefer quieter, but tactile clicks, which this mouse does quite nicely. The mouse clicks don't bother me when I'm working at night.
Battery life lasts quite a long time for this mouse. I can use this mouse for a couple of days (or even a week, if I'm taking breaks) without having to charge it. On Logitech G HUB, it says the battery life lasts for approximately 96 hours. You'd have to download Logitech G HUB to customize macros and set sensitivity on the mouse. If you're using this mouse for mainly gaming, make sure to go to "Device Settings" and under "Lightforce Switch" set it to "Optical Only". This will decrease battery life, but will utilize the full performance of the optical switch and has lower latency.
My only gripes are the Logitech G HUB is glitchy sometimes and certain game profiles don't automatically switch over, like when I tab in and out between the desktop and Fortnite, and the software doesn't automatically switch to the "Fortnite" profile, and the side buttons feel a bit mushy when building and editing in Fortnite. The side buttons could be a bit crispier.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Tildon M.", "review_title": "Pretty Sweet Gaming Mouse", "review_text": "I've had it for 4 1/2 months now, great feeling mouse, very responsive and fast, it looks sick in my setup, and I've only had to charge it about 2 times since I got it so good battery life. Having to download G Hub to configure it for the first time I'd say was fairly easy but I recommend configuring it, turning on on board memory mode, and forgetting the software. Also about 3 months into having it I spilled a whole cup of water on it and spent like 20 minutes getting all the liquid out of the mouse and a month later it still works like it's brand new lol.
For the price, I'd only recommend it to some, but overall pretty sweet mouse.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Derek", "review_title": "Logitech still hasn't gotten their quality control in line over the last 6 years of making mice.", "review_text": "About 6 years ago I bought a g pro wireless, the first one had an issue with double clicking with the primary left click AND the middle click. That developed after ~4-7 days of use. Logitech RMA'd it and sent me a new mouse. This second mouse immediately had issues with the left click where it was mushy and had significant travel past the actual click sound. They RMA'd this one too. Finally by the third mouse I got one that worked good, no double clicking, no middle mouse button issues..... for maybe 2.5 years. 0.5 years past the warranty period. I lived with the mouse button issues for a while until it became unbearable to the point where I can't reliably move the camera anymore in league of legends, or rotate the camera in many 3rd person games/3d software. I decided to get this mouse (G PRO X SUPERLIGHT 2) to replace the aged g pro wireless. It seems logitech has learned absolutely nothing in their quality control department over the years. This mouse that I just got ALREADY has scroll wheel decoder issues where it scrolls in the opposite direction briefly before scrolling in the correct direction. Secondly, it has a squealing noise as a scroll upwards that is already unbearable to listen to. I've had enough of logitech mice. I hate the situation because I love the G pro's shape and feel. The silver lining is that there are MANY competing mice now that offer great performance for less, or about the same amount of money which copied the shape and feel. This will likely be the last logitech mouse I buy and am returning it. Razer Viper V3 pro here I come.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Ivan Guerrero Azamar", "review_title": "Resistente", "review_text": "El mouse se siente mas robusto que el G Pro Superlight al igual que sus clicks pero eso mismo hace que el mouses aguante mas y apesar de que es mas robusto pesa menos que el anterior, es una compra totalmente recomendable si es que quieres un mouse que los clicks duren mucho, que sea comodo y pesando casi nada", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "AC", "review_title": "Great for fps, ok for work, same issues as other mice", "review_text": "Using this for work and various video games (cs). Very light mouse, almost feels like air. Build quality is excellent, the materials are pleasant to the touch. The sensor is very precise and smooth, this mouse wont let you down in a clutch. No issues with battery life (multiple full days), just keep a usb-c cable nearby. My phone charger is multipurpose now, phone/headset/mouse.
The only issue is the middle click (mouse3): when held down, it can register multiple clicks when slightly changing pressure. For gaming, no big deal; for working, very lame (can close/open multiple tabs by accident). From forums/reddit, this is common to most (if not all) superlights.
I've used the superlight for several months now with no new issues (other than the middle button).
Before this, I've had at least seven wired and later wireless g703s. Something usually breaks within a year or so (left/right double clicking, mouse wheel issues, etc.). I expect the same for the superlight. That's gaming, cant help it. Might sound bad, but both g703 and superlight are excellent mice. With heavy use, it is inevitable that something breaks eventually. If looking for cheaper mice, g703 is a heavier alternative.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "S.Almheiri", "review_title": "Logitech G PRO X Superlight 2", "review_text": "I have tried various types of gaming mouse set-ups and I have found this mouse to be almost perfect from the ergonomics, battery life, charging, and practicality. I have been using it for a couple of months for various tasks such as work, studies, gaming, and general use. Currently I have no complaints other than that price is high. Finally what made buy this version compared to the superlight 1 is the type-c charger which is worth it.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Kauan Veras", "review_title": "Excelente Mouse", "review_text": "Muito bom chegou em perfeito estado e gostei muito do mouse", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jehiel George", "review_title": "Solid Mouse, But Time for a Price Drop", "review_text": "I got the G PRO X SUPERLIGHT 2, and it's pretty great. First off it's insanely lightweight, which is a great touch if you're into quick movements. Feels good in the hand and is super responsive. The battery life is solid too, it holds charge for a decent amount of time, and when you do need to charge it, it's fast. Build quality seems sturdy, like it won’t just fall apart if you’re a bit rough with it.
That said, for how good it is, there are a lot of other mice out there offering similar stuff at cheaper prices now. I still like it, but honestly, it might be time for Logitech to consider bringing the price down a notch with all the competition around. It’s still worth it, just... a little less of a splurge would be nice.", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: GravaStar Mercury X Pro Wireless Gaming Mouse, Come with 8K Dongle – 32,000 DPI PAW 3950 Sensor, 8,000Hz Polling Rate, Only 49g, Magnesium Alloy Hollow Frame, RGB Lighting, 5 Programmable Buttons
Description: Innovative Hollow Skeleton Design - Maximized airflow with a durable, lightweight magnesium alloy frame to keep your hand cool and dry during intense gaming sessions.
Category: Video Games,PC,Accessories,Gaming Mice
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Steven", "review_title": "Very Cool, but does have a premium price for the extra coolness", "review_text": "It has been a long time in the accessory space since a company came out with products that were different and unique but didn't also stink at the function that they are supposed to perform. This is not one of them. Like their keyboards, GravaStar has made this crazy looking mouse that is actually an excellent gaming mouse. (Or just mouse in general.)
It is a premium product at a premium price so I do have a few nitpicks, but overall it is an excellent mouse.
Taking it out of the box, and it is both very light but also feels premium. Squeezing it much harder then I should and it is very rigid and strong. The web based configuration is okay. Since I have one of their keyboards and the software that comes with that I think it would be nice if that was integrated into one system. Otherwise it is nice to be able to fine tune the sensitivity and even though I had no issue with debounce (clicking once and sometimes getting double clicks) but it is nice to be able to adjust that. And finally something that I never thought I would say... I like the RGB. In generally it just seems sort of silly to have RGB on a mouse, but this one makes it work and adds to the whole vibe, especially when paired with one of their keyboards.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Mustang GT", "review_title": "My favorite gaming mouse I've ever owned", "review_text": "I've used quite a few gaming mice over the years, and this is easily my favorite. I'm a huge GravaStar fan, and this mouse absolutely lives up to the hype. I mainly play Apex Legends, Call of Duty, and Fortnite, and the accuracy and responsiveness are insane. It feels incredibly precise, making quick movements and tracking feel effortless.
One of my favorite features is how customizable everything is. After downloading the software, you can adjust the polling rate, DPI, RGB lighting, button functions, and even the breathing effects for the lighting. It's easy to use and gives you complete control over how you want the mouse to perform and look.
The lightweight design is also extremely comfortable during long gaming sessions without sacrificing durability. For me, this mouse has been worth every penny. If you're looking for a premium gaming mouse with excellent performance and endless customization, I highly recommend giving this one a try. This is a mouse that will last you forever and thats why I bought it.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Brittany Lammers", "review_title": "Great fancy mouse", "review_text": "Really nice mouse. I love the look of it. Love how Alien type looks, my hand is really small and have palm rest on it and i love all of it!. I was scared at first that would be too big, but nope fits perfectly for small hands, it feel sturdy and very light. So far it have lasted great I will update if something happens, the battery life is great i'm someone that love have the lights on all the time and always forgets to charge their mouse. I could be more than 3 days with 8+ hours play time and it last for long.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Alfredo", "review_title": "Sick high quality", "review_text": "Excellent item, I’m coming from a Logitech g502 pro wireless that is a pretty heavy one, I use it for play fps games and I have to say it works perfectly. I play full hand so I was worried about the size before get this one but I have to say that for the minimum weight, it has a pretty decent size that feels great in the hand. You can feel the high quality there and the software is pretty easy to use. And also looks sick. Great value if you constantly play and want something of quality", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Claudia Lacosta", "review_title": "Buy it!", "review_text": "Hands down it’s worth every penny. It’s pricey but love it, don’t cheap out. Light weight & fast.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Michael Berry", "review_title": "From a mouse junkie... Nearly Perfect", "review_text": "I was pleasantly surprised by the Gravastar Mercury X Pro... This mouse is really great and has the features we're all looking for (3950 sensor, 8k polling rate, adjustable LOD, motion sync) all wrapped up in a downloadable OR web interface. I love having the choice - you can configure the mouse via webpage, or via the software to download.
The RGB is great. I usually don't pick mice with it, I go for the $100-150 class mouse (I have around 10 of them, too). This mouse is definitely up there in the quality department, it feels just as nice as my other $170 magnesium mouse. The look is stunning and unique, I love the default colorway and it really stands out. It's a pleasure to use, except...
Side slits :( Side slits :( Side slits :(... this is the only thing preventing me from giving it 5 stars. Your thumb and ring/pinkie fingers on the side of the mouse will be holding slits. It's not so bad, they feel okay, but man would this mouse feel amazing with solid sides. I'm recommending to the vendor: Make the sides solid in the next revision. Give us something nice to hold onto. Ultimately there are two types of customer feelings about side slits: you've got the people who don't notice or care, and you've got the people that the side slits drive nuts. I am one of the people who go nuts about them. Your design is either going to drive people nuts with the feel of side slits, or it's going to be ignored by people who don't even notice. [{"reviewer_name": "John Caravaggio", "review_title": "Do you have an external drive that has a short cable?", "review_text": "I have a LITE-ON USB 2.0 External CD/DVD Writer Model eUAU108, manufactured in 2013, with an attached cable that is slightly less than 4 inches long. [{"reviewer_name": "Keegan Q.", "review_title": "A hub is not a dock. The big caveats are that the host cable is extremely short and the power made available to downstream devices is significantly reduced from what the host provides. It's still a five star device because these short cables are universally present on all USB-C hubs, and the power limitations are less severe than other similar products that I have tested. Most importantly, the data connectivity offered by this unit is excellent, and it's extremely portable, being barely larger than the connectors it contains.
I would still very much prefer a version of this device with a USB-C female connector on the back instead of the permanently attached short cable but apparently there are valid technical reasons that USB-C hubs are not made in this way. Devices that offer more power and better cabling options are now classified as docks rather than hubs, they tend to be based on Thunderbolt rather than plain old USB-C, and some of these docks are quite excellent, but they are comparatively very expensive. This particular device is just a hub, it is very affordable compared to a dock, and it's as good as USB-C hubs get.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Father Goose", "review_title": "Belkin's USB-C Hub: A Reliable Winner!", "review_text": "Okay, so I'm pretty picky when it comes to my tech accessories, but Belkin almost always nails it. Title: USB C Hub 7 Ports USB 3.0 Hub with 4*USB-A&3*USB-C (4ft)

Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Vine Reviewer", "review_title": "Easy USB port expansion for my desk", "review_text": "I picked up this 7-port USB C hub because I had simply run out of USB ports on my docking station. Between my mouse, keyboard, speakers, webcam, and all the newer devices using USB-C, I needed an easy way to expand what I could connect without replacing my existing setup. The 4-foot cable is particularly useful on my desk because I can position the hub where it is convenient instead of having everything crowded around the back of the docking station.
I have been using it for the wireless dongles for my mouse and keyboard, along with my small Polycon speakers and webcam, and everything has worked perfectly for me. I like having four USB-A ports and three USB-C ports available in one place, especially as I am accumulating more USB-C devices. The aluminum housing feels sturdy, the non-slip base keeps it from sliding around, and the small LED lets me know it is powered. One thing to pay attention to is that the USB-C port marked 5V is for power input only, not data transfer, so it is not an additional data port. That is clearly stated in the description, but it is worth knowing before plugging something into it and wondering why it isn't recognized.
I think this is a practical solution for anyone who needs more USB ports without rearranging their entire computer setup. The long cable and combination of USB-A and USB-C ports make it especially useful on a desktop workstation. For my particular setup, it has done exactly what I needed and saved me from constantly swapping devices between limited ports.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Amazon Reviewer", "review_title": "Versatile and Well-Built USB Hub", "review_text": "Very pleased with this USB-C hub. Having seven ports in a compact enclosure is extremely convenient, especially when connecting multiple peripherals to a laptop or desktop with limited USB connectivity.
The four USB-A and three USB-C ports provide a useful mix for both older USB devices and newer USB-C peripherals. USB 3.0 speeds are also fast enough for transferring files to external storage and for everyday devices such as keyboards, mice, USB adapters, and other peripherals.
I particularly like the straightforward plug-and-play operation. There was no complicated setup or additional software required—just connect it to the computer and the ports are immediately available. The compact design also makes it easy to keep on a desk or take along with a laptop, its heavy weight keeps it from moving around when attached devices move around, a problem I've had with lighter-weight models.
Overall, this is a very practical USB expansion solution at a great price. The combination of seven ports, a good mix of USB-A and USB-C connectivity, compact size, and USB 3.0 performance makes it a useful addition to any computer setup. Highly recommended!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Crash", "review_title": "Nicely Designed USB Hub", "review_text": "The XIAOBI USB 3.0 7 Port Hub looks really nice. It is aluminum and has 7 ports, 3 USB C and 4 USB A all rated at 5Ggps. It does require a 3 Amp 5VDC power supply (not included -1 Star) of some sort if you are going to be using external hard drives and the like.
I am glad I got this hub because I had two other 10 port USB hubs connected I thought were connected to USB 3.0 ports but when I started speed testing this hub, I noticed they were only transferring at USB 2.0 speeds. I connected all hubs to legit USB 3.0 ports and the speeds increased by 5 times. Almost all the things I have connected to the USB hubs work fine at USB 2.0 speeds, dongles, wireless headset etc. but if you transfer files on to a thumb drive or an external hard drive; you want the USB 3.0 speed.
With the other two 10 port hubs connected; when I connected this hub to my system it started to do squirrely things. The Logitech mouse & keyboard didn’t work and thumb drives would not register on some hubs but would on other hubs. I think this is a problem of my system; too many USB ports connected so I removed this one.
I connected this hub to my windows 11 laptop as the only hub and it worked perfectly with no problems. So, if you have a power supply and only use this hub; you should be fine. I really do like the looks and speed of this USB hub.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Sbc", "review_title": "No more cord chaos in the living room entertainment center", "review_text": "I didn't realize how much I needed to clear up my messy living room hub center for cords until I plugged in this 7-port USB 3.0 hub from Xiaobi. The solid aluminum alloy build feels genuinely sturdy and doesn't slide around thanks to the non-slip rubber base, which also keeps my TV stand safe from annoying scratches. With seven ports available, I can easily leave the grandkids' Xbox, PS4, external media drives, and peripheral receivers plugged in all at once without constantly swapping cables. Transferring large video files and photos takes just seconds with the speedy 5Gbps data transfer, and the 4-foot cable gives me plenty of slack to route it neatly behind my entertainment center. It even comes with a handy dedicated 5V power input port on the back to keep all my devices running super stable under a heavy workload. At this price point, getting a slim, travel-friendly, and wide-compatible hub that works seamlessly across multiple systems is an absolute steal for the value.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Paul Archambault", "review_title": "Solid hub, passes USB 3.0 speeds with no loss.", "review_text": "For being a USB 3.0 rating, this is a good hub. Solid metal construction with a tapered angle front for easier access. Rubber strips on the bottom of the HUB keep it in place. It has a tight form factor, up to seven devices without over crowding while keeping the overall width to a minimum.
The input USB C port is on the rear of the chassis, along with an external power input (optional). For my desk design, the rear ports don't work out well, plugging the cables into the rear of the HUB chassis, pushed it out away from the rear wall of my desk. Side input ports work out better for me.
Throughput speed is what you would expect for a 3.0 USB rating, there is no discernable loss of speed using the hub, it seems to pass data without any loss of packets or bandwidth.
For a 3.0 hub, the price point makes it a good value.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Adam Mitskevich", "review_title": "Useful Mix of USB-A and USB-C Ports", "review_text": "I like the combination of ports on this hub. The ports are spaced well and easy to access, and the metal housing has a solid feel.
The 4-foot cable is one of the more useful features for my setup. A lot of hubs have short cables that limit where they can be placed, while this one gives me enough length to position it where it is actually convenient on my desk.
It is also worth noting that this is primarily a USB data expansion hub. The additional USB-C connection on the back marked for power is there to provide supplemental power to the hub; it is not another data port or a charging port for connected devices.
Overall, this is a straightforward way to add several USB-A and USB-C connections while keeping everything organized in one compact hub.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "GoodErNah?", "review_title": "Nice Hub", "review_text": "This is a really cool design. The design makes really efficient use of the available room, and I like that you get quite a bit of functionality without having another bulky item sitting around. The speeds also seem nice and fast in my use, which makes it feel even more capable for something this compact.
