Mais dans le format ISO, il y a une touche supplémentaire, la touche "<" et ">" à coté de Shift. J'ai du créer un layout custom pour mettre ces caractères sur Algr+W et Algr+X, mais c'est pas idéal.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Alex B", "review_title": "Comfortable and modern.", "review_text": "The keyboard itself is good, although the keycaps are not defined well and mistypes were common (I replaced them with a somewhat generic full size keyset, which despite the low profile switch, works quite well - mind the rounded keyboard corners though. That did fix my typing issue though).
Functions well, and unlike some keyboards, off is off. The 2.4GHz dongle even works for USB wake. The QMK fork that the devs works well and is easy to use.
The switch between wired/wireless/off is a bit stiff at first but wears in well. I do wish it was more pronounced to be more easy to switch between modes though.
The cable did die super quickly though, for reasons I'm not entirely sure of. I switched the keyboard between wired and wireless, and one time it just didn't want to connect back. Fixed with a replacement cable without problem.
Overall, I like this keyboard. It's as compact as a keyboard with all the necessary keys, can be.", "review_rating": ""}]

The metrics are fantastic—sleep stages, recovery scores, strain, HRV, respiratory rate, and all the deep physiological insights feel accurate and meaningful. Reviso mi Recovery y HRV cada mañana, y eso me ha ayudado a tomar decisiones más informadas sobre cuándo exigirme y cuándo bajar el ritmo.
Lo que más valoro es cómo se volvió clave para mejorar hábitos generales: sueño, energía en las mañanas y alimentación. El Journal te deja agregar tus propios factores personalizados, así que puedes cruzar tus datos con lo que realmente te importa a ti, no solo con lo genérico.
La configuración inicial toma un poco de tiempo (calibración de varios días, ajustar metas, notificaciones), pero vale la pena una vez está bien ajustado.
Punto en contra: algunas funciones como Advanced Labs (exámenes presenciales) son exclusivas de EE.UU., así que si vives fuera no podrás usarlas del todo — aunque sí puedes subir tus propios resultados de laboratorio sin problema.
En general, muy recomendado si buscas datos reales para tomar mejores decisiones sobre tu salud y bienestar día a día.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "longfellow", "review_title": "Whoop has some good stats, and some fake hype too", "review_text": "WHOOP will be at you day and night; the device is very frisky when it comes to telling you your basic health stats and behaviors. However, I would like to add a few caveats:

Reviews: [{"reviewer_name": "Janette", "review_title": "Perfect Mix of Style and Function", "review_text": "I absolutely love my Garmin watch! It\u2019s sleek, comfortable, and has so many helpful features without feeling overwhelming. I especially love being able to track my workouts, steps, sleep, and daily activity all in one place. The display is bright and easy to read, and it\u2019s comfortable enough to wear all day and night.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "LDRB", "review_title": "Finally found the Fitness Watch that works as advertised!", "review_text": "I have tested numerous \u201csmart watches\u201d in my quest to find a decent replacement for my ever faithful and reliable, Fitbit Versa 4. I purchased it almost four years ago to replace the original Fitbit Versa. But then Google took over Fitbit, and I was looking for a reliable alternative to the Fitbit products. I tried a Samsung Galaxy watch 7 that lost steps by the thousands each day. I tried an Apple Smart Watch that sometimes had to be charged more than once EVERY DAY! I tried a Parsonver (less expensive) but even though it was advertised and labeled IP 68, (indicating that it would withstand submersion in water) I actually received an email from the company before the watch was even delivered advising me to be careful even showering or washing my hands with it on! SERIOUSLY???? And the step counts were not even close to correct! Then I tried an Amazfit BIP6 (also advertised as IP 68, but clearly IS NOT) and thought I had finally found what I was looking for, until it completely malfunctioned after only 3 weeks of use. So Amazon replaced it with ANOTHER BIP6, and that one lasted almost 5 months before it began to seriously malfunction and the touchscreen no longer worked. So my new search began and I decided to give Garmin a try as my walking and swimming buddies swear by their Garmins, and the results that they get with them compare favorably to my old Fitbit. I have now only had the Garmin Vivoactive 5 for about a month, but so far, it is AWESOME! It tracks extremely well with the Fitbit, and I have had no issues whatsoever with water infiltration. If that changes, I will be back to downgrade my rating, but so far, so GREAT! This proves that you don\u2019t have to buy the most expensive models of ANY brand of fitness watch to find one that does what you need it to do. Most of them have more functions than you will ever need or use anyway. I bought separate, different color bands to customize it and love that you have a lot of choices for watch faces, so pick the one that works best for you! (Although - once again, Fitbit has a much better and more user friendly watch face selection portal!)", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Kim", "review_title": "Love me a Garmin", "review_text": "I've been using Garmin for running for years now. They've improved a lot! This one does everything I need and more. I like the body battery, sleep info. The 5 syncs up to GPS much faster than my 4 to run or walk. I love the music, however, my headphones sometimes disconnect to the watch while running. Not sure if it's the headphones or the watch. It's pretty easy to use if you've had one before. It has changed on the strength where you hit the bottom button vs tapping the watch to enter weight/reps (don't have to do that anymore, not that it was a problem). Overall I'm super satisfied. Can see it better as well with the new display.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jared King", "review_title": "The best fitness tracker I've used", "review_text": "I'm coming from an Apple Watch Series 5. I had gotten frustrated with the battery life and sleep tracking and wanted to see if a more fitness-focused watch would be a better fit. I'm not a big runner or someone who does a lot of intense exercise, but I do like to track my exercise and sleep and get nudges to move when I've been sitting down for too long. I also like to get notifications on my wrist without needing to pull out my phone.\nCompared to the Apple Watch, the first major thing I noticed was this is nowhere close in terms of smarts. I had gotten used to Apple's smooth interface, built in microphone and speaker for voice commands, and often useful apps that can be used without needing to get my phone out. That being said, after a few days I can confidently say that I don't need them. I would argue that Garmin knows what this is and what it is not - it's a fitness device first and foremost, and everything else comes second. And on that basis they nailed it - the fitness tracking has been excellent and noticeably better than the Apple Watch especially in sleep tracking. I also much prefer their approach to goals, which tracks exercise over the course of a week rather than focusing specifically on individual days. Whenever I was sick or had a down day I would feel guilty if I didn't close all of my rings on my Apple Watch, but I don't feel that same pressure with the Garmin. I do miss being able to use voice commands with my watch, but I could have gotten a more expensive Garmin if I really wanted that, and I don't think it's worth it for me.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Amazon Customer", "review_title": "Good watch", "review_text": "This is my first Garmin. Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Jack", "review_title": "Packed with Upgraded GPS L1 & L5 tracking & 4 Med Sensors", "review_text": "A lot of Good things to say about this Sport watch. I don't know about reliability , but for accuracy, for med data like heart Beat, & Oxygen I measured those against my Oxi meter & Blood Pressure Kit and data was very accurate. The watch faces however, are not as Felxible/adjustable as others where some watches actually allows you to create them. This watch has a L1 & L5 GPS system which is highly reliable and unlike many other watches especially under $150 , will find a GPS signal within 3- 5 seconds per my test. It also has 4 sensors to give you more reliable health readings. It has as many, sleep mode that measures many factors. I had a $250 sport watch that did the same, (Recently died) and the results were within boundaries of the more expensive watch, but it did not track snoring . Battery life seems to be good though I only had this watch about 4 days , but I have been busy testing this one and another watch BVLRKSC . I tested distance accuracy with my Odo on my electric bike on both watches. The resutls were pretty good. You can spend a lot more $$ on other watches that have the same upgraded functions that the Pro 3 has, and not be any more accurate. Both watches are comfortable, though this watch tends to lean on less color, and less choices for dial display. I am leaning more on the other watch just for its Dial faces and easy choices , but its a tough decision because this one really packs a wallop for upgraded tech. The other watch you have to go into the App to sync up a GPS signal, that transfers to the watch (You don't have to have the phone with you after that) in order to use GPS within seconds, otherwsie you wait 3 -5 minutes. This watch connections to GPS within 3-5 seconds thanks to the L1 & L5 GPS. One can hardly go wrong with these watches. The only thing that I have read on this watch was poor follow up with the manufacture if you experience problems etc. Hopefully that's been addressed.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "KK", "review_title": "Fantastic for the price.", "review_text": "So I am coming to this watch from an absolutely ancient Apple Watch 2. The battery on that finally bit the bullet and wouldn't charge anymore.
Not wanting to spend the 200+ dollars on a new lower end Apple Watch, I decided to take the chance on this one after reading reviews and doing some research.
First in terms of looks - This looks fantastic. The watch faces are modern and there are so many options - from more minimal to hyper functional - displaying most of the metrics you would want to see in a smart watch/fitness tracker. I got the dark grey version and it is very clean. There is minimal branding with small text displaying "CMF by Nothing" on the rim around the watch face, but it is barely noticeable. The screen is bright, and I always have mine set on adaptive brightness. I haven't had any issues seeing the screen during a bright day yet.
The biggest plus for me is battery life! This thing will not die! The biggest issue I had with the Apple Watch was the battery life. Mine would die near the end of the day, even when the battery wasn't cooked from age. I had to constantly have it on the charge at the end of the day and never used its sleep tracking because the watch would be dead in the morning if I did. This definitely does not have that problem. I've worn this watch 3 days in a row without a charge, and even with pretty frequent use/checking it was still at 60ish percent. I usually charge it by putting it on the charger while I'm getting ready for work in the morning. It will go from 80ish percent to 95+ in the time I'm getting ready. I'm looking at the battery life right now - it is 2:30 in the afternoon and I've had the watch on me since I charged this morning around 6:30 - 95% battery life!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Aradhya", "review_title": "Great for the price!", "review_text": "The cmf watch 3 pro is an amazing stylish smartwatch. I’ve had it for a few months and this is my honest review. The quality of the app is unlike any, CMF or Nothing gives a great app experience that makes it very easy for users to work. The heart rate monitoring is absolutely amazing and is right most of the time. Features of the watch such as features work MOST of the time, not Apple Watch quality level, but potentially some of the best for 80$. The water resistance is great, I submerged it in water and noticed that speakers and microphone still worked great. The watch has many sizes to fit all. Certain features such as the news feel more like a gimmick than a feature. Now since I use an iPhone, many features don’t work too well because of how closed IOS is. This means that the software experience while is refined has multiple instances of not working. Bluetooth may disconnect sometimes, notifications can be buggy (not showing emojis or pictures) which some other watches at the same price do actually show. Overall this watch is amazing for the price point so its accuracy, material quality, ESPECCIALY at its price point. This is a great recommend to those who would like a smartwatch, but aren’t too serious about its features.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Fortiskev", "review_title": "Cheap Price but Great Smartwatch with Some Limitations", "review_text": "I decided to buy a new smartwatch because my previous one had died, wasn't charging so I saw this and did my check to see if it was worth buying.
Pros
Falls under 100USD so great price
Long Battery life 3 days use with everything on, wake on wrist, AOD, all the tracking everything.
No connectivity issues, gets all my notifications and everything no issues
all in one", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Zach", "review_title": "Practical but disappointing.", "review_text": "I wanna like the watch, but I immediately ran into a lot of limitations. The things I like about the watch and app follow plus some suggested tweaks. On the positive side customisable heart rate zones are useful, and it is easy to develop warm up, walk, run, repeat x8 workouts, which can then be modified in subsequent weeks. However, I had to use AI to pose a dozen or so technical questions about how to set up specific procedures and to analyse and interpret some of the performance data that the Garmin produces. Great buy!!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Ya Ya Queen", "review_title": "Recommended, lots of pluses, a few caveats", "review_text": "I've come to really like this rose gold smartwatch that I bought as a replacement for a Fitbit Charge 4. I have narrow wrists so it's big in comparison but as said, I'm getting used to it. I love being able to read it at a glance without squinting. The screen is sharp, crisp, gorgeous color and easy to read.
Set up was initially easy but when I started using the watch, customizing screens, layout of icons and grant it the permissions it needs, I had to turn to googling "IDW28" and found most of the answers i needed. I am fairly tech savvy and after a lot of frustration, I could only solve my issues this way. (The companion app was no help.) The biggest problem was the watch would compete with my ear buds, phone or bedside speaker to take over Bluetooth control, and attempt to direct the audio to the watch. Audio would cut in and out as it repeatedly tried to take control. I finally figured out what was wrong when I realized a phone call I received was switched to my watch. I had a Dick Tracy watch! 😂 Lol and the audio is not nearly loud enough to make calls on our listen to music.
Overall the watch with its phone app is exceptional to monitor steps, heart rate, sleep patterns, exercise sessions, stress level, water intake, weather and control your phone's music app, camera and much more. It also alerts you to notifications of messages and emails. Essentially it's the same notification that your phone displays (not the whole email or text) and you cannot respond. It does not measure blood pressure as some reviews suggest. It will connect to your AI asst but I don't need that.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Kassandra", "review_title": "Can't complain...much", "review_text": "Hello there, future watch owners. If you're like me, you've spent wayyy too much time agonizing over which knockoff smart watch to buy, and have probably read every review ever written. So, here is a list of every observed helpful and unfortunate aspect of this quality timepiece. I've been using it about a month.
Pros:
It looks nice. The screen is large enough to read and navigate easily, without feeling like you have a tablet on your wrist. The responsiveness is decent and the picture is clear. The swipe-right shortcut saves your most recent selections.
There are lots of options for what it can do. Workouts, music, phone, calculator, stress, sleep, O2, heart rate, water intake, and something I found especially helpful as someone who leaves their phone lying around, Find My Phone. I've used most of these but have barely scratched the surface on the sports/workouts.
Notifications show up with a red dot rather than a large icon, which I like and are easy to read and clear.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "foxinGirl", "review_title": "Great value smart watch with tons of features", "review_text": "This is a great budget smart watch for someone who is maybe interested in trying one and doesn't want to spend hundreds of pounds on a top branded one.
This watch offers you a wide variety of apps and facilities that you would find on a top branded watch
It has lots of health apps such as heart rate, sleep, blood oxygen levels and stress levels.
It also has a wide variety of fitness apps included which can help you begin your fitness journey with things like walking plans and running plans, or to continue in a journey with more advanced features.
The display is large and clear, colours of vibrant and it's a very sensitive screen allowing you to easily navigate your way through the various menus and settings.
You will download an app indicated in the instructions, this will allow you to fully personalise your watch as well as store your data - obviously your watch has a limited memory and you will need to store data externally.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Amy", "review_title": "Packed with Features and Surprisingly Polished", "review_text": "This smartwatch delivers far more than I expected at its price. It’s stylish and comfortable to wear, and the pink gold version looks particularly refined without feeling too flashy. The screen is clear and responsive, and basic navigation feels smooth.
Bluetooth calling has worked well, and the battery life has easily lasted a full week with moderate use. I like the health features, especially the heart rate and sleep tracking, which seem reasonably accurate for general wellness. Notifications come through reliably, and I’ve found the hydration reminders and camera shutter function more useful than expected.
The included extra strap is a nice touch, and the ability to swap bands with standard 22mm ones adds even more versatility. While I didn’t dive deep into the fitness modes, the range of options is impressive for anyone with an active routine.
The app has room for improvement, especially in reducing clutter and simplifying customization, but it does what’s needed once set up. Overall, this is a very capable smartwatch that gets a lot right, especially for everyday tracking and light communication needs.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Mrs Natalie Anne Webster", "review_title": "Lovely watch", "review_text": "I can’t seem to find anywhere to message seller direct. My watch won’t charge or turn on.
I bought in December so I know it’s been 7 months, however it does say 5 year guarantee and to just message the seller if any issues, sad this isn’t made easy.
Review update: After writing this review the company kindly reached out to me and offered me a full refund or replacement watch. I requested the replacement and I am very happy I did, my new watch arrived within days. The watch was easy to set up and sync with my phone. It is working beautifully and after using for a few days I still have good battery life. Very different to my first experience so it must just have been a faulty one.
The watch itself has some nice features like the weather app, steps monitor, BP monitor etc. It also sends me notifications when I get messages through my phone including Whatsapp.
Thank you so mush for taking the time to resolve my issue and I look forward to using my watch with confidence.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Deb from Oz", "review_title": "Awesome", "review_text": "This feature-packed watch goes beyond just telling time, diligently tracking your steps and much more. Setting it up is a breeze, and personalizing the watch face to match your style is a real treat. With its stunning design and the comfortable Velcro band option, it not only looks fantastic but performs exceptionally well, rivaling watches at three times the price – making it an incredible value.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Lucio", "review_title": "Ottimo prodotto ricco di funzioni ed adatto ad ogni occasione!", "review_text": "Questo smartwatch della AEAC si è dimostrato un prodotto davvero valido e qualitativamente ben fatto. Arriva a casa in una scatolina carina bianca con l’immagine di un orologio e la scritta smartwatch. Aprendo il packing troviamo lo smartwatch con cassa quadrata di colore dorato con un cinturino in silicone di colore rosa già montato. In dotazione abbiamo poi il cavo di ricarica usb con attacco magnetico e il libretto di istruzioni con la lingua italiana.
L’orologio, che è un articolo da donna, si presenta molto elegante e adatto ad ogni tipo di occasione. Presenta 1 pulsante al lato che serve per accenderlo/spegnerlo e per navigare nei vari menù e sottomenù, in alternativa al touch screen che risulta comunque preciso e sensibile. Una volta acceso compare la schermata iniziale ed effettuando swipe si scelgono le varie funzioni.
Le cose che questo smartwatch può fare sono davvero tante: per le sportive ci sono tutte quelle funzioni relative al benessere del corpo dovute a più di 100 attività tra le quali nuoto, trekking, corsa etc.etc. Ci sono anche molte funzioni più o meno utili come contapassi, cardiofrequenzimetro, monitoraggio ossigeno, monitoraggio del sonno e misuratore di pressione. Poi ci sono le funzioni di un orologio classico come la sveglia e il datario e le funzioni smart che attraverso un collegamento bluetooth ad uno smartphone ci permettono di leggere messaggi da app social come instagram e facebook o da applicazioni come messanger o whatsapp.", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: Smart Watch with Alexa Built-in, 1.83" HD Bluetooth Calling Fitness Tracker
Description: Bluetooth 5.3 Call and Message Notification: Cillso smart watch features an advanced single-chip processor and sensitive microphone, enabling direct call making and answering. When you enable the "VeryFit" App to receive messages, notifications will be displayed on the smartwatch. Get all your messages and notifications (Facebook, Twitter, WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, Linkedin,Skype etc.) sent straight to your smartwatch with intuitive customizable vibrations
Category: Electronics,Wearable Technology,Smartwatches
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Baby T", "review_title": "Good quality for price!", "review_text": "For somebody who doesn’t wanna spend $100+ on a smart watch I do really like this one, affordable, it works pretty, easy to use, well now am I expecting the step counting and calories to be exact? No. But it’s a great tool for if I don’t wanna carry my phone. I love that I can receive my calls and text through it, I do wish I could respond to texts but that’s okay it keeps me off my phone some. Now I’ve had it for 8months and worn it every single day just about, and my latch finally broke 🥲 I’m sad I don’t wanna order another watch. I wonder if I can easily replace the band or latch.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "J. Ward", "review_title": "An excellent value!", "review_text": "My watch works very well. Make sure the download the VeryFit app set up some features and monitor your workouts. Also, when attaching the power connector to the watch and One direction it will magnetically clamp to the back of the watch if you flip it around it will not, so make sure it holds on tight. You can set it to respond to incoming phone calls via a sound or a vibration or silent and it will also show you snippets of text messages and emails. I really like this watch. Try to select a snug fit around your wrist, not a loose one, not a tight one just snug. Battery power will last for days. Don't let yourself be frustrated by the information in the manual. There's only a small section in English that will help you get it connected the rest of it is pretty straightforward on the watch and the VeryFit app. You may also select from a large variety of watch faces through the app.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Lynn", "review_title": "Exceed my expectation", "review_text": "This is a great deal. It integrates so many functions onto it, which is way much beyond my expectation for smart watch at this price. The most practical functions for me so far are the stopwatch, camera control, sleep monitoring, and music control. It functioning like a 10 times more expensive watch, highly recommend it.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "cher", "review_title": "Mostly Glad I Bought It", "review_text": "I am really liking this watch! I was horribly sad when I broke my Apple watch. I refused to pay to fix it or to pay for a new more expensive one. This watch made my month. Rarely it does something annoying like warn me about high heart rate that is not high, not switch time zones, or light up too much bursting forth light while I try to sleep, but the price made it well worth it. Plus, the battery lasts about 5 days. Oh, I had to go back and edit this post to mention that...it does disconnect from my phone a lot which is mildly annoying but no biggie. I don't care for the charger though. It is a bit wonky, but it does work. In addition, the band would fit a huge range of sizes.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Sarah Davidson", "review_title": "Great smartwatch for an Android (Google pixel)", "review_text": "I had gotten a different smart watch originally just so I could see who was texting or calling so I didn't have to have my phone out all the time. It was junk! I stumbled across this watch and am sad I didn't replace the other one sooner! This is a big enough screen to be able to see the start of a text or email, but not so big that restricts mobility! Decent range between phone and watch to keep the Bluetooth connection, and accurate steps count! Also love that I can customize the picture it uses for the home screen", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Joe", "review_title": "Great Value Smartwatch with Useful Features", "review_text": "For the price, this watch has been a nice surprise. It looks good on my wrist, feels comfortable even after wearing it for hours, and I really like the color. Pairing was easy, the connection stays stable, and calls come through clearly without much delay.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Ashley C.", "review_title": "Not Built for the Water", "review_text": "It’s honestly a decent smart watch/exercise/step tracker, and connectivity on land is pretty good (I can go a fair distance in open space away from my phone before the watch disconnects). Battery life is pretty good, and it does receive texts and allows you to control your music.
I am writing this review as someone who works in aquatics-specifically spending a lot of time in the water. While the watch does have good water resistance, the connectivity under water is non existent and it also tends to react as though I’m manipulating the screen (I am aware that all these complaints are normal with water). All in all, it’s not what I was looking for.
One other MINOR complaint. The app that comes with the watch gives you the ability to personalize your home screen (which is genuinely fun/a great feature). A lot of them come with a “current outside temp” reading, but I can never get this part of the home screen to connect properly regardless of the home screen in question. A petty complaint but a complaint nonetheless XD
All in all, it’s probably great for on land day to day/exercise, but definitely not for water related activities.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Amazon Customer", "review_title": "So far so good", "review_text": "I love this watch. It was easy to set up the Veryfit app does not have ads only internal options to upgrade and buy. I'm giving it four stars instead of five because I've had it less than 60 days so I'm not sure about the longevity and the wristband is a little stiff. But no binding issues and the quality of phone calls is good. I have not used it for music or exercise but the step counter is accurate. And it even lets you know when the charger is attached", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Peter Scully", "review_title": "Works a treat.", "review_text": "Not a true smart watch which can operate without a phone, but the features it does have work extremely well. You can sign up for a fitness tracker, or just use it to check vitals on the go. Only annoyance is the magnetic charging piece, nowhere near as easy as Qi charging, but it is a lot more affordable than others. We used it to monitor blood oxygen when suffering from influenza A - the missus has asthma, but no need to go to hospital if O2 remains above 90%", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Brandt", "review_title": "Ideal para uso diario", "review_text": "Este reloj inteligente con Alexa y pantalla de 1,83″ me ha sorprendido para bien, especialmente por lo completo que es para su precio. Ya desde el tamaño de la pantalla se nota que puedes leer notificaciones y ver información sin forzar la vista, y con Alexa integrada se siente más “inteligente” que otros relojes básicos.
Al abrir la caja encontramos:
El propio reloj un cable magnetico para cargar y un folleto a modo de manual de instrucciones.
Lo primero es ponerlo a cargar y luego escanear con el movil el codigo QR para obtener la aplicación Veryfit.
Lo que más me ha gustado:
La integración con llamadas y notificaciones funciona fluida y hace que no tengas que sacar siempre el móvil.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "ANNADIMAR", "review_title": "Tantissime funzioni e bellissimo design", "review_text": "Fra i tanti smartwatch provati, ammetto che questo è sicuramente fra i migliori! Ha addirittura100 modalità sportive diverse!! Qualunque sia il tipo di allenamento che si sceglie di fare, trovate la funzione adatta!! L'ho indossato durante la notte e il monitoraggio del sonno è molto preciso e vi aiuta a migliorare la qualità del sonno. È resistente all'acqua con codice IP68, infatti l'ho provato sotto la doccia. Si possono inoltrare chiamate direttamente dal display. Lo consiglio vivamente!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "dino", "review_title": "Acquisto positivo!!", "review_text": "Comperato nel 2024 è un prodotto ottimo !", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Amazon Customer", "review_title": "Une montre intelligente complète et étonnamment convaincante pour le prix", "review_text": "1) Mise en route et connexion
La configuration initiale se fait sans difficulté majeure. L’appairage avec le téléphone est rapide et stable, à condition d’installer l’application compagnon requise. Ce passage est obligatoire pour exploiter pleinement les fonctions, mais l’ensemble reste accessible même pour un utilisateur peu habitué aux objets connectés.
Connexion fluide dès la première tentative.
Application nécessaire pour les réglages et le suivi des données.
Synchronisation fiable au quotidien.
2) Fonctions et usage au quotidien

Notifications, appels via Bluetooth et suivi d’activité pratiques.", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: Amazfit Active Max Smart Watch, 1.5" AMOLED Display, GPS, iOS/Android
Description: BIGGER DISPLAY. MAX CLARITY: Active Max features a shine brighter screen with a 3,000-nit display engineered for ultimate clarity, even under the harshest sunlight. See your data clearly on a large 1.5″ ultra-bright AMOLED display built for easy readability in any condition — from the gym to the mountains.
Category: Electronics,Wearable Technology,Smartwatches
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Michael JS", "review_title": "Best smart watch ever made !!!!", "review_text": "Amazing !!!!!!!!!!!! I’ve had the Apple Watch SE the Apple Watch Ultra 2 . The bip active max it’s beyond better I actually get all my notifications messages with sounds alert, massive days without charging truly a smart watch that everybody should have I could not stand charging my Apple Watch every day. The active Max does all the vitals track steps like a track dog. It’s really amazing. I’m so happy I got it really high-quality . 170 dollars is extremely good for all you get !!! It’s great and highly recommend . Big round interactive face makes it very resourceful with interactive icons and multi function ..", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jotten32", "review_title": "This watch has big bang for your buck!", "review_text": "This watch is awesome! I’ve used Apple watch for years and the battery life on that is terrible. Very different story for the Amazfit Active Max! I’ve had it for a month now and haven’t fully exhausted the battery life on this one yet. I have charged it back to full a couple times, but I’m on my 9th day now, attempting to drain the charge completely to cycle the battery, still at 27%. The Zepp app syncs with IOS health and it has so many features! I was looking at $500-$600 Garmin watches before this, but this watch does everything they do. I’ve also inadvertently banged the bezel on the countertops in my home several times, no scratches! Went for a jog the other day and the watch started a workout and mapped my run! There’s a lot of free watch faces to load to it, and very simple and quick updates. I’ve also used the phone feature to receive a call and the voice and sound were crystal clear! This is a great watch, I absolutely recommend it!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "door", "review_title": "Not just a sport watch", "review_text": "Excellent battery life paired with one of the brightest screens. OS is snappy and rich in useful features. 3000 nit screen is great for viewing in bright daylight. The flashlight function is one of the most used features on my watch. The light can be toggled to red as well. The sleep tracking is improved over the balance model. Find my phone is another feature that I use daily. I prefer this to apple or popular android brands. The watch itself has a nice sporty look but can also be dressed up just by changing the clock face. This is my 3rd amazfit and they just keep getting better. The price is a steal. This is a legitimate high end brand with some fantastic budget watches. Lastly, there are many accessories from 3rd party manufactures available.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "enrique berrocal", "review_title": "Solid smartwatch that punches above its price", "review_text": "Stunning 1.5" AMOLED display with sharp, vibrant colors even in direct sunlight, 25-day battery life is genuinely impressive and delivers as advertised, built-in GPS maps work reliably without needing your phone nearby, lightweight and comfortable for all-day wear. Overall a fantastic value smartwatch — the battery life and display alone justify the purchase.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "PaulN", "review_title": "Perfect in many ways", "review_text": "It’s been a week now since the purchase and I can honestly say this is an excellent smart watch!

Functionality: Excellent and very responsive. I would say, it beats my Apple watch in receiving the same alerts from the phone!
If you’re very active and do all kinds of sports, you’re in luck. The watch is loaded with functions for any sport imaginable. These functions can be turned on or off / customized to suit your life style.
Zepp app: The Zepp app is used to set up / pair / customize the watch and it is an excellent app actually!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "WrekyllNHyde", "review_title": "I really can't say enough.", "review_text": "Best smart watch I have used by far. This watch is so easy to use, has a huge display, fits snuggly, looks great and holds up in my job, working with my hands.
I really can't say enough, I have tried several other smart watches for long periods of time and this in two weeks is by far superior. This is my first review for any watch I own. I use my watch and phone for personal communication as well as fitness tracking and it uses maybe 5% battery life a day, max.
It was an excellent purchase. Glad I did. Would buy again. Wish It was around sooner.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "wall walker", "review_title": "Yes it’s what Apple should be making. You’ll like it !", "review_text": "I’ve been an Apple Watch wearer for many years. I eventually was tired of how the battery life just didn’t cut it. I thought I’d try this watch. The size is easy to read and it’s simply a wiser choice.
It’s a great watch", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Ralph Bergin Jr.", "review_title": "Not bad for the price.", "review_text": "Had it for about 3 weeks now. It was very uncomfortable and actually gave me a pretty bad rash so I replaced it with a flexible one.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "VIKRANT KULKARNI", "review_title": "Runners Watch", "review_text": "I used coros pace 3 for almost 2.5 years until there was hardware issue with crown and touchscreen. Next I decided to go with Amazfit watch because i had good experience with my GTS and BIP. Scrolling around I came to know about newly launched Active Max. After using coros pace 3 i was not expecting much from this watch but to my surprise it surpassed my expectations. It did everything what my coros pace 3 did and at not so expensive price tag. It is pretty accurate in distance, heart rate, calories tracking. The calling feature is amazing and speaker and mic are crystal clear. So many good features like quick notifications, bt calling, offline and online music control, AI coaching, Always on display and not to forget it has a very strong gps connection. Gps locks up very fast, within few seconds and doesn’t loose signals throughout the run.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "High Tech Hen", "review_title": "Surprisingly amazing for the price.", "review_text": "I am pleasantly impressed by this watch especially since it's replacing my Garmin Forerunner 945 which has lost its bezel seal. Title: Samsung Galaxy Watch 8 (2025), Graphite, 40mm, Bluetooth Smartwatch
Description: WHY GALAXY WATCH8: Advanced health and sleep tracking features.* A lighter, more snug design for all day comfort.* Improved user interface.* Personal AI assistant for hands free help.⁴* 2-Year Warranty.
Category: Electronics,Wearable Technology,Smartwatches
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "javier navarro", "review_title": "Returned this and upgraded to LTE version", "review_text": "I've had Garmins and Fitbits only in the past and this is just a huge, massive upgrade. Love the customizations that can be done with the watch too with the cool looking bands and faces that I bought separately on Amazon. I've had it for a year without any screen protectors and it's been durable enough that it's held up well with very little wear and tear on it, but I'm wise enough to use protectors for it now. My only complaint is the battery. It's a bit disappointing that the battery barely lasts a day. I've had to buy 3 chargers for it. One charger for my car, one for work, and one for home because this thing dies fast if you plan to work out with it and use it all day. Still, I love this watch.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "BL60", "review_title": "Great for Water Sports!", "review_text": "I have had a Samsung Galaxy watch since they first came out. My first one is still going strong, but I needed one that would track my activity in the water, since the majority of my activity is water related. This watch is great for that! It has been in the water with me now almost daily for weeks and works like a charm! I have an app that will automatically set the watch to the water mode, or I can set it myself. It counts each step, stroke and workout moment - and seems to do so accurately. The size is a nice upgrade from the earlier versions, being slightly easier to read. All my apps and information were easily transferred to this new watch, making the transition seamless. It doesn't vibrate quite as strongly as my last one did, so I miss a notification here and there, but since my phone is never more than a few feet away from me, that really isn't an issue. Time will tell if it lasts as long as my first watch did, but I am really so impressed with this watch. To me, it is worth spending the cash to have the added assurance of counting my water activities.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "LeZette Polanco", "review_title": "Love my watch !!", "review_text": "I'm normally a regular watch wearing person but have been contemplating on getting either an apple watch or samsung to switch things up, I finally switched from apple products to Samsung and decided to go all out with the samsung tech and I couldn't be happier. Title: Garmin Forerunner® 165, Running Smartwatch, 43mm, Black
Description: Easy-to-use running smartwatch with built-in GPS for pace/distance and wrist-based heart rate; brilliant AMOLED touchscreen display with traditional button controls; lightweight design in 43 mm size
Category: Electronics,Wearable Technology,Smartwatches
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "HwnMelody", "review_title": "Good economy sport watch", "review_text": "Best purchase I made all year. I started running recently, training for a marathon at the end of the year. I used to spend my time trying to take my run time and miles to try and calculate my pace. Now I just look at my watch and all the metrics are right there for me. It can take all of my runs and predict my race times. I no longer have to guess how many miles I put in for my run or for the entire week. It gives you heart rate, HRV, VO2 Max, step counts, sleep scores and suggested training plans. Battery life is good. If you’re running a lot and using the GPS, the battery will drain faster. I tend to charge after my long run.
If you’re in training, and looking for a good sports watch, consider this one.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Christopher Henry", "review_title": "13 days battery life", "review_text": "Ok so I purchased this Garmin 165 watch for just $200. So the price was excellent. It has a nice bright amoled screen and has a good build quality. However, I only use this watch as a fitness, wellness and running watch. That is, I turned off the notifications. I don't see the point of trying to read a notification or message on a watch face when my phone is right next to me. So with notifications turned off I got 13 days of battery life before the watch went down to 9%. I also do not have on the "always on display". With this set up you can get 13 days of regular (non smart watch) use. This is what I wanted the most, a descent battery. So having to just charge the watch every 2 weeks or twice a month is really great. I also wore the watch every day and did walking workouts. One thing to note : I DID NOT SLEEP WITH THE WAATCH ON... I do not know if that helped the battery life but I generally do not sleep with any watched or rings or anything restrictive when I sleep.. I need comfort... lol.. But I did sleep one night with it and it was comfortable.. just not my thing... but great watch, connected to GPS is seconds, gives good info in the app and is comfortable. Highly recommend for someone who is into fitness... it can track most activities like running, walking, swimming, hiking, trail run, in door run etc.. most general activities.... look... there is really no need to go out an buy a $500 or $900 watch.. this one does the job at $200.. no point getting a watch that gives you tons of stats that you will not use or understand... if you do triathlons or want those pretty maps on the watch then by all means get the more expensive watch but if you just want to keep healthy and run.. then this watch is prefect..", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "BigRon", "review_title": "Great running watch", "review_text": "I’ve been running for over 20 years and have only ever used by Apple Watch and before that my timex iron man running watch. Getting a dedicated running watch like this is a game changer. So many more metrics and options to use while running and to review after running has really made me a better runner. I’ve had this watch about 8 months now and have had no issues at all. Heart rate functions great for all day monitoring. I have used a chest strap for a long time for activity monitoring. Even w this watch chest strap heart rate monitoring is the only way to go for accuracy. Wrist based monitors are ok, but if your training and trying to hit certain heart rate zones I would to recommend a chest strap. W that said. Compared to my Apple Watch this wrist based monitor is better. It locks on faster and seems to be pretty accurate. Screen is easy to see in bright sunlight and inside as well. U get access to free training plans within the Garmin app which is easy
to use but looks a bit outdated. W this watch you don’t get training load or training status or readiness like the more expensive Garmin watches but u do get training effect for each workout for aerobic and anaerobic metrics. I use iPhone and have the watch set to notify for calls and text only and the rest of my phone notifications are send silently to my notification widget on the watch which I love. Helps minimize distractions. The watch stays connected very good to my iPhone 14 and always syncs w the Garmin app. The strap the comes w it is comfortable but I did switch it out for a nylon strap which I feel is better and lighter. I would highly recommend this watch for its functionality, metrics and price when u can find it on sale. Overall Garmin products are over priced. But having a worry free experience when paired w an iPhone and accurate training metrics is worth it for this particular device.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Michael", "review_title": "Garmin Forerunner 165", "review_text": "As a half marathon runner training for a full marathon, I wanted this watch to be my full time training partner (and bully at times..lol). I notice a large improvement from my previous watch (apple watch series 10 I believe). It has great tracking for mileage, pace, HR, and a more accurate Vo2max. The sleep metrics are detailed well, I just wish the alarms were louder. The set up was very easy to complete, just create a Garmin account, sync your watch, and boom, you’re in. The battery life is insane, up to a week of battery for me (depending on usage) and very fast to charge. I like that the bands are removable to make it easier to clean the watch after getting sweaty or dirty. The watch itself is clean looking, I love the black color with the grey band.
However, it was a little confusing for the first few days of me having it, trying to learn how to use it, navigate it, and get the hang of where everything is. The manual doesn’t help much 😅😅.
Over all, best (impulsive) purchase I think I have made so far! I don’t regret it and look forward to continue training with the Forerunner series! 💪💪", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "tyler", "review_title": "Top notch", "review_text": "My first Garmin and I love it! Even though it’s an older version it does everything I need it to. Love the battery life and the step tracker. Links well with Strava and tracking my walks and runs. I especially love the heart rate monitor and pace tracker. Definitely a game changer if you take running seriously. I love the break down as well of the zones and seeing where you can improve. Has all the same features as the iwatch but better. I’d say the only downside is not being able to reply to messages off the watch. But I’ll take it.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Amazon Customer", "review_title": "Incredible first smartwatch – lightweight, comfy, and amazing screen!", "review_text": "This is my very first smartwatch, and I am absolutely blown away by it! The colorful AMOLED display is incredibly bright, clear, and easy to read. Since it’s my first time using a smartwatch, I am still learning all the features, and it feels like there is a huge variety of functions to explore.One of the best things about this watch is how lightweight it is. It is so light that when I am wearing it, I barely even notice it's on my wrist!Another big difference from traditional watches is the rubber (silicone) strap.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "George Ross", "review_title": "Nice watch, great battery life. Good for small wrists too.", "review_text": "This is a nice watch with very nice features. Was a great price for this kind of watch and has enough features at this price range, but cannot compare with the other watches that cost more. But this does what I need it to do. It's small enough and light enough for a small wrist as well as a bigger wrist. Using the app, you can made the readout bigger if needed. Numbers track very well, similar with the Well known watch that costs more, as compared on their app with garmins. It is comfortable to sleep with and the battery life is great! Overall, a great watch that is really accurate.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "C Long", "review_title": "Great for Fitness Metrics", "review_text": "It seems like a good watch and can do all the things for health/fitness/recovery metrics that Garmin is so well known for. The band was a little skinny for my liking (kinda looked like a “girls” watch if I’m allowed to say that). And perhaps it was a learning curve, but it just didn’t feel very user friendly. Maybe hardcore fitness people aren’t as concerned with changing songs (or maybe they don’t listen to music at all) and doing “smart watch” things. If you want to track fitness metrics, this is great. If you want a smart watch, this probably isn’t the one for you.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Laudiceia Balbino Esmeraldo", "review_title": "Excelente compra!", "review_text": "Excelente! Cumpre o que promete! Foi presente e a pessoa adorou!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Kenneth LEE WM", "review_title": "Great GPS watch for runners that syncs with SG's Healthy 365 app (steps, mvpa, sleep)", "review_text": "I have been using a G-Shock GBX-100 for a couple of years now to track my runs but I also wanted to track my heart rate at the same time. This watch ticks all the boxes for me.
- track steps
- accurate distance (GPS)
- track heart rate during runs
bonus for me
- running courses
- coaching
- resting recommendations
- electronic wallet payment via Revolut (the only credit card supported in singapore)
- basic navigation ie: direction/distance to a saved location", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Hannan", "review_title": "Stunning watch with amazing battery life!", "review_text": "I’ve been using the Garmin Forerunner 165 for a few weeks now, and it’s honestly one of the best purchases I’ve made for running and daily tracking. The bright touchscreen is gorgeous—super vibrant and easy to read even in direct sunlight, which makes checking stats mid-run a breeze.
GPS is spot-on for pace and distance, wrist-based heart rate feels accurate, and I love the adaptive training suggestions and recovery insights that help me avoid overdoing it. Battery life is solid too—easily lasts a full week with regular runs, and up to 11 days in smartwatch mode.
Lightweight, comfortable to wear all day, and packed with way more features than I expected at this price point. If you’re getting into running or want a reliable Garmin without breaking the bank, this is it. Highly recommend!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Víctor", "review_title": "Garmin Forerunner 165: El reloj para correr sin enrollos", "review_text": "Primeras impresiones: Minimalismo en estado puro
El Garmin Forerunner 165 entra por los ojos si eres fan de lo simple y funcional. No es el típico reloj con acabados premium, pero sí transmite ligereza y un diseño sin cosas de más. Si buscas algo minimalista que acompañe tu día, da el pego tanto para salir a correr como para ponértelo todo el día sin que moleste o cante.
¡Corre sin distracciones!
Este reloj es la definición de “ponértelo y listo”. Si lo tuyo es correr (ya sea por hobby, para entrenar en serio o simplemente porque te ayuda a respirar mejor), el Forerunner 165 deja de lado los extras sobrantes y se concentra en lo más importante: medir bien tu distancia, ritmo, frecuencia cardíaca y darte datos útiles mientras corres o andas.
El GPS engancha rápido y el seguimiento es acertado, casi sin margen de error como cabría esperar de un Garmin.
Salud y motivación al toque", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Regis Gabineski", "review_title": "Ótima relação custo benefício", "review_text": "O relógio é um absurdo de bom! Muitas funcionalidades e integração com app. Uso para natação e os indicadores são ótimos! Para dormir, os indicadores são extremamente precisos. Ótimo garmin de entrada. Possui sistema operacional avançado e hardware mais simples, o que faz dele uma ótima relação custo-benefício!", "review_rating": ""}]

[{"reviewer_name": "Jack", "review_title": "Packed with Upgraded GPS L1 & L5 tracking & 4 Med Sensors", "review_text": "A lot of Good things to say about this Sport watch. I don't know about reliability , but for accuracy, for med data like heart Beat, & Oxygen I measured those against my Oxi meter & Blood Pressure Kit and data was very accurate. The watch faces however, are not as Felxible/adjustable as others where some watches actually allows you to create them. This watch has a L1 & L5 GPS system which is highly reliable and unlike many other watches especially under $150 , will find a GPS signal within 3- 5 seconds per my test. It also has 4 sensors to give you more reliable health readings. It has as many, sleep mode that measures many factors. I had a $250 sport watch that did the same, (Recently died) and the results were within boundaries of the more expensive watch, but it did not track snoring . Battery life seems to be good though I only had this watch about 4 days , but I have been busy testing this one and another watch BVLRKSC . I tested distance accuracy with my Odo on my electric bike on both watches. The resutls were pretty good. You can spend a lot more $$ on other watches that have the same upgraded functions that the Pro 3 has, and not be any more accurate. [{"reviewer_name": "Kyle", "review_title": "Slim and reliable iPhone case with good protection", "review_text": "I’m very happy with the ESR iPhone 14 Pro Case. MagSafe compatibility works well
Clear design looks great
Durable build quality", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Robert H.", "review_title": "Legit Military-Grade protection without the "Brick" feel!", "review_text": "If you’re tired of cases that claim to be "tough" but feel like cheap plastic, or "rugged" cases that make your phone too big to fit in a pocket, the ESR Military-Grade Shockproof Case is the upgrade you’ve been looking for. Title: NOCO GENIUS1 1A 6/12V Smart Battery Charger, Trickle Charger & Maintainer
Description: MEET THE GENIUS1 — Similar to our G750, just better. It's 35% smaller and delivers over 35% more power. It's the all-in-one charging solution - battery charger, battery maintainer, trickle charger, plus desulfator.
Category: Automotive,Tools & Equipment,Jump Starters, Battery Chargers & Portable Power,Battery Chargers
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Shane", "review_title": "Works as intended", "review_text": "So I just bought a brand new one two years, but it’s because I never registered the warranty for our first one. This is basically a one piece kit that is a great starter for battery charging for most kinds of automotive and marine batteries. It’s very simple to use, and the one reason our last one stopped functioning is because of built in fail safes. In this case: my wife and I were washing our camper and this got wet and then got some dirt on it, it got through the water resistant seal and the charger could detect this. The great news is the charger will literally cease to function if it has become damaged. It will give a flashing red light, and you cannot put it into Force Charge mode. The only downside is unless you have a multimeter, you may not know that it has become damaged internally. I figured it out because of the mode not working, and it wouldn’t charge any batteries. The fuse was fine. So make sure you register this when you get it. It does the job and the only way you know it’s working is because of the status light, as it is beyond quiet. It’s basically a plug with the clamps for the battery terminals, so it is easy to store and carry around. I highly recommend this charger if you need something simple without a lot of functionality, just don’t leave it exposed to the elements.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "C. Nekritz", "review_title": "Little Miracle", "review_text": "Okay, I did NOT expect this little thing to work, but it did and might for you IF you have patience.
My Grandfather who was MoAT (Mechanic of All Things) owned back in the day what I thought were REAL chargers, they were so big and heavy they had to be put on wheels and rolled around, they had giant switches that'd illuminate and while I'm probably purely imagining this they were plugged into 220-volt outlets. This thing fits in the palm of my hand, just as pictured, smaller than most mobile phones. "Huh," I said, "this should be comical."
I hooked it up and, as others have said, figuring this thing out is NOT straight forward, the instruction manual is weak to say the least, the good news is, as I found, there are many intrepid experimenters who, like me, bought it on a whim and did some trial and error which it'd seem 99% of them got the thing to work to their needs, just like me hence, I'm taking the time to write this review. What this lacks in coherent features or instructions it makes up for it in the end by eventually (boy I mean eventually) getting the job done, for that honestly I'm giving it a generous five stars, because it did what I wanted it do against all odds, just like the Phil Collins song. ("Just take a look at my car now, 'cause it's finally starting here.")", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "dsk", "review_title": "Reliable. Battery was ready when needed", "review_text": "In January 2026, the temperature dropped to -25°, without wind-chill, over 3 days. The electricity went out. I needed to start my emergency generator, and the battery was dead. I start the generator every month and run it for 1 hour to maintain the battery. This battery was only 7 months old. I was lucky. I had a battery for the sump pump in case of emergency, and I was able to use it.
Here it is the end of August 2026, and we've been experiencing thunderstorms daily. Last night the electricity went out. I've had the battery on the NOCO Genius 1 since January. I installed it and the generator started right up.
The battery has been on the charger for 7 months, so if there was a problem with the charger, I'd know by now. The charger is reliable and it protects the battery. Choose the right one by amperage of your battery.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Brian", "review_title": "Seems pretty good so far", "review_text": "I have two of these. They are not exactly the same model (I think one of them is an older version of this model). The older one, I have had in the garage for several years to keep the batteries in the cars up when they are not driven very often. Some people say these are not for car batteries and I won't argue with them but the one I have out there definitely keeps the battery in my 2001 Corolla charged. And in fact, we had an incident where someone left a dome light on in that car and drained the battery to the point to where there was absolutely no response from anything electrical in the car. We started the car with a jumper pack, pulled it in the garage and connected it to the Noco and let it do it's thing. That's been at least a year and that battery is still going strong in that car.

[{"reviewer_name": "Chris C", "review_title": "About The Charging Speed...", "review_text": "Many reviews mention that it charges oh, so slowly. I tried lots of things. So, I'm starting out disagreeing with it's biggest problem, according to many reviews. It charged to 100% in about 4 hours. At 100%, it showed 1 minute remaining and it stayed that way for a very long time. I unplugged it for about 5 minutes and plugged it back in. It started out right back at 60 watts, but dropped quickly to 44 watts. LiFePo batteries do that. I have huge ones in my off-grid solar and you have to set them up for an "equalization" phase on the charge controller. Time to stop getting more and more technical. This thing charged from 30% to 100% in about 4 hours. My plug-in power bank got quite warm, almost hot, during this time. The charging cable, itself, got a little warm. Title: NOCO GENIUS10 10A 6/12V Smart Battery Charger, Trickle Charger & Maintainer

Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "SlickBuyer", "review_title": "Perfect for a second car that doesn't get driven often", "review_text": "I was hesitant to buy one of these because of the reviews about fires. Don't pay attention to those reviews. This little trickle charger keeps your car battery at full and in brand new condition. I read somewhere online that if you put a brand new AGM battery in your car like I did and keep this NOCO Genius10 hooked up, the battery can theoretically last up to 10 years because the NOCO will continuously keep it charged and repaired. It seems that my battery was not the problem with my car as the starter relay on the clutch needed replacing so now my car starts again. But I put in a new AGM battery anyways and won't have to worry about replacing it for another 7-10 years as long as I keep the NOCO attached when not driving the car for long periods of time.
As for the NOCO functionality itself it has a couple buttons, one to choose what kind of battery you are using, regular 12V, AGM, or Lithium Ion. The cord length is not very long so in order for my NOCO to reach my car battery and the wall socket in my garage I used a decent gauge extension cord. The instructions say not to use an extension cord but there is no other way since my wall outlet in my garage is too far away from the car battery. Now, I keep the Genius5 connected to my motorcycle whenever I’m not riding for more than a week, and I haven’t had any battery issues since. [{"reviewer_name": "modemman", "review_title": "Good HD 120 FOV webcam (if you don't mind orange)", "review_text": "I got this for a very specific purpose where a c930c (with a 90 degree field of view) did not do the job - trying to stream a robotics competition where the 12' by 12' playing field has to be seen in entirety. This is an issue for me because I use a custom web-base app that has no settings, this webcam comes with no drivers (relies on OS) and the OS (Win 10 in my case) says there are at least 3 ways to access settings on a webcam but in reality, without a special piece of software, there are absolutely none (no, I don't want to take pictures with the Microsoft Camera App, thank you sigh...) I was relieved to see that the camera I received does not mirror the image (maybe I got a different firmware?) Other complaints revolve around fraudulent resolution claims. I tested it with webcamtests.com and it is a true 2.07Mp sensor so res is FHD 1920x1080. Again, maybe some got clones / copies with cheaper CMOS sensors (nothing unusual here) but mine looks HD (even compared visually with my Logi c930c). Fps tests were also positive, clean sustained 30fps. In a real live scenario, it was able to handle constant streaming at about 20fps which is very decent in my experience. The only negative as I see so far is the horrible white balance mechanism, everything is indeed yellow/orange. My room has light blue walls, the cam shows a weird green/brown color. I get compliments on the quality of every call I'm a part of.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Rachael Houser", "review_title": "Doesn't have auto focus- it's manual- some might like- I do not", "review_text": "First Off let me say when they say wide view they mean it -- it is very wide-- too wide for my liking -but I imagine that is a pro for most so if that's what you want then this is your camera!

it stays nicely mounted at the top of my monitor, and it can be adjusted a lot, as far as how far down it points (particular useful if you need people watching to be able to see your whole body, including the feet). the image is nice and clear. i have only used the auto focus, not tried the manual focus yet, but it has been perfectly fine.
and man, the panoramic view thing is useful! most of my students use a more normal webcam, and they are constantly stepping out of the scree in just a step or two. i can move around a lot and still stay in view with this webcam.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Nicole", "review_title": "Best webcam we tested", "review_text": "Our office actually did a good test of five different webcams before settling on this to use for all of our employees.

[{"reviewer_name": "RAJENDER SINGH RATHEE", "review_title": "Versatile and easy to use", "review_text": "I’ve been using this for quick weeknight meals, and it cooks everything evenly. They added a new app option when timed venting is selected, so now you can choose the amount of time you want to vent the pot. It takes the guessing game out of using the timed venting feature. It's the addition I have been hoping for ever since they added timed venting to the app.
Updated 9/27/24: They just added a new notification feature to the app and I really like it. You get a push status notification when the pressure cooker starts preheating, then moves to the cooking cycle, then goes into venting mode and when it completes the venting cycle. It's particularly helpful to get notified when it goes into the venting process in case you want to precisely time the venting based on what you are cooking. It's a helpful enhancement.
Original review - I have an older model 6 QT Instant Pot Pro and I wanted this new one for its ability to connect to wifi, so I can use the app to control it. I especially like that the app has an extra venting option that is not available on the panel of the Instant Pot itself. It's a "Timed" option (see photo) that I actually discovered by accident when I was programming a cooking cycle. It's not explained anywhere in the documentation or even in the app, but it's very helpful when doing grains where I want it to natural release for a few minutes and then quickly finish the release without manual intervention. This is where the "Timed" option comes in. It seems to kick in about five to seven minutes after natural release starts. It varies, maybe based on how full the pot is, but since there's no documentation, it's just a guess on my part. It works great because I can be anywhere in the house and not have to rush to my kitchen to manually change the venting to quick release. I really love being able to monitor the progress from my iPhone and see when it has finished whatever cycle I've chosen.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "GeauxBucks!", "review_title": "Techies like us, love having Bluetooth accessibility! Great InstantPot!", "review_text": "Our original InstantPot just "bit the dust." We LOVED having it and it produced many, many wonderful memories meals for us.

After reading all of the reviews and articles on this particular model, I told my wife 'PLEASE, PLEASE get me this one for Christmas!" She said, you can go ahead and order it but you're not allowed to open it until Christmas! Like anyone, I said YES!!!!
I opened it and then downloaded the app being that it is Bluetooth compatible. I cannot tell you enough, what a pleasant surprise it was, to see just how easy it was to set up and connect via our home WiFi. I can now use the app to set the time, the release time, etc. It's amazingly friendly to use and works great. One thing I will tell you is that if you, like me, use the Saute' mode, to first brown meat, you can NOT start hte InstantPot in this mode via the app. You must physically hit the start button in order to have the Saute' mode come on. Yes, you can set it up in the app but cannot physically start the InstantPot in this particular mode. I know I"m repating myself but I want to make sure that everyone understands this. To me, it's a safety feature and I can appreciate why it's done this way. The last thing you want to do is to accidently have your InstantPot start in this mode while you're away or remote.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "St8kout", "review_title": "So far it's pretty great", "review_text": "There are a ton of youtube videos, showing you not only how to use it but how to make one pot dinners.
It's easy to use, wifi is easy to set up which afterwards connects whether you are using the app or not, to show remaining cooking time. I only have basic cooking skills, so I prefer to watch the youtube videos for recipes than the app for now.
Food prep always takes the longest, but once you have everything ready, put the food in, close the lid, set the time and wait for it to finish.
When you set a time according to a recipe, that is the actual Pressure Cooking time. The unit has to preheat before Pressure Cooking time begins, and that's several minutes depending on the model. Then the unit has to vent the pressure (choice of Natural, Pulse, or Quick Vent.) Be careful with Quick Vent as it may make some meats tougher than if you simply waited for the Natural vent process.
If you enable push notifications, it will tell you when preheating has ended and cooking has begun, and of course when cooking has ended and venting has begun (you'll likely hear the venting process from the next room.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "sgopal2", "review_title": "Better Features than Older Models - But Several Important Differences", "review_text": "This is my second instant pot. Not a deal breaker for me, but you should be aware of it.
3) Steam valve: this works a bit differently than other models. No way to manually vent or release steam. It has to be done through the control panel. It is possible to change the setting mid-stream, but there is a delay of a few seconds once you input on the control panel.

But the first time I tried it in my IP Pro Plus, the pin got stuck, and the lid locked closed. I couldn't open it because the pin needed room to clear. I managed to figure a way out to open it by turning the pot upside down. But this new IP seems to have a slightly lower clearance. So you'll have to use a shorter trivet, or a shorter PIP. Otherwise your lid may get stuck in locked mode.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Amazon Customer", "review_title": "Connectivity problems at first but resolved now and great product", "review_text": "What’s the point of having this fancy model if I can’t download and use the app with it?! Benefits:
1. Handles on the inner pot. This keeps the pot from spinning during saute mode and makes it easier and safer to remove the pot when it's full of food. I can do this even after a wrist injury.
2. Flat bottom on the pot. Makes any added oils spread evenly instead of running to the edge and enables #3 below.

Easy to clean too which my other AF is not.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "At Our Home We Think", "review_title": "What was I thinking?!", "review_text": "What was I thinking, taking so long to get this!!?

pot roast with carrots and potatoes. Prep time was a whole 15 minutes. That
was just to get the veggies ready. Then we seared the pot roast in the Instant
Pot. Super easy! The searing isn't something everyone does, so that's a good
part of the prep time. Then the cook time was 40 minutes. That's it!! Dinner time!
I will say, you don't smell the food cooking. That may be a plus or a minus, depending
on how you're wired. I have fibromyalgia. Smells of foods cooking are NOT my friend.
So not smelling the food until right before eating was a real blessing for me! Now, to
the roast. It was so tender, we were able to cut it with a fork, and it was incredibly juicy!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Mark Hastings", "review_title": "Glad I bought it.", "review_text": "I decided to cheap out and bought one of these from the Amazon Warehouse. This is a great piece of cookware, that is capable of many cooking techniques. I am happy with my purchase and would buy it again. It is relatively easy to program but you have to remember to press the Start button. (Something I forgot to do a few times.)
Saute - seems a little slow to get up to full temperature compared to stove top cooking, but it get there. The indicator is helpful to give you some idea of the current temp.
Pressure - works well. Lid is easy to place. One feature that seems small, but I REALLY love is the little "lid" on the top that you can remove to open a spot to place ice. This feature is wonderful as it allows you to quickly cool the pressure cooker and eliminate the need to do a pressure release and blow steam all over your kitchen. In practice, I have found that a handful if ice will drop the pressure in under 3 minutes.
Air Fry - this is a really nice feature to "finish" roasts. Pretty much a must have feature. However, this is also true of most air fryers unless they have a tumble basket.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Michael R Herl", "review_title": "Good All Purpose Multi Functional cooker", "review_text": "Had to replace my all in One Ninja Pressure and Air Fryer combo unit. Only issue is quick release is metal so need something to push it down., use wooden spoon. Appearance is nice in its metallic modern look", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Katie", "review_title": "So far so good!", "review_text": "I love my old instant pot, so when I was looking for a new one and saw that the version with the air fryer lid I was sold (after reading some reviews to make sure it wasn't terrible lol). Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Lisa C", "review_title": "Affordable and effective for dust and allergens", "review_text": "We moved into an incredibly dusty townhouse, I have terrible allergies, and we discovered our neighbors are chain smokers. We now have 3 Levoit air purifiers in our home: Vital 100 (non-smart version), Core Mini and Vital 200S.
I initially bought the Vital 100 and put it in our bedroom because I have terrible allergies. It collected a ton of dust and helped a lot with the allergies. I thought I didn't need the smart version but in hindsight the availability of specialty filters and the remote control would be very helpful. It's relatively quiet although on high it's too noisy for me to sleep with. I absolutely love that you can turn the all the control lights off. We tried using this for the cigarette smell but it wasn't very effective except when the smell was very light. It did completely abolish cooking smells though. If I could go back in time I would have ordered the 100S instead but this one works fine.
The smoke smell from the neighbors comes into our house through the laundry room which is a very small room. I bought the Core Mini to try to combat it. The Core Mini doesn't really do much to get rid of smells and was definitely overwhelmed by the smoke so now we move it around the house now when the pollen level is high. It works ok for dust and allergens but the range isn't great; you need to be right next to it to notice a difference. On low and medium speed it's barely audible and high is relatively quiet but overall the fan isn't very powerful. The lights on this one automatically turn off after a few seconds making it bedroom friendly. If I could do it again, I would have skipped this one and bought one of the larger ones sooner.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "RAERAE", "review_title": "Best Purchase All Year", "review_text": "I simply cannot say ENOUGH good things about this product! After 2 weeks of use the air feels lighter, I no longer wake up with a stuffy nose or junk in my lungs and I bought the pet specific air filters that are an added bonus. I LOVE the lighting features and that you can sync the device to my phone and set up schedules so it's quiet at night. The controls are SUPER easy to use and fool proof.
Just don't forget to open the base when you get it and take the plastic packaging off around the air filter!!! I forgot to do this and wondered why there was no air flow coming out of the top till I Googled it. 😂😂😂", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Robert Blackorbay", "review_title": "great replacement for my bedroom", "review_text": "I use this in a room I use to have an Ionic air purifier, the old worked there was some dust near the unit, but the smell of Ozone was too much since i kept my door closed most of the day. the Levoit was a perfect replacement, no smell, lot less noise and my room felt refreshed when i open the door. It still works well on the lowest setting to keep the room fresh so it's a good deal.
Setup was easy as can physically, however I cannot as yet speak to the application setup as I haven't gotten to that.
