All the modes do exactly as they say and the sleep mode is ultra quiet which is nice. I've been using this air purifier for almost 2 years now and it is still working great. You can immidetly tell when you take it out of the box that it is a good high quality purifier and not a purifier where they say its high quality and after a week it stops working... My last purifier was lmof a lower quality and stopped working with-in a year, but also I paid $50 for that one and I didn't have a dog at that time.
It is so nice to have a higher quality purifier that works exactly as it says on the ads. The app also includes other Levoit electronics you can add to your account so you have all your Lwvoit products in one spot on your phone which I think is so mice and easy. The app is also really easy to use and to set up everything on, it looks and feels very professional and easy which I really enjoy. I love opening up my app and seeing all my Levoit electronics in one spot, ready to turn on or off, or to change any mode it's on to something different. You can aslo set up a schedule of when you would like your devices to turn on and off and what mode to use whenbit does.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "KW", "review_title": "Surprisingly effective — glad I stuck with it", "review_text": "This was my first time ever using an air purifier, so I was pretty skeptical even after reading all the good reviews. The first few days were honestly a little discouraging because my bedroom still smelled kind of funky. I live in an older house, and getting certain smells out of the rooms has been a big priority while I finish setting everything up.
But after about a week, the difference became really noticeable. Now it’s actually refreshing to walk into my room. I’m really glad I didn’t give up on it early.
I also share my bedroom with a Husky, and there’s no dog smell anymore — which is huge. The fan is pretty quiet, and even when I turn it up, the sound is kind of soothing. It actually reminds me of the ocean waves from my trip to Ormond, FL, which is a nice little bonus.
The filters are easy to insert and remove (I haven’t had to replace mine yet, but I tested it out just to see), and the whole unit feels simple and user‑friendly.
Overall, very happy with this purifier. [{"reviewer_name": "Anja Miles", "review_title": "Cheaper than a filling & totally worth the investment after 9 months of use", "review_text": "My dental hygienist recommended this toothbrush about nine months ago. When I mentioned how expensive it was, she said, “It’s still cheaper than getting a filling.” That changed how I looked at the price, so I went for it.
The guided brushing app takes the guesswork out of whether I’m actually brushing everywhere. I used it twice a day in the beginning, which really helped me build better brushing habits. Nine months later, I don’t use the app every time anymore, but I still check in here and there to make sure I’m staying on track. The pressure sensor is also super helpful! My dentist mentioned that many people damage their gums and teeth by brushing too hard, and this makes it very obvious when you’re using too much pressure.
I’ve had two dental cleanings since switching, and both were probably the quickest I’ve ever had. My dentist and hygienist said everything looked great with very little cleaning needed and mentioned they commonly see this with patients using an Oral-B iO.
The brush heads indicate when they need replacing, which for me has been roughly every three months. They’re about $10 per replacement head, so that’s another ~$40 a year to factor into the cost. Not cheap, but reasonable enough for me considering how well the toothbrush has performed.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Brandon Sokolnik", "review_title": "Recommended for Traveling and At Home", "review_text": "I've had this now for nearly a year and it's been working well. The built in 2 minute timer with vibrations are great for knowing when to move on from the sections of the mouth. Wish the brush heads would last a little longer but they clean fairly well. I do keep my brush on the wireless charger all the time but I've been able to take it on trips without it running out of power, and I bring the travel case just incase but never had to use it. I would recommend this to get your brushing habits fixed if you have a hard time of sticking to the brushing schedule.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Amazon Customer", "review_title": "Buy this!", "review_text": "I'm new to electric toothbrush & it took me a minute to get use to this but once I did, I am very, very happy with it! That is the freshest my mouth & teeth feel. It's as if I'm coming out of the dentist every time (& that is a great feeling!). My teeth are WAY cleaner & even stains are nearly gone (I drink a lot of dark drinks). It'll stop/vibrate every 30 seconds to let you know to switch to another side of the mouth. I also love how it tells me if I'm pressing the brush to lightly or to hard on my teeth (the colors will tell you, green is good).
The spin is powerful & toothpaste will be slinging out. I always turn it off before I take it out of my mouth because it slings so much. I love the multiple settings you can choose but I always choose the sensitive option. It's not as strong as the daily clean option (daily clean was irritating my gums).

Main Purpose:
I purchased this toothbrush to maintain optimal dental health and minimize the need for extensive dental procedures.

The toothbrush is excellent, and you can even turn on the phone to track your performance. It offers awards for meeting specific goals, some of which can be challenging to achieve.

The Series 9 comes with additional sensors and a flat magnetic mount for convenient charging. While the battery drains quickly, it's not an issue for short 2-3 minute sessions.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Michael Smith", "review_title": "A baffling design flaw in a very expensive toothbrush", "review_text": "I bought the Oral-B iO Series 9 expecting a premium product. The toothbrush itself has a lot to recommend it, but the charging base has one of the worst design flaws I have encountered in a consumer product.
The iO9 is a relatively tall, expensive electronic device, yet while charging it essentially balances upright on a small, shallow magnetic base. There is no meaningful post, socket, collar, or other mechanical support to keep the handle from tipping sideways. Because the handle is so tall, it takes remarkably little lateral force to knock it off the charger.
This isn’t a hypothetical concern. I had a previous Oral-B toothbrush fall from its charger and break. With this one, I eventually stopped keeping it conveniently in the bathroom because I didn’t trust the charger to keep it secure. I actually improvised a second magnetic support against the handle when I kept it elsewhere, which dramatically improved its stability.
What makes this especially frustrating is that the problem is neither difficult to foresee nor difficult to solve. Competing electric toothbrushes use charging designs that mechanically locate and support the handle. Even a modest post, recess, collar, or other positive restraint could dramatically reduce the chance of an expensive toothbrush being knocked onto a hard bathroom floor.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Garrett & Shefali", "review_title": "If you need a brush like this it will be worth it", "review_text": "Loved this toothbrush, didn’t use the app. Just found it gave me the best cleaning and most options. Now for the downside: battery life. Oral-B advertises over two weeks of battery life with two 2-minute sessions per day, but in reality, that was not even close. [{"reviewer_name": "Jeff S.", "review_title": "Great budget smartwatch", "review_text": "After 17 years in the Apple ecosystem, I recently switched from an iPhone to a Samsung S26 Ultra so I needed a watch that worked with my new Android phone to replace my Apple Watch. I wasn't ready to throw down $300+ on a Galaxy Watch just yet so I looked for cheaper alternatives and that's when I found the Galaxy FIT 3. It does all of the major functions I need from a smart watch (time/date/temperature, fitness tracking, basic notifications, media playback controls). It comes with 100 different pre-set watch faces to customize your watch but they cannot be individually customized nor can any more be downloaded. The band is soft and comfortable (I'm not sure if there are many replacement bands to customize your FIT like are available for Apple Watches). The watch itself is much narrower vertically and lighter than my Apple Watch. I have to recharge it every 5-7 days (nowhere near the 14 day claimed battery life but much better than when I had to recharge my Apple Watch every day). It takes about 30 seconds per 1 percent to recharge the battery. The biggest downgrades from the Apple Watch or other higher end smartwatches is the smaller size of the display and its reduced scratch resistance (I've already gotten several small scratches on the watch face within the first month of use). Only mildly sucks because I use the live feed heart rate monitor to help clue me in to if I might have a panic attack or if I'm overreacting. Another thing. I have been using google health to track my calories and set specific goals for some of my macros I'm trying to hit. Unfortunately, the samsung health app doesn't get this specific and just gives you the suggested daily intake as a metric rather than letting you set your own. [{"reviewer_name": "drshmug", "review_title": "The only knives that you will need?", "review_text": "I have tried several Chinese made knives recently and only found one that was reasonably close to the quality of my 30 year old Henkel set. We’ve used the paring knife the most, so far and it’s great. When I say they come sharp, I’m not kidding, be very careful with them because they are easily as sharp as razor blades. The sharpening angle is very acute so I’m thinking the edges won’t last as long between sharpening as some more obtuse angles but will report back after I’ve sharpened them for the first time. The look reminds me of the Ikon series and they feel almost identical. You’d expect to pay much more for this set than this price, in my opinion. The butcher block is great quality wood and well made. It’s super heavy and compliments the white handles of the knives. The scissors are really nice because you can easily break them down into two pieces for sharpening. IF you have a sharpening system that you use for other knives, I have a feeling this is an heirloom quality set of knives. I only wish they came with more knives, specifically steak knives. Be sure to hand-wash these knives and not just throw them in the dishwasher. I’m less worried about the steel and more worried about incidental damage that can occur when mixed with other cutlery and utensils. Overall, I have zero hesitation when recommending this set to anyone that wants a really nice set of knives.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Gary Y", "review_title": "Quality is missing", "review_text": "Quality of the handles and the actual steel was not as good as expected. Overall, extremely pleased!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Sig", "review_title": "Decent", "review_text": "Knife snob here. These are plenty sharp and the tips are nicely pointy. Seen better but at this price point it's quite good.
These knives are pretty solid and stiff but do have some flex. I think some of the rigidty is coming from them being thick at the spine. I'm not a fan of the thickness; I'm more into Japanese style knives which tend to be thinner. These knives feel like hybrids, opting for narrower shapes but keeping the thick blades.
They did a good job with rounding off the edges, particularly at the bolster. The rivets could be more flush, but it's a comfortable gripping experience.
I think this makes for a good entry level "good knife" set. The criticism of sets in general is that they give you a bunch of pieces you don't need, but here at least these knives don't overlap in purpose terribly much, so it's a reasonable set.
At $250 they seem like good value for what they are. The question most will have is whether or not buying something more expensive will gain them anything more than brand recognition, and I'd say yes, it can be worth it to bump up if you're looking for better edge retention or the perfect weight balance for your preferences. But the gains wouldn't be much. Only in a professional setting would you likely be concerned with keeping an edge for so long between sharpening, so for home cooks these Cangshans seem fine.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "The Crow’s Nest", "review_title": "Great set of knives", "review_text": "I really don't understand why the same exact knife set but in black is only about $80 when this white set is about $250 (quick buy the black set before they raise the price!)

The gorgeous silky smooth wooden block is the star of the show - it looks & feels exquisite. The co-star for me is the scissors - great comfortable grips, sharp, work great and even have metal prongs sticking out the ends (for shucking, I think?) (but be careful per they are a little dangerous to have sticking up like that). There's a slight learning curve to remember to put the knives the right way with the block being slanted. The knives have a nice weight, really sharp, cut cleanly & with very little effort, easy to use, semi-comfortable handles but I wish the metal connectors & trim was completely flush with the other material (lessens the quality for me). They still work great & the whole set looks really nice on the counter. They are fairly easy to clean. Good quality construction & out of really strong good quality German steel. Hold an edge great but easy to sharpen. Good variety of styles & sizes of knives. All in all, great set - I recommend.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "UniversalPen", "review_title": "A stunning sharp, full-tang knife and scissor set", "review_text": "I don't know why, but the first thing I thought when I opened the box was, "Wow, that is one beautiful block of wood!" Okay, so what about the knives? They look amazing, feel really good in the hand, and are really sharp. Even the scissors are really sharp, which is something I've never seen before. The blades are nice and balanced in the hand, and I really love how my index finger rests on the bolster. I notice that the handle fasteners stick out slightly, and so you can feel them a little as you slide your hand across the tang. As high quality as these seem, that aspect cheapens them for me but doesn't take away from how much I love this set. Because these are full-tang knives, they are a lot more rigid and more reliable than other less expensive knives.
This is not a cheap set of knives, and they also aren't expensive. I think there is a lot of value in what you get, in that they look great, perform well, and will last a long time.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "JW", "review_title": "Very fine", "review_text": "The blades on this set of knives arrived very sharp-sharper than most new knives I’ve had. Title: Dalstrong 8-Pc Steak Knife Set, 5" - German HC Steel
Description: About this item                     FOR DINNER PARTIES AND LARGE TABLE SERVICE WHERE FOUR KNIVES ISN'T ENOUGH: Eight matched non-serrated steak knives cover a full dinner party table — no mismatched blades, no guests left with the dull knife from the back of the drawer. All eight blades are the same German HC steel, the same G10 handle, the same edge geometry. Consistency from the first guest to the last.     FOR THE BBQ HOST WHO SERVES THE WHOLE TABLE AT ONCE: Smoke a full brisket, carve it at the station, and send eight matched knives to the table with it — each one capable of slicing through bark, fat cap, and smoke ring in a clean single stroke. Non-serrated straight edges slice rather than saw; your guests' plates look like the cook they came from.     SHARPENABLE, NOT DISPOSABLE — THE CASE FOR NON-SERRATED AT SCALE: Eight serrated knives are eight knives you can't resharpen at home. Eight non-serrated straight edges sharpen back on the Dalstrong Whetstone Set (B07KKQHKMV) in a single session when they eventually dull. That's the practical math for a set you'll use for years.     FORGED GERMAN HC STEEL — THE SAME BUILD AS THE GLADIATOR CHEF LINE: High-carbon German steel at 56+ HRC, full-tang, triple-riveted G10 handles — the same construction commitment as the Gladiator ELITE chef knife, applied to eight steak knives. These aren't stamped filler blades; they're forged, balanced, and built to last a decade of weekly dinner use.     CUSTOMER SUPPORT, EIGHT INDIVIDUAL SHEATHS, GIFT-READY PACKAGING: Eight knives with individual protective sheaths in Dalstrong premium packaging — the set for housewarmings, wedding registries, and the host who takes the table seriously. Backed by Dalstrong's customer support on all eight.                 ›  See more product details

I was almost to the point of going back to film due to the drawbacks (slow shutter, quality of enlargements, limited versatility etc.) of my past digital cameras. As a customer I should be able to buy something and get what I paid for, if such item doesn't work 100% out of the box I should be able to get a new one and not have it sent for repair (then what is their quallity control good for?) - I barely found any issues with the Nikon brand, I found more praises that anything else. I also looked for a good and convinient bag for it and the best I found was the Mytho Swiss Gear (model GA-7865-02F00) that you can find for 49.00 bucks at your local electronics store. And as a last note, I love buying from Amazon, they have good prices and good customer service.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Harry W", "review_title": "Poor room light or High Fstop performance", "review_text": "My biggest problem with this camera is that in normal room light performance (without flash) is sub par, even worse than my Fuji A700 compact. The camera fails to freeze even the slightest motion without flash under normal room light. IT behaves better with 1/80s shutter spped at iso 1600 at normal room light (6, 65W floodlight bulbs in a 11x20 room).
But at iso 1600 and shutter speed 1/80, the picture quality is not acceptable, pretty dark and grainy. Surprsingly my compact Fuji A700 does a better job in the same light (it also beat canon sd1000 compact) in the same test.
I was hoping that I would get good normal light performance from a DSLR (espacially D60 with its good reviews) but I was wrong.
Pros: Good auto focussing, 3 points is more than enough for a normal user. Single point is even more predictable. Good shoe to shot time and flash recycle time.

Instead I went by then 4.5 star rating on this site & ended up wasting my money...", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Bluirv", "review_title": "Great Entry-Level DSLR Camera!", "review_text": "If you are used to a compact point-and-shoot and want to overcome the shortcomings of these cameras, then consider the Nikon D60.

In diesem Punkt ist die Nikon D5100 wie auch schon die D7000 (letztere in der Semiprofiliga) ein Schnäppchen.
Das Bedienkonzept ist, für Nikon-Verhältnisse, relativ menülastig. Das ist aber kein gravierender Nachteil, denn es lassen sich durch zweimaliges Drücken der "i"-Taste Zugriffe auf alle fotografisch relevanten Einstellungen ermöglichen. Auf dem scharfen Display werden auch, sehr einsteigerfreundlich, Tipps und Hinweise angezeigt bzw. technische Funktionen wie Blende und Verschlusszeit durch gelungene Symbolik nachvollziehbar dargestellt.
Wie bei Nikon üblich, ist die Kamera sehr reichhaltig ausgestattet. Neben reinen Konfigurationsmöglichkeiten kommt auch die kreative Fotografie nicht zu kurz. So ist z. B. auch eine Mehrfachbelichtungsfunktion verfügbar, bei der etwa zwei Aufnahmen zu einer verschmelzen. In Kombination mit dem klappbaren Monitor und den damit machbaren Perspektiven kann der Künstler sich hier voll austoben!
Was mir ebenfalls gut gefällt, ist die sehr ordentliche Verarbeitung der Kamera, welche subjektiv wertiger daherkommt als jene der "Plastikbomber" des großen Konkurrenten. Kunststoff ist in dieser Preis-Liga üblich, aber das bringt eben auch einen Gewichtsvorteil. ... et la sensibilité : incroyable ! pas de bruit, rendu excellent ! Donc idéal quand on évite le flash !
L'usage : facile à manier avec sa poignée, réglages faciles et en français (presque aussi pratique que les réglages des Lumix de chez Pana !...). Quant aux préréglages et options possibles, ils sont plus nombreux que nécessaire.
L'écran pivotant dans toutes les directions, robuste comme on dit, permet de photographier sous tous les angles.
Je l'ai depuis un an, je fais les réglages manuels et suis très content de cet appareil. Je regrette seulement de n'avoir pas pris un objectif 18 - 105, car le zoom est un peu limite sur ce modèle.

It has been an absolute refreshing change to receive prompt responses to problems, to answer questions on the phone and provide an excellent after sales care, to the point i've even bought a book for the D5100 and another lens of them. I have absolutely no affiliation with the company, in fact i don't think i could further away from them. I would recommend them to anyone wanting camera equipment on here 100%

Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Ken", "review_title": "Why buy a Canon 50D?", "review_text": "I've used Canon equipment and other brands, but Canon has always been my favorite, since the mid 60's. And I was an early adopter for the switch to digital, although I stuck with film for my serious work until the pixel count got high enough for a decent 5 X 7. Then I put away my film camera for good.
I upgraded my camera frequently until I got the Canon 20D. I stuck with the 20D until now. The 30D and 40D just didn't add enough in features or pixel count to entice me. But the 50D tipped the scale and I again upgraded. And I'm glad that I did. It's a great camera, worth the asking price.
What's so great about it? Simple, features and pixels. You can read all of the technical stuff elsewhere, but the automatic modes and the program modes just work. Yes, I know all about depth of field and manual controls from the days when that all that there was, if you wanted good pictures. But nothing beats the landscape, portrait, or macro settings on a Canon camera. If you want a portrait, set the dial. The camera sets the depth of field properly and you can concentrate on your subject, not the camera. Same goes for the other auto modes. The camera balances every setting in the same way that I used to do it. So why not let the camera do the work? I really tough situations, I will switch to the program mode to gain a little more control, but that's not often.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Ceit", "review_title": "Great Camera for the price and features!", "review_text": "I just received my new Canon 50D. I have to say that I am in love with this camera, no, it's not perfect. I would have loved to see a full frame CMOS sensor, but I can't have everything and price too! I find the images to be crisp and clear and the operation easy to use. I have shot over 300 pictures with this camera so far and I am very happy with the quality of images, especially at the high ISOs. I also gave it to a novice photographer to use on Thanksgiving and they loved it as well and had no problem operating the camera
A couple of nitpicks - First, on the new CA mode, I completely understand the need for this setting, there are many people picking up these cameras who have never used an SLR before and don't understand aperture or shutter speed. However, this feature is only as good as the lens. If someone is using a lens that doesn't have an aperture of 2.8 or 1.4 then they won't get the background to be too blurred. Second, the exposure compensation is now on the rear dial, this is more a preference and I will most likely get use to it, in time :).
ETA: Another thing that would have been nice is a video setting like the 5D and the Nikon D90. But again, you can't have everything.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "dinub1", "review_title": "Dinu", "review_text": "I moved to this camera body from a Canon EOS 10D model 2003. That camera served me very well throughout the years, but it had some limitations.
In all aspects this new EOS 50D camera seriously outperforms the other camera on a large margin.
As a sign of excellently built and sturdiness, this camera with a Tokina 12-24 ATX Pro zoom lens and a Speedlight EX-430 flash attached, recently fell on the wood floor of my house, from my tripod. Tripod was faulty and the head separated from the tripod body. I was horrified. To my amazement, nothing happened. I do not know how lucky I was, but I won't ever play with my luck again. I bought a new tripod since.
LCD display: 3" diagonal, bright, high res. LCD display, easily viewable indoors and out, a pleasure to use, compared to the small 1.8" diagonal LCD display of the EOS 10D.
Exposure meter: much more accurate, compared to the older camera. Canon cameras, over the years typically underexposed, when a wide angle lens was used. This one seems to have overcome that issue. Extremely accurate exposures on evaluative metering, with or without flash.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Bill Latta", "review_title": "CANON EOS 50D CAMERA", "review_text": "After owing a Canon EOS 10D camera, which was damaged while traversing a mountain stream during a photo shoot, I wanted to continue with a like-kind Canon replacement. The EOS 50D was just released in October. I purchased it and have been using it for one month now. The 50D is just like my now retired 10D but with a few upgrades.
One significant upgrade is the larger LCD display. It is crisp and sharp and easy to review images captured. While I do like the larger LCD display, there is a downside to the larger LCD display. I have found that my face inevitably touches the LCD display while looking through the viewfinder. This almost always leaves facial marks (oils) much like fingerprints all over the left side of the LCD display. I now find I must keep at-the-ready a soft, clean cloth to wipe it clean to review images clearly. While this is not necessarily a hardware issue, it is becoming somewhat of a major annoyance--especially when on a fast-paced photo shoot. Of course, unless one is as particular about a clean LCD display as I am, it might not be an annoyance. Perhaps Canon could consider moving the LCD display to the right side vs the left in later models.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Vikki M.", "review_title": "Wow! Very happy with this camera!", "review_text": "I wanted to move up from my Canon Rebel t3 which I have been using since 2012. The high end Canons are beyond my budget. I stumbled upon this Canon 50D while I was browsing cameras here on Amazon. Yes it is discontinued by the manufacturer, yes it is older than my Rebel t3. The price was right so I thought I would take a chance on this camera. The listing described it as "very good". Excellent describes the condition of this camera more appropriately. I can find no scratch, smudge, ding, dent, wear and tear etc anywhere on this camera body. It came securely packaged and was delivered on time. In the box was the camera body, a battery and the battery charger. The charger and battery appear to be brand new also. The battery must have had a partial charge as it was fully charged within 20 minutes. A user's manual is not included with this package, but, having used the t3, I was able to make my way around it quite easily. I am told that manuals for all models can be downloaded from the Canon web site and I will eventually get the manual this way. I have a small collection of Canon, Sigma and Tamron lenses and they all work with this camera body. I live in NE Ohio and sun is a rarity here this time of year. I couldn't wait to try this camera out and, despite getting hit with winter storm "Harper" this weekend and being house-bound due to the weather, I decided to spend the time getting acquainted with this camera. These pictures (with the exception of the 2nd) were taken through a not so clean window at 3pm during the winter storm with gray light and falling snow. The camera seemed to focus quickly, shutter is fairly quiet compared to my t3. I used a Sigma 150-600mm sport lens with shutter speeds of 1/630 - 1/1250. My USB cord from my t3 worked just fine for this 50D . Pictures transfered effortlessly when I connected the 50D to my computer. Photos edited very slightly in Lightroom for crop and brightness. I mainly photograph birds/wildlife. Very happy with this camera and highly recommend this seller.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Aurora Michelle", "review_title": "Better Than I Thought It would Be", "review_text": "This is my first Canon SLR in a very long while, and was unsure of the move from Nikon, but decided to check it out. Overall this is a nice camera. Noise level is indeed more than Nikon, my old D90 did some beautiful shots at high ISO where the 50D strugles. I would not go any higher than ISO 800 or so with this camera. Thing is I never do, so this is fine for me, but might be a problem for some.
The button layout I would say could use some work. Nikon I would give a major advantage here as all there buttons are easy to get to and navigate, where the Canon I have to look and fumble around to find even the basic stuff. I admit allot of this has to do with me needing to needing to know the camera better and will improve over time, but the D90 I picked up in like 20 min of using. Don't get me wrong, I don't think Canon's is bad, but could use some more work is all.
The camera is fast and starts up almost before I know I want to turn it on. (almost)Though I do feel Canon do need to add more AF points the nine it has seems to do the job well, even when following moving objects it keeps right up with it without a hint of wanting to slow down. Just make sure your memory card can keep up with this camera when your shutter is on auto fire. Like some reviews have stated, I have noticed the tracking does tend to want to go to brighter areas in the frame. This has not been a big issue with me, but is something you might want to watch for.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jonathan Acierto", "review_title": "Big Step Up", "review_text": "I started a photography business and I've been using my Canon Rebel T1i for the past year. It's been a great camera and I love it, but now that I'm starting to do more weddings, I needed a more semi-professional camera to keep up with the pace and strain of your average wedding. I had been looking to get the 50D for some time and after I was paid for a wedding and the 60D was announced (looks like Canon is making the XXD line more consumer oriented), I knew it was time to get the 50D.
Having come from using the T1i, the first thing I had to get used to was all the buttons. Seriously, there are more buttons on the 50D because parameters like meter, white balance, etc. have their own button rather than having to go through menus like on the T1i. But this makes adjustments much faster, since there are less menus to dig into. And the adjustment wheel on the back of the camera is awesome, again because it makes adjustments quick. I no longer have to press a button to adjust exposure compensation, I can just use the wheel on the back.
The camera is also quieter than the T1i. Shutter and mirror noise from the 50D are noticeably quieter than the T1i. This will help greatly with the weddings I'll be shooting and with more photojournalistic shoots.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Scholtz Life", "review_title": "Very Happy with My 50D's IQ :)", "review_text": "There are already a lot of detailed reviews about the 50D. With that in mind I'll keep this brief. My background: I'm an amature with a lot of SLR experience. I started taking photography classes in high school...back when there were only film SLRs!. Photojournalism was also my major for one year in college. And since it's been an on and off hobby of mine. I have a Canon SD 700 IS but this 50D was my first DSLR.
Maybe it's because I work long hours and I'm not outside during the day, but most of my 50D photos so far have been in the late afternoon or evenings, or indoors. As such I've used ISO 1600 quite a bit. The images to my eye look fantastic! Within the menu system there are High ISO Noise Reduction and Long Exposure Noise Reduection options that can be turned on/off as needed.
If one is to compare image quality of the 50D to the 40D, I think it's interesting to remember the 50D takes larger, higher resolution images. In other words, the 50D images start out with more detail. And from the research I did it appears the 50D's images can be sharpened and still have more detail than the 40D. There are good explanations of this on the web. Amazon censored out the article links I included but if you contact me I'd be happy to provide them.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Miguel C.", "review_title": "Great value!", "review_text": "Great condition! Works perfectly. Already taken many pictures with it on our vacation and continue to use it as my primary photo taker.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Stuart Waters", "review_title": "Arrived in immaculate condition", "review_text": "The D50 arrived promptly and in perfect condition, this was due to the marvellous packaging, it looked as if it could have gone through the most clumsy carrier!
I like this Camera because it is a Canon. My last Camera was a Canon D30 which lasted 24 years! Also it is a lot more advanced than the old one.The controls are similar, it just has a few more whistles and bells which I find most useful", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Anon", "review_title": "Used product works as described", "review_text": "Product was as described.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Michael Colvin", "review_title": "Buyer beware…", "review_text": "The camera I purchased was very inexpensive. [{"reviewer_name": "Chris & Lindsey", "review_title": "A Meaningful Upgrade From the Nikon D3400", "review_text": "I upgraded to the Nikon D7500 from a D3400, and it has served me extremely well. The D3400 was a good camera to learn on, but the D7500 provides much more control without requiring me to constantly enter the menus. The additional buttons, front and rear command dials, top display, and customizable settings make it much quicker to adjust while shooting.
I primarily use it for aquarium, wildlife, and nature photography. Its autofocus and continuous shooting perform especially well when photographing fast-moving fish, while the image quality gives me plenty to work with when editing RAW files. The camera feels solid and comfortable in the hand, and the tilting touchscreen is helpful when shooting from lower or more difficult angles.
There is a learning curve when moving up from an entry-level camera, but the added control and flexibility are worth taking the time to learn. It has allowed me to grow as a photographer without feeling like I’ve quickly outgrown the camera. Overall, the D7500 has been a reliable and capable upgrade that I’m very happy with.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Mrskelly17", "review_title": "Amazing camera — huge upgrade for me", "review_text": "I absolutely love this camera. The Nikon D7500 has been an amazing upgrade and the image quality is incredible. The photos come out sharp, detailed, and the colors look great straight out of the camera.
It has a lot of features and settings, but once you get familiar with it, it’s very powerful and easy to customize. The autofocus is fast and it handles action really well, which is great for sports photography.
Overall I’m extremely happy with this purchase. If you’re looking for a high-quality DSLR that performs really well for both photos and action shots, this camera is a fantastic option.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jill Anderson", "review_title": "Great Camera!", "review_text": "Camera is exactly as described, the images are crisp and clear. I bought it to go with my 500mm lens and I love it! It focuses fast and crisp, I took a photo of a bird behind some branches and it focused on the bird instead of the branches which my D3500 could not do. I'm very pleased with this purchase.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "ecforman", "review_title": "Meets my needs", "review_text": "Before I start, these are simply my own impressions. I was once a professional photographer way back in the days of film and photographed over 600 weddings, as well as sports teams and schools. Nowadays I am just an amateur who sells prints once in awhile. I am also a recently retired economics teacher and in my quest to upgrade from my excellent, but outdated D7000, I applied the principles of wants vs needs, trade-offs, opportunity costs, and cost benefits.
Realizing the no camera will give one exactly what they want, I narrowed the requirements down. My two main criteria were higher ISO performance and more accurate focus. I do a lot of bird in flight, and both are essential. It came down to the D7200, the D7500, and the D500. The D7200 already being two years out, I ruled it out. The D500 fit my needs, and a few wants, but the price tag was a bit steep. The D7500 seemed the best fit, and after trying it for a couple of days I believe I made the right choice.
ISO- While the D7000 had an upper limit of ISO 1600 before degrading, I now feel quite comfortable at 3200 which helps with the 180 f/2.8 for birds. I will test at higher when I do some Milky Way shots next week.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "nic", "review_title": "Awesome", "review_text": "This camera is so great! At first seeing the low price thought it was used or refurb but no it’s actually new in box. All box accessories came with it. The camera itself has lots of features and takes amazing pictures. I highly recommend getting this if you can get new for the price I paid. If anything changes I’ll edit this", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "dewlap", "review_title": "Great camera for the price", "review_text": "This is a great camera! I was hoping to buy a more expensive Nikon model, but due to a job loss, was unable to do so. After reading a lot of reviews about the D7500, I was convinced that this camera would meet my needs. So far I am loving it!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "D. Bank", "review_title": "Far improved over the D7100", "review_text": "Just a short review, more of a user experience. I bought the D7500 for a month long trip to Europe. I was replacing a D7100 that had some nagging problems that often left me less than satisfied (It had been dropped - and repaired - early in its life, but was never as good as I expected). Anyway, I filled 4-5 64 Gig memory cards on the trip, and I have to say that this camera is far better than my old one. The low light abilities are awesome, and on the few instances where I needed to take a picture hand held in low light with some depth of field, ISO 16000 was a very viable option. Not noise free, but better than ISO 6400 on the older camera. Other features that made the user experience better: I could easily transfer pictures to my phone - very important to my wife and convenient for sharing or posting to Facebook when traveling without a computer. The connection to the phone also meant that I could share the phone's GPS with the camera and therefore get location tags on every photo. This worked very well, though it is possible that it negatively affects the phone's battery - but my phone is old and it is hard to really tell. (I think the automatic download was more detrimental to the phone battery, and it took a little searching to figure out how to turn off automatic downloads for every photo). As for the camera battery, it was also good, though again, the automatic download seemed to affect it a lot, as did a lot of activity on the display. The tilting screen was useful to have, but not as useful as a fully articulating screen (like the D5300). The touch screen was awesome, and made it VERY easy to check critical focus and work with the menu - even with gloves on. I was in a cold weather environment, so I had gloves on much of the time. These gloves had something on each finger that would let it work with an iPhone, and therefore it worked just as well with he camera. I liked the feature where you could use the live preview and touch the screen where you wanted it to be in focus, and it would refocus and take the shot.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "David W. Ranck", "review_title": "D7500 - A great step up from D3400, D5600", "review_text": "I've only had this camera for less than a day and have taken about a dozen keepers. The build quality is outstanding compared to the D3400. The D7500 I believe, will fill the role as an enthusiast camera. Not quite up to its big brother the D500, but at least in the ways that really matter to me it is spot on. BTW, I gave 4 stars for battery life but that is based on what I've read. I haven't had enough experience with the camera to have my own opinion. Also keep in mind that picture quality is a function of the photographer and the lens even more than the camera IMHO.
The first big difference to me over the D3400 is the focusing system. I haven't had a chance to use it track birds but the 51 focus points and the 3D and group modes seem to work well in simple tests. We'll see how they perform for me in real world scenarios like tracking a bird. Regardless the focusing system is much better than the D3400. Another important feature for me is the ability to shoot at 8 frames / second and up to 50 RAW photos before the buffer fills up.
I love the touchscreen display and the fact that it articulates up and down. I do wish it moved further down for taking overhead shots, but it will work fine. Being able to use the touch screen for menus and photo review is a real plus. "My Menu" is a great time saver. [{"reviewer_name": "T. Haight", "review_title": "Perfect for the evolving enthusiast...it is ok to leave your D3200 behind and upgrade!", "review_text": "I purchased this a few days ago here on Amazon. I brought a slightly used one with just over 3,000 shutter actuation's. Saved a LOT of money. I came from the delightful rank-beginner D3200 camera to this upgrade. Here are my thoughts after 2 years of shooting with a D3200 and upgrading to the D5300:
1. Stellar upgrade in sharpness! Without a doubt, the most noticeable thing. 39 autofocus points over the 11 on D3200 really helps! That irritating OLPF is gone! I use a 37" monitor to develop in Lightroom, and pixel peeping on the D5300 is a delightful experience. My friend who owns a D7200 thinks the image quality is identical. It is close, my friends. Too close to call.
2. Smaller and lighter than D3200, but still substantial enough in the hand. Anyone with slightly smaller hands will really enjoy this camera. Me? I am 6 4" with big hands, and it still felt just great. No issues there as far as I can see.
3. Your EN-EL-14 batteries will work in it. The D5300 is recommended and comes with EN-EL-14a. Battery life is just fine. To make a guestimate from the 150+ images shot and no budge on the battery meter...500-600 may just be possible without heavy flash use. I should not admit this, but even an aftermarket battery I used in my D3200 for 2 years works perfect in my D5300. Loving the auto barista feature! 10/10", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Ody A González", "review_title": "Súper bien", "review_text": "Me encanta todo de este equipo", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jimmy", "review_title": "Amazing espresso machine!", "review_text": "I'm going to preface this by saying I am no coffee expert and I don't drink coffee that often. This is my first ever espresso machine from Ninja, but it is not my first coffee machine from Ninja. My experience with this machine has been amazing! It takes the guess work out of making espresso drinks completely. All you have to do is add your favorite beans and press some buttons and you'll have a drink in no time. The machine will grind the beans for you and suggest a ground size based on the settings you pick. It'll also calibrate the recommendation based off of your beans. To do this, you do 2 calibration cycles with the grinder first. After that, it'll be locked in. It'll grind out about 18.5g of coffee for the double espresso attachment. You can manually set the strength and temperature. The strength will change the recommended size of the coffee grounds and also the amount of liquid you get out. They provide you with a book that has all of the recommendations based on the roast you buy. After it grinds the beans, you just tamper it with the provided tamper and then lock it into the brewing portion of the machine. Then you press the start brew button and let it do its thing. You'll have fresh espresso in a few seconds! There is also an attachment called luxe for coffee and triple shots. This machine can make coffee and espresso. This thing also comes with an auto-frother. You just put milk in and set it to the right type of milk (plant or regular), your froth level, and then press a button and it'll automatically do the frothing for you. I find that it works really well for latte art! Setting up the machine was super easy. You just have to measure the hardness of your water first with the provide test strips. This is just so your machine will remind you when you need to descale it. This machine is very quiet. It isn't that loud at all. It looks sleek and amazing. It is smaller than the original version and takes up less counter space. It only feels a little bit cramped because you can't froth and make espresso at the same time. This isn't a big deal though. The frother also has a manual option if you would rather do that. I can steam milk as well. This machine is pricey, but I think it is worth it for the price if you want fresh espresso without having to worry too much about thinking. This machine does it all. Overall, I would recommend this machine! It's also super easy to clean. The water tank in the back comes out, the bean hopper comes out, the grinder comes out. The frother purges itself after you're done. The waste water base comes out to pour out easily. You just gotta wipe down the frother with a towel after using it. You can also wipe the area that comes into contact with the portafilter afterwards. There is also a thing that pops up to bring your cup up higher if it is too short. Definitely a 5/5 machine.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "James Dangelo", "review_title": "Good Espresso; Poor Regular Coffee", "review_text": "Makes a very good espresso pour, but regular coffee not so good. I'll leave the review as-is below, but I've got an update to add at the top here: The water tank is easy to break, and near-impossible to replace. Compared to my other machines (and I've been through a few) the water tank plastic is thin. I had the tank sitting empty on the counter while I cleaned some stuff, and knocked it from the counter to the floor... and that shattered the tank. The company currently has no supply of spare tanks. Assuming costs are similar to other, similar machines from Ninja, this will be an expensive replacement as well. So be super careful with the tanks - the plastic is just... not durable compared to others on the market.

I start every day with an espresso, and I've gone pretty far down the rabbit hole with Gagguinio. [{"reviewer_name": "Mike S", "review_title": "Love it! However.......", "review_text": "I bought this coffeemaker because I was looking for a insulated carafe with a cone filter. Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Dorothy F.", "review_title": "Makes Hot coffee", "review_text": "I bought this exact coffee maker about 3 months ago and I haven’t had any issues or problems with it so I decided to get a second one for my vacation home. The coffee maker is compact and looks nice on my counter. The instruction manual has straightforward step by step instructions for first time use and for normal coffee brewing. However, there are a couple of things in the instruction manual that I disagree with. First, it says “the appliance can be used by children 8 years old and above if they’ve been given supervision or instruction.” I can’t imagine letting my 8 year old grandson use my coffee maker or why I would want him to. Also, it says you should unplug and thoroughly clean all parts of the coffee maker daily. That’s probably a good thing to do but I have only been cleaning mine periodically. And for clarification, #3 under Normal Brewing says to use one level spoon of coffee for each cup. This should say one level Tablespoon for each cup of coffee. Other than those things I found the instruction manual to be helpful and clear.
The coffee maker has all the common features found in coffee makers. It can be programmed to go on automatically at a specified time which is convenient for people who work or are in a hurry in the morning. We tried this function and it was easy to do, however, since we are retired we like to prepare the coffee the night before but then press the on/off button when we get up in the morning. The coffee maker has a pause and serve function so you can grab a cup of coffee before the brewing stops. It also has an automatic shut off that turns the coffee maker off two hours after it was turned on. I find this feature to be very important because I often forget to turn it off. There are two other features on this coffee pot that I really like. First, it has a button to make the coffee a little stronger. You just press the “strength” button and a little coffee bean symbol shows up under the time. This slows down the drip and gives the coffee a bolder flavor without making it bitter or too strong. With this, I can just top it up and make it hot again. So luxurious and timesaving.
Love the rich setting for making it stronger. Puts hair on your chest, like I need any more of that. LoL.
Love that it stops dripping while you pour a cup! That feature is to die for, because sometimes you really need that first cup, and it's not done brewing, so you make a mess. Not now.

I love the grey color.
What i dont like:", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "William", "review_title": "Best Cup of Coffee", "review_text": "I upgraded my previous Keurig coffee maker that I bought in 2013. It was worth the upgrade.

Title: Ninja Luxe Café Premier 3-in-1 Espresso Machine, Drip Coffee, & Cold Brew
Description: About this item                     BE YOUR OWN BARISTA: Café-quality espresso shouldn't require a PhD. HANDS-FREE FROTHING: Dual Froth System combines a spinning whisk with automatic steamer to produce perfect, silky-smooth microfaom every time. COFFEE MAKER WITH GRINDER: A built-in conical burr grinder features 25 settings for precise, versatile grinding based on your specific drink. SMART TECHNOLOGY: This coffee and espresso combo machine features Barista Assist Technology that guides you every step of the way, from automatic precision grinding to weight-based dosing, assisted tamping for the perfectly pressed puck, and active real-time temperature and pressure adjustments based on your selected drink. [{"reviewer_name": "J. Nichols", "review_title": "Starbucks has lost my business", "review_text": "⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Starbucks has officially lost my business
I am happy to report that I am now a former customer of Starbucks — and honestly, pretty much every other drive-thru coffee place — after buying the Ninja Luxe.
First things first: there IS a learning curve. This is not a “push one button and magically become a barista” machine. You’ll want to do a little homework. Research your beans, watch a few videos, and plan on grabbing a few extras like an espresso glass/cup, microfiber cloths for wiping down the milk wand, a knock box, and obviously some syrups because we are not animals.
You also have to maintain and clean the machine. Again, this isn’t a Keurig situation. BUT it simplifies the espresso-making process enough that you can make genuinely good coffee at home without needing to enroll in barista school.
It took me about three days to really dial in my preferred drink, and once I did, I haven’t looked back.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Mixeddestinations", "review_title": ""This One Earned Its Spot."", "review_text": "My wife had always wanted an espresso machine without spending a fortune. The night she ordered this one, she could barely sleep. When it finally arrived, her excitement was through the roof.
We've been using it regularly since it was delivered on May 29, and it has exceeded our expectations.
The reality is that this is an excellent product at a reasonable price. There isn't a single part that feels cheap or flimsy. The machine feels sturdy, well-built, and refined, and it looks great sitting on our coffee bar.
I think the stainless-steel finish is a great neutral color that fits into almost any kitchen. If you're looking for something a little different, Ninja offers other color options on their website. You can certainly spend more on a higher-end model, but for our family, this machine has everything we need.
If you're looking for Starbucks-level speed every morning, it's capable of delivering that. However, I'd encourage you to slow down and enjoy the process. There's something incredibly satisfying about crafting your own coffee and producing a drink that feels café quality from the comfort of your home.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Unsettled", "review_title": "Truly an all-in-one machine", "review_text": "I love this machine! I will note that mounting the handle can be pretty tight at first but it does loosen with use. The grinder is a great addition and am very happy it is truly an all-in-one machine. I have had mine for two months without any issues.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jason Lheureux", "review_title": "Fantastic for casual use. Not for hot rods.", "review_text": "I’ve owned this machine for about 8 months and I am comparing this to my Breville Barista. It’s a great device, if you’re getting it for the right reason.
I have this one in my office at work and it’s a fantastic machine. Fast, easy to use, minimal clean-up, no fuss. It does the thing. Easy to follow steps leading to fast and delicious beverages. If you are looking for something fool-proof with a variety of drink options this is absolutely for you. An average achieving 4th grader can set up and run this machine. You will not go back and you will save sooo much money in the long run getting yourself un-addicted to $7 lattes.
If you are looking to tinker, tune, hot-rod or slap on a bunch of aftermarket parts, this isn’t the device for you. Go for a more traditional machine. This machine works best when you run it as is and let it do its thing. It doesn’t even have enough clearance for most puck screens, and I think it throws off its calibration. The wastewater tray is also pretty small. I empty it much more than I do on my Breville. You can make a variety of drinks in this and many are great (cold press works well) but some are more gimmicky. Regular brew coffee doesn’t taste great. Also it’s harder to use this as a dedicated on demand hot water source for tea and such. It doesn’t have a dedicated spigot for hot water. Lastly the water frothing feature is awesome, but for some reason the steam wand (which has restrictive movement and you must use the stock pitcher) the wand always dribbles on me when I’m cleaning it. I think it’s a personal problem.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Melissa L.", "review_title": "Exceptional Coffee!", "review_text": "This Espresso Maker is so beautifully designed! It looks a little intimidating at first, but the videos and instructions are excellent and within no time it will be second nature to you. The machine is able to sense a lot of what needs to be done and guide you through the process. The only "wish" I would have is that during the cleaning process, you need to vacuum out the burr grinder which is a bit of a hassle. But for this level of quality coffee, it is worth it!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jody Bortz", "review_title": "Ninja to the rescue.", "review_text": "Do you want a good cup of coffee? I absolutely love it. The machine I used before used K cups and and that was getting old fast. With fresh coffee beans the coffee is delicious. The machine fits perfectly on my rolling cart. It takes maybe five minutes from start to finish for my caramel macchiato in the morning. And the temperature is perfect. The thing that I love the most about this machine is it comes with a video on how to help you to use it for the first time. It’s very simple to use. If you’re looking for a good espresso machine for the first time, I recommend Ninja.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "jimmy", "review_title": "Best coffee maker I’ve ever bought", "review_text": "It’s definitely the most expensive coffee maker I ever paid for, but it is well worth it. There’s nothing better than warm frost creamer to go in your coffee taste like roasted marshmallows.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "The Ransoms", "review_title": "Ninja luxe Cafe Premier", "review_text": "This machine does a lot, and somehow doesn’t feel overwhelming. The ability to make espresso, drip coffee, and cold brew all in one setup is a huge win, especially if you don’t want three different machines taking over your counter.
The built-in grinder and guided settings make it really easy to get a good cup without having to mess with a bunch of complicated adjustments. Espresso comes out rich and consistent, and the drip coffee is well-balanced. The rapid cold brew is a nice bonus and actually tastes smooth, not watered down.
The milk frother works well and is pretty much hands-off, which is great if you’re not trying to play barista at 6am. Cleanup is also easier than expected for a machine with this many features.

The grinder sounds different, and the setting numbers for getting the proper grind with my favorite beans have shifted, but the motor sounds steadier now and strains less. Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Robb Ryniak", "review_title": "Tips for a genuinely amazing cup of a coffee...", "review_text": "My family has owned this percolator for 6 years now, purchased right here on Amazon in 2010, and I'm about to buy another one for work.
This pot has consistently delivered the best tasting coffee - better than all restaurants we frequent, better than friends and family's coffee... just awesomely, amazingly good. I've had a couple of minor maintenance issues over the years (see below) but they were super easily overcome, and in general this has been a super-reliable and very inexpensive appliance. Honestly, this has to have been one of my most favorite appliance purchases ever. And all for less than $40. Take THAT, you overpriced, overly featured drip machines that make lousy coffee!! ;-)
*TIPS*
With this, and any other stainless percolator, there are some basic guidelines to follow that aren't necessarily in the manual:
1. DO NOT use a paper filter. Ever. Use the metal basket ONLY. The holes are tiny enough to allow the coffee through, but to keep 99.9% of the gains in. Using the metal basket without a paper filter allows the flavor oils that naturally exist in the coffee bean to STAY in the coffee and contribute to its amazing and full flavor. If you use a paper filter, you'll lose the oils and get an "over-extracted" flavor that's more bitter than bold... so don't use a paper filter, follow the instructions, and you're GOLDEN - perfect coffee every time. The chair is great. I have been looking for a chair for several months, and finally settled on this one. My only hang-up was that I really wanted genuine leather, which this chair is not. The chairs with genuine leather are either (a) priced well over $1k, or (b) are cheap junk. This chair replaces my old, genuine leather chair, that was less than 3 years old. Unfortunately, it fell into the "cheap junk" category, as I came to find out. I had ordered that chair, just based on the leather...and in fact that is the ONLY part of the chair that held up. I replaced the base when it broke, replaced the hydraulic lift when it broke, and had to re-work the arm rests so they would stop falling off. The sides and back were also deteriorating...so quite literally, the ONLY "good" part of that chair was the actual leather itself.
So, apologies for the back story, but that leads me into the review of this chair. In putting it together, I could easily see that this chair is hands down much more well-made than my old one. Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Aṃazon", "review_title": "A great budget friendly 4K monitor that makes a lot of sense for work, school, and everyday use", "review_text": "This Samsung ViewFinity S7 is the kind of monitor that makes the most sense if you care more about a sharp picture and useful screen space than gaming features.
The 27 inch size with 4K resolution gives you a lot of room to work with, and text looks especially crisp. That makes it a really nice fit for web browsing, spreadsheets, schoolwork, research, office work, and having multiple windows open at the same time. I think students would get a lot of use out of it for exactly that reason.
I also think this would be a great monitor for seniors. With Windows or macOS scaling turned up, you can make text and icons larger without giving up the sharpness that comes with a 4K screen. That gives you a nice balance between readability and screen space instead of everything looking oversized or blurry.
The picture quality is very good for everyday use. The IPS panel gives you natural looking colors and good viewing angles, and the matte screen helps keep reflections under control. Samsung also includes Eye Saver Mode and flicker reduction, which are nice features if you spend a lot of time in front of a monitor.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "MK", "review_title": "A Great 4K Monitor for Coding and Everyday Work", "review_text": "A 27-inch 4K monitor hits a really nice sweet spot for productivity because you get an enormous jump in sharpness without taking up a huge amount of desk space. That is what I like most about the Samsung ViewFinity S7. Text looks incredibly crisp, small UI elements are easy to read, and I can fit a surprising amount on screen without everything feeling cramped.
The 3840 x 2160 resolution is especially noticeable for the kind of work where I am staring at text all day. Coding, spreadsheets, documents, and web browsing all benefit from the extra pixel density, and it makes lower-resolution 27-inch monitors look a little soft once you get used to it. I usually use some display scaling rather than running everything at native size, but even then the added resolution makes fonts and icons look much cleaner.
The IPS panel is another good fit for a productivity monitor. Colors look accurate and consistent, and the image holds up well when I am not sitting perfectly centered in front of it. That is useful if I am moving around my desk or showing something on screen to someone beside me. The matte finish also helps keep reflections under control without making the picture look dull.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jakey Saxx", "review_title": "solid monitor", "review_text": "its big, it works, just make sure your docking station is compatible with 4K", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "JD_reviews", "review_title": "Excellent 27" 4K productivity monitor without unnecessary extras", "review_text": "Pros:
Sharp 3840×2160 4K resolution
Excellent text clarity
Bright IPS display
No noticeable backlight bleed
HDR10 support
HDMI and DisplayPort inputs
PIP/PBP support
100×100 VESA compatible
Great straightforward productivity monitor", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Andromeda", "review_title": "Very nice display, great office and general monitor, easy setup, 100x100 VESA", "review_text": "Display quality on this 27" monitor is excellent, details are sharp and it's very, very good for photo editing and similar detail work, or for detailed text work. There were no display defects on arrival, such as missing pixels and even without eye saver mode the IPS panel is easy to work with.
It arrived well packed and with a long power lead combined with small power brick. The cable length from monitor connector to power brick is approximately 56" excluding connectors, and similar from power brick to power plug.
Setting up is as easy as installing the monitor and power cables, and powering on. There is one point to be aware of if setting up for Display Port operation - the default input mode is set to HDMI, without auto-switching. Changing to Display Port and auto-switching is managed via the On-Screen Display (OSD). This is a little inconvenient, but certainly not unique, since it is accessed from the rear of the monitor, not via edge switches. In DP mode the display is rock solid, with no aberrations.
I tried out Game Mode, also accessed via the OSD, but found it too bright to use for general use, so left it off since this isn't intended as the perfect gaming monitor (although there is a lot of customization for colors etc, and Game Mode is easily accessible at any time).", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Wheels in Idaho", "review_title": "Sharp 4K IPS panel, great color accuracy, premium build", "review_text": "Upgraded to this 27 inch ViewFinity from a lower resolution monitor and the difference for day to day work has been noticeable right away. The 4K UHD resolution on an IPS panel gives sharp, accurate detail whether I'm reading dense spreadsheets, reviewing documentation, or working on anything with fine text, and colors stay consistent even viewing from an angle thanks to the IPS panel type.
HDR10 support adds a nice bump in contrast and color range when viewing HDR content, deeper blacks and brighter highlights without the image looking blown out or flat. For general productivity use it's not something I lean on constantly, but it's a welcome bonus when watching video or reviewing photo and video work.
Build quality of the stand and overall unit feels premium, matching what I'd expect from Samsung at this tier, no wobble in the stand and the bezels are slim enough that the screen doesn't feel boxed in. Ergonomic adjustment on the stand allowed me to get the height and angle dialed in for comfortable extended use, which matters a lot when you're staring at a screen most of the day.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "ZackL", "review_title": "Great monitor with natural colors. Works great with a Mac Studio.", "review_text": "This is a great monitor. The slim bezel and lightweight build give it a very clean, look and there's a nice cable organizing clip built into the back of the stand, which I find useful.
Picture quality is excellent with no dead pixels and images look natural, not over sharpened and there is no ghosting. I'm using it on a Mac Studio and, in addition to the great image quality, the connection has been flawless. The native resolution works fine with the Mac Studio, even though the computer is optimized for 5K - 8K.
There are a few things I'd improve. The color controls could be more granular and a bit more intuitive to navigate. I'd also like slightly more brightness available. The stand is tilt-only, with no height adjustment and no swivel. The monitor controls would be easier to use if they were located on the bottom or side rather than the back.
One unexpected benefit is that with other all other monitors I've used, I couldn't drag a window to span across both screens in my two-monitor setup (meaning I could move it between the screens, but it was only on one or on the other), but with this one, I can. I hadn't realized that was even dependent on the monitor itself, but apparently it is.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Styx", "review_title": "Sharp, spacious monitor for everyday work", "review_text": "This Samsung 27-inch ViewFinity S7 has been a solid monitor for daily use, especially for work, browsing, streaming, and having multiple windows open at once. The 4K resolution makes text look sharp and clean, which is nice if you spend a lot of time reading documents, emails, or spreadsheets. The 27-inch size feels like a good middle ground because it gives plenty of screen space without taking over the whole desk.
The picture looks clear, and the IPS panel helps the colors stay consistent even when I’m not sitting directly in front of it. Videos and photos look crisp, and HDR10 adds a little extra depth, though I wouldn’t expect it to feel like a high-end TV. I also appreciate the Eye Saver Mode for longer sessions because the screen feels easier to look at when working for a while.
Setup was straightforward, and the monitor has a clean, simple design that fits well with a home office or regular desk setup. The stand works fine, but it is pretty basic, so anyone who wants more height or angle adjustment may want to use a separate monitor arm. Overall, it’s a nice choice if you want a clear 4K display for everyday productivity, school, or casual entertainment without anything overly complicated.", "review_rating": ""}]

[{"reviewer_name": "CoS", "review_title": "Small, pretty, and very convenient!", "review_text": "This bottle does exactly what it's supposed to do. Yes, it's small, but that's the point. There are definitely pros and cons.
The obvious downside is that I have to refill it a few times throughout the day. On the other hand, it's incredibly convenient. It's not too heavy when full, fits easily in my bag and my spin bike's water bottle holder, and the locking latch doubles as a carrying handle. I've even clip it to my fanny pack with a carabiner for hands-free trips to the gym.
It keeps drinks cold exceptionally well. I usually fill it with ice, and it lasts all day and overnight.
One unexpected benefit is that it fits perfectly in the portable "ADHD caddy" I carry from room to room, which has actually helped me stay hydrated because my water is always with me. (I wrote a separate review about that caddy if you're curious.)
If you want a bottle that travels well, doesn't leak, and keeps your drinks ice cold, this is a great choice.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "MRuss", "review_title": "Best water bottle ever", "review_text": "I purchased this bottle just to try out in the summer of 2023. It is now the summer of 2026 and I still use it multiple times a week (only because I now have multiple Owalas and I have just ordered my third Owala FreeSip). I have used so many cups—Stanleys, Yetis, Hydrojugs, Hydroflask, etc—and the Owala is still my favorite. Here’s my favorite things about it:
LEAKPROOF! This is the biggest one. I can throw it my bag and trust that everything will stay dry.
THE SPOUT! Hands down the best spout I’ve ever used. I love that I can sip through the straw but then close the lid and keep my straw clean and not have any spills if it tips over. And then it also gives me the option to absolutely inhale water if I’m about to shrivel up from dehydration. I think this alone is why I now own three in different sizes.
STAYS COLD! The 32 ounce holds ice for quite a while. It varies depending on how often I refill it but if I’m not constantly refilling it, it will hold ice for about 24 hours.
THE SIZES! I love the size options. My original one was a 32 ounce and is a great middle ground for me. It holds enough water that I’m not refilling it every hour but it’s not huge. It’s great for work and this bottle will be going to live at my job. I just ordered the 40 ounce for home because I want a little more volume when I’m outside gardening but I can’t say much about the 40 ounce size yet. I also have a 16 ounce (kids size) that I use when I leave the house. It fits in a lot of my bags and it’s leakproof so I always have cold water with me. It’s perfect especially since I’m on medication that causes dehydration if I’m not careful.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Karina de Ormo", "review_title": "A thermos with the perfect nozzle and spills", "review_text": "The FreeSip system. The lid also closes very well and so far I have not had problems with spills.
It keeps the water cold for many hours and the large size really helps me drink more water during the day. Despite its capacity, it feels comfortable to wear thanks to the lid handle.
I also really liked the design. The color is beautiful, it looks modern and the bottle feels resistant and of good quality.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Abigail Jones", "review_title": "Our favorite water bottles", "review_text": "Owala water bottles for the win! These are hands-down our favorite water bottles. We have tried just about every popular brand out there—Yeti, Stanley, Hydro Flask, and others—and the Owala is the one that everyone in our family consistently reaches for.
I absolutely love the versatility of the lid. You can use the built-in straw when you want to sip, or easily flip it open and drink straight from the opening. Having both options in one bottle is incredibly convenient, especially when you're on the go.
The color combinations are also so fun! There are so many options to choose from, and the colors and designs make the bottles feel a little more personal and fun to use.
Durability is another huge selling point. These bottles get used constantly and have been dropped and knocked around, yet they hold up extremely well. They seem much less prone to denting than some of the other brands we've tried, which is especially important when they're being used by kids.
And, of course, they keep drinks really cold! We can fill them with ice and water, and they stay cold for hours. The lid also seals extremely well—we have never had an issue with them leaking in a bag.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Kelly", "review_title": "My Favorite Water Bottle", "review_text": "I’ve tried many water bottles over the years, and there are a few qualities I always look for. This bottle delivers on every single one.
#1 – Easy to clean. Bottles with fold-up straws tend to trap moisture and get musty over time, and they’re especially hard to clean where the mouthpiece connects to the lid. This bottle avoids that completely. The straw mouthpiece is integrated into the wide-mouthed spout under the lid, so there aren’t all those little crevices that are so difficult to clean.
#2 – Keeps water cold for a long time. This one does an excellent job of keeping my water cold for hours.
#3 – A carry handle that doesn’t get in the way. I LOVE the carry loop on this cup. It folds down over the lid when you’re not using it, so it doesn’t stick out or get in the way.
#4 – A practical size. The opening is large enough to fit my 2” x 2” ice cubes, but the cup itself is still narrow enough to fit in a standard cup holder.
Overall, this checks every box I look for in a water bottle. The bottle itself feels sturdy and good quality, and the lid closes securely and has a handle that makes it easy to carry. The colors are also really fun and vibrant.
My only concern is the coating on the outside. It feels like it may be somewhat easy to scratch, especially since this is going to be used by a kid and tossed into bags, taken to school, etc. We’ll see how it holds up over time!
Overall, though, I’m really happy with it.
I’ll update my review once I find out how sturdy it is.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jennifer", "review_title": "My New Favorite Water Bottle!", "review_text": "I absolutely love this Owala FreeSip water bottle!
