The FreeSip design is my favorite part because I can either sip through the built-in straw or tilt the bottle back when I want a bigger drink.
It keeps my water cold for a long time, and the stainless steel construction feels sturdy and high quality. The lid closes securely, and I love the sleek Very, Very Dark color—it looks simple, stylish, and goes with everything.
It’s perfect for the gym, work, errands, or just keeping next to me throughout the day. Great size, keeps drinks cold, comfortable to use, and absolutely worth it.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Dixty", "review_title": "Produto perfeito, mas a entrega deixa muito a desejar.", "review_text": "Vamos lá, primeiramente que eu AMEI a garrafa, estava super ansiosa pela chegada dela e não me arrependo em absolutamente NADA de ter comprado. Ela mantém a água gelada por MUITO tempo(se você for como eu q é curioso em saber quando tempo exatamente, um ótimo exemplo foi que eu coloquei água nela SEM GELO ás 16 da tarde e no dia seguinte ás 8 horas quando acordei ainda estava gelada como se tivesse acabado de sair do filtro d'água, lembrando que meu filtro tem agua gelada). O canudo dela é sensacional e super prático, mas também recomendo comprar uma daquelas escovinhas pra limpar.
Além disso, ela é muito linda e grande. Eu comprei a de 945ml e tá perfeita pra mim, já que tem uma alça e o material externo da garrafa não é escorregadio ao toque.
Agora falando dos pontos negativos, o único ponto negativo que eu tenho a mencionar aqui sobre essa garrafa é a entrega. Vi muitas pessoas reclamando sobre a demora da entrega e realmente aconteceu comigo também, o prazo pra envio é ENORME, acredito que seja por causa da quantidade de pessoas que compram essa garrafa, então demorou MUITO pra enviarem, aprox um mês. A entrega em si depois do envio foi de uma semana +/-, então acredito que seja mesmo uma coisa de estoque.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Fernanda Raquel Freitas de Sousa Rolim", "review_title": "Não vaza", "review_text": "Muito boa, não vaza, conserva a temperatura.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Lin", "review_title": "Love", "review_text": "Did not include the green ”cover” as shown.
Other than that, I adore this bottle!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Valentina", "review_title": "Molto soddisfatta!", "review_text": "Un po' cara rispetto alla media, ma ne vale la spesa! Tieni molto bene la temperatura, ma soprattutto la possibilità di bere a suzione grazie alla cannuccia, premette l'utilizzo facilitato anche durante la guida!
I colori sono fantastici!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Christian", "review_title": "La meilleure bouteille d'eau, tout simplement incassable et ultra-stylée !", "review_text": "Si vous hésitez encore, foncez les yeux fermés ! Je suis complètement sous le charme de ma nouvelle bouteille Owala.
Les couleurs : La palette de couleurs (ce mélange de rose et de touches orangées/corail) est juste magnifique en vrai, encore plus belle que sur les photos ! Le fini mat est très agréable en main.
L'isolation thermique : La capacité à garder l'eau glacée est tout simplement impressionnante. Même après des heures ou une longue journée, l'eau reste fraîche comme au premier instant grâce à l'isolation sous vide en acier inoxydable.
Pratique & Capacité : Sa grande contenance en ml est parfaite pour rester bien hydraté(e) toute la journée sans devoir passer son temps à la remplir.
Le fameux couvercle FreeSip : C'est là que la magie Owala opère ! La possibilité de boire soit à la paille intégrée (en restant droit), soit en la penchant comme une bouteille classique est une invention géniale. Le bouton poussoir avec le loquet de sécurité étanche évite absolument toutes les fuites dans le sac.", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: Owala FreeSip Stainless Steel Water Bottle 32 oz Very, Very Dark
Description: About this item                     32-ounce insulated stainless-steel water bottle with a FreeSip spout and push-button lid with lock     Patented FreeSip spout designed for either sipping upright through the built-in straw or tilting back to swig from the spout opening     Protective push-to-open lid keeps spout clean; convenient carry loop doubles as a lock     Double-wall insulation keeps drinks cold for up to 24 hours; wide opening for cleaning and adding ice; cup holder-friendly base     This bottle is not compatible with standard automotive cupholders; it is best secured in cup holder organizers, door pockets, or bags during transport                ›  See more product details
Category: Home & Kitchen,Kitchen & Dining,Storage & Organization,Thermoses,Insulated Beverage Containers,Thermoses
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "CoS", "review_title": "Small, pretty, and very convenient!", "review_text": "This bottle does exactly what it's supposed to do. Yes, it's small, but that's the point. There are definitely pros and cons.
The obvious downside is that I have to refill it a few times throughout the day. On the other hand, it's incredibly convenient. It's not too heavy when full, fits easily in my bag and my spin bike's water bottle holder, and the locking latch doubles as a carrying handle. I've even clip it to my fanny pack with a carabiner for hands-free trips to the gym.
It keeps drinks cold exceptionally well. I usually fill it with ice, and it lasts all day and overnight.
One unexpected benefit is that it fits perfectly in the portable "ADHD caddy" I carry from room to room, which has actually helped me stay hydrated because my water is always with me. (I wrote a separate review about that caddy if you're curious.)
If you want a bottle that travels well, doesn't leak, and keeps your drinks ice cold, this is a great choice.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "MRuss", "review_title": "Best water bottle ever", "review_text": "I purchased this bottle just to try out in the summer of 2023. It is now the summer of 2026 and I still use it multiple times a week (only because I now have multiple Owalas and I have just ordered my third Owala FreeSip). I have used so many cups—Stanleys, Yetis, Hydrojugs, Hydroflask, etc—and the Owala is still my favorite. Here’s my favorite things about it:
LEAKPROOF! This is the biggest one. I can throw it my bag and trust that everything will stay dry.
THE SPOUT! Hands down the best spout I’ve ever used. I love that I can sip through the straw but then close the lid and keep my straw clean and not have any spills if it tips over. And then it also gives me the option to absolutely inhale water if I’m about to shrivel up from dehydration. I think this alone is why I now own three in different sizes.
STAYS COLD! The 32 ounce holds ice for quite a while. It varies depending on how often I refill it but if I’m not constantly refilling it, it will hold ice for about 24 hours.
THE SIZES! I love the size options. My original one was a 32 ounce and is a great middle ground for me. It holds enough water that I’m not refilling it every hour but it’s not huge. It’s great for work and this bottle will be going to live at my job. I just ordered the 40 ounce for home because I want a little more volume when I’m outside gardening but I can’t say much about the 40 ounce size yet. I also have a 16 ounce (kids size) that I use when I leave the house. It fits in a lot of my bags and it’s leakproof so I always have cold water with me. It’s perfect especially since I’m on medication that causes dehydration if I’m not careful.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Karina de Ormo", "review_title": "A thermos with the perfect nozzle and spills", "review_text": "The FreeSip system. Being able to drink directly through the nozzle or use the integrated sorbet seems super practical to me, especially when I'm busy or driving. The lid also closes very well and so far I have not had problems with spills.
It keeps the water cold for many hours and the large size really helps me drink more water during the day. Despite its capacity, it feels comfortable to wear thanks to the lid handle.
I also really liked the design. The color is beautiful, it looks modern and the bottle feels resistant and of good quality.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Abigail Jones", "review_title": "Our favorite water bottles", "review_text": "Owala water bottles for the win! These are hands-down our favorite water bottles. We have tried just about every popular brand out there—Yeti, Stanley, Hydro Flask, and others—and the Owala is the one that everyone in our family consistently reaches for.
I absolutely love the versatility of the lid. You can use the built-in straw when you want to sip, or easily flip it open and drink straight from the opening. Having both options in one bottle is incredibly convenient, especially when you're on the go.
The color combinations are also so fun! There are so many options to choose from, and the colors and designs make the bottles feel a little more personal and fun to use.
Durability is another huge selling point. These bottles get used constantly and have been dropped and knocked around, yet they hold up extremely well. They seem much less prone to denting than some of the other brands we've tried, which is especially important when they're being used by kids.
And, of course, they keep drinks really cold! We can fill them with ice and water, and they stay cold for hours. The lid also seals extremely well—we have never had an issue with them leaking in a bag.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Kelly", "review_title": "My Favorite Water Bottle", "review_text": "I’ve tried many water bottles over the years, and there are a few qualities I always look for. This bottle delivers on every single one.
#1 – Easy to clean. Bottles with fold-up straws tend to trap moisture and get musty over time, and they’re especially hard to clean where the mouthpiece connects to the lid. This bottle avoids that completely. The straw mouthpiece is integrated into the wide-mouthed spout under the lid, so there aren’t all those little crevices that are so difficult to clean.
#2 – Keeps water cold for a long time. This one does an excellent job of keeping my water cold for hours.
#3 – A carry handle that doesn’t get in the way. I LOVE the carry loop on this cup. It folds down over the lid when you’re not using it, so it doesn’t stick out or get in the way.
#4 – A practical size. The opening is large enough to fit my 2” x 2” ice cubes, but the cup itself is still narrow enough to fit in a standard cup holder.
Overall, this checks every box I look for in a water bottle. I’ve tried a lot of them over the years, and this is easily one of my favorites.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Bubbles", "review_title": "Hiding that lipstick in style!", "review_text": "I freaking love this thing. I'm not a trend person, I go for function. And when my STB SIL got my fiancé a shiney new Stanley I decided it was time to replace my beat up Rtic with the mismatch lid and straw.
I may not follow trends, but I didn't want my fiancé's cup to put mine to absolute shame!
First off, can we all agree that the marshmallow is gorgeous? THIS cup is spectacular. Strange to say that about a water bottle, I know. But since I never jumped on that train, I didn't know what I had been missing out on. Let me tell you what!
The most important things to me is taking care of my service dog. She keeps me safe so her care is paramount to me. This enables me to pour my water into her bowl on the fly, without having to open my bottle past what I would do to drink from it. Quick and easy. That right there was the selling point for me. But as it turns out, there was even more benefit than that.
I don't chug my water but if I did, the chug hole does works fine.
The straw portion is ready to sip from, and it doesn't stick up tall like other water bottle straws. It's JUST tall enough to get the job done. No worry of toppling over because the straw got knocked over by the cat. (Because that happens.)", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "PowersofCali", "review_title": "Love the straw + chug option!", "review_text": "I got this Owala for my son and really like it so far! My favorite feature is that you can drink from either the built-in straw or use the chug opening. It gives him both options without having to switch out lids or pieces, which is really convenient.
The bottle itself feels sturdy and good quality, and the lid closes securely and has a handle that makes it easy to carry. The colors are also really fun and vibrant.
My only concern is the coating on the outside. It feels like it may be somewhat easy to scratch, especially since this is going to be used by a kid and tossed into bags, taken to school, etc. We’ll see how it holds up over time!
Overall, though, I’m really happy with it.
I’ll update my review once I find out how sturdy it is.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jennifer", "review_title": "My New Favorite Water Bottle!", "review_text": "I absolutely love this Owala FreeSip water bottle! The 40 oz size is perfect for keeping me hydrated throughout the day without having to constantly refill it. The FreeSip design is my favorite part because I can either sip through the built-in straw or tilt the bottle back when I want a bigger drink.
It keeps my water cold for a long time, and the stainless steel construction feels sturdy and high quality. The lid closes securely, and I love the sleek Very, Very Dark color—it looks simple, stylish, and goes with everything.
It’s perfect for the gym, work, errands, or just keeping next to me throughout the day. Great size, keeps drinks cold, comfortable to use, and absolutely worth it.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Dixty", "review_title": "Produto perfeito, mas a entrega deixa muito a desejar.", "review_text": "Vamos lá, primeiramente que eu AMEI a garrafa, estava super ansiosa pela chegada dela e não me arrependo em absolutamente NADA de ter comprado. Ela mantém a água gelada por MUITO tempo(se você for como eu q é curioso em saber quando tempo exatamente, um ótimo exemplo foi que eu coloquei água nela SEM GELO ás 16 da tarde e no dia seguinte ás 8 horas quando acordei ainda estava gelada como se tivesse acabado de sair do filtro d'água, lembrando que meu filtro tem agua gelada). O canudo dela é sensacional e super prático, mas também recomendo comprar uma daquelas escovinhas pra limpar.
Além disso, ela é muito linda e grande. Eu comprei a de 945ml e tá perfeita pra mim, já que tem uma alça e o material externo da garrafa não é escorregadio ao toque.
Agora falando dos pontos negativos, o único ponto negativo que eu tenho a mencionar aqui sobre essa garrafa é a entrega. Vi muitas pessoas reclamando sobre a demora da entrega e realmente aconteceu comigo também, o prazo pra envio é ENORME, acredito que seja por causa da quantidade de pessoas que compram essa garrafa, então demorou MUITO pra enviarem, aprox um mês. A entrega em si depois do envio foi de uma semana +/-, então acredito que seja mesmo uma coisa de estoque.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Fernanda Raquel Freitas de Sousa Rolim", "review_title": "Não vaza", "review_text": "Muito boa, não vaza, conserva a temperatura.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Lin", "review_title": "Love", "review_text": "Did not include the green ”cover” as shown.
Other than that, I adore this bottle!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Valentina", "review_title": "Molto soddisfatta!", "review_text": "Un po' cara rispetto alla media, ma ne vale la spesa! Tieni molto bene la temperatura, ma soprattutto la possibilità di bere a suzione grazie alla cannuccia, premette l'utilizzo facilitato anche durante la guida!
I colori sono fantastici!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Christian", "review_title": "La meilleure bouteille d'eau, tout simplement incassable et ultra-stylée !", "review_text": "Si vous hésitez encore, foncez les yeux fermés ! Je suis complètement sous le charme de ma nouvelle bouteille Owala.
Les couleurs : La palette de couleurs (ce mélange de rose et de touches orangées/corail) est juste magnifique en vrai, encore plus belle que sur les photos ! Le fini mat est très agréable en main.
L'isolation thermique : La capacité à garder l'eau glacée est tout simplement impressionnante. Même après des heures ou une longue journée, l'eau reste fraîche comme au premier instant grâce à l'isolation sous vide en acier inoxydable.
Pratique & Capacité : Sa grande contenance en ml est parfaite pour rester bien hydraté(e) toute la journée sans devoir passer son temps à la remplir.
Le fameux couvercle FreeSip : C'est là que la magie Owala opère ! La possibilité de boire soit à la paille intégrée (en restant droit), soit en la penchant comme une bouteille classique est une invention géniale. Le bouton poussoir avec le loquet de sécurité étanche évite absolument toutes les fuites dans le sac.", "review_rating": ""}]

Title: Nalgene 32 oz Wide Mouth Water Bottle
Description: About this item                     FOR EVERYDAY & EVERYTHING: From the office to the outdoors, the Nalgene 32 oz Wide Mouth Water Bottle keeps you hydrated on the go. It's simple, versatile, and practically indestructible – a trusted companion for your everyday adventures.     DURABLE & LEAK-PROOF: This impact-resistant bottle survives drops on trails, streets, and subway floors. The leak-proof lid ensures an airtight seal to prevent bag spills. VERSATILE & EASY TO CLEAN: This wide-mouth travel bottle is dishwasher safe and has curved corners for easy scrubbing. Measurement lines (mL & oz) help with tracking daily water intake, mixing in drink powders, and measuring liquids for backpacking meals.     HEALTHY HYDRATION: Made BPA, BPS, and phthalate-free, this microwave-safe bottle lets you reheat liquids or stir up camp ramen without worry. [{"reviewer_name": "Rita K.", "review_title": "Simple bottle that’s actually easy to use and clean", "review_text": "I really like the simplicity of this water bottle! I got it in the color “cotton,” and it’s honestly such a nice neutral shade, knd of a soft beige that looks way more expensive than it is. The wide mouth is one of my favorite features because it makes cleaning super easy and also makes it easy to add ice. I also really like the ounce/milliliters markings on the side of the bottle, it became surprisingly helpful to me for keeping track of how much water I’m actually drinking throughout the day. This is actually my second Nalgene bottle, I bought this one to replace my older one because plastic bottles should be replaced once in a while, especially after heavy everyday use. My previous one lasted a long time though, which says a lot. The only downside is that because there’s no straw and the opening is pretty wide, drinking from it while walking or moving around can be a little awkward unless you’re careful.
Overall, really happy with it. Simple, durable, lightweight, and super practical, which honestly matters more to me than trendy designs ;)", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "GreenPanda", "review_title": "Nalgene, hard to beat!", "review_text": "Nalgene bottles just work.

For starters the material. Not only is it BPA-free, the Tritan material is perfect for a drinking bottle. It's extremely rugged, in fact Nalgene has gained a reputation for how long their bottles last. It also doesn't leave much of a taste! A lot of my experience with plastic bottles is that you can taste the plastic, the problem persists with metal as well. Nalgene bottles have a fairly neutral taste. It's also very resistant to trapping odors and tastes. My problem with alternatives is that if you hold coffee in them for a long time, then your water tastes like coffee even after a clean.
1L is a perfect amount of water to hold in my opinion. It's enough to be usable, but not overkill to where it's not a functional bottle. It's great for day to day use as well, I find myself finishing a Nalgene just fine. The size is great in this aspect, it doesn't waste space with insulation. Wide Mouth Water Bottle in the clear finish is my new absolute favorite. Title: Owala FreeSip Stainless Steel Water Bottle 32 oz Boneyard
Description: About this item                     32-ounce insulated stainless-steel water bottle with a FreeSip spout and push-button lid with lock     Patented FreeSip spout designed for either sipping upright through the built-in straw or tilting back to swig from the spout opening     Protective push-to-open lid keeps spout clean; convenient carry loop doubles as a lock     Double-wall insulation keeps drinks cold for up to 24 hours; wide opening for cleaning and adding ice; cup holder-friendly base     This bottle is not compatible with standard automotive cupholders; it is best secured in cup holder organizers, door pockets, or bags during transport                ›  See more product details
Category: Home & Kitchen,Kitchen & Dining,Storage & Organization,Thermoses,Insulated Beverage Containers,Thermoses
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "CoS", "review_title": "Small, pretty, and very convenient!", "review_text": "This bottle does exactly what it's supposed to do. Yes, it's small, but that's the point. There are definitely pros and cons.
The obvious downside is that I have to refill it a few times throughout the day. On the other hand, it's incredibly convenient. It's not too heavy when full, fits easily in my bag and my spin bike's water bottle holder, and the locking latch doubles as a carrying handle. I've even clip it to my fanny pack with a carabiner for hands-free trips to the gym.
It keeps drinks cold exceptionally well. I usually fill it with ice, and it lasts all day and overnight.
One unexpected benefit is that it fits perfectly in the portable "ADHD caddy" I carry from room to room, which has actually helped me stay hydrated because my water is always with me. (I wrote a separate review about that caddy if you're curious.)
If you want a bottle that travels well, doesn't leak, and keeps your drinks ice cold, this is a great choice.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "MRuss", "review_title": "Best water bottle ever", "review_text": "I purchased this bottle just to try out in the summer of 2023. It is now the summer of 2026 and I still use it multiple times a week (only because I now have multiple Owalas and I have just ordered my third Owala FreeSip). I have used so many cups—Stanleys, Yetis, Hydrojugs, Hydroflask, etc—and the Owala is still my favorite. Here’s my favorite things about it:
LEAKPROOF! This is the biggest one. I can throw it my bag and trust that everything will stay dry.
THE SPOUT! Hands down the best spout I’ve ever used. I love that I can sip through the straw but then close the lid and keep my straw clean and not have any spills if it tips over. And then it also gives me the option to absolutely inhale water if I’m about to shrivel up from dehydration. I think this alone is why I now own three in different sizes.
STAYS COLD! The 32 ounce holds ice for quite a while. It varies depending on how often I refill it but if I’m not constantly refilling it, it will hold ice for about 24 hours.
THE SIZES! I love the size options. My original one was a 32 ounce and is a great middle ground for me. It holds enough water that I’m not refilling it every hour but it’s not huge. It’s great for work and this bottle will be going to live at my job. I just ordered the 40 ounce for home because I want a little more volume when I’m outside gardening but I can’t say much about the 40 ounce size yet. I also have a 16 ounce (kids size) that I use when I leave the house. It fits in a lot of my bags and it’s leakproof so I always have cold water with me. It’s perfect especially since I’m on medication that causes dehydration if I’m not careful.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Karina de Ormo", "review_title": "A thermos with the perfect nozzle and spills", "review_text": "The FreeSip system. Being able to drink directly through the nozzle or use the integrated sorbet seems super practical to me, especially when I'm busy or driving. The lid also closes very well and so far I have not had problems with spills.
It keeps the water cold for many hours and the large size really helps me drink more water during the day. Despite its capacity, it feels comfortable to wear thanks to the lid handle.
I also really liked the design. The color is beautiful, it looks modern and the bottle feels resistant and of good quality.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Abigail Jones", "review_title": "Our favorite water bottles", "review_text": "Owala water bottles for the win! These are hands-down our favorite water bottles. We have tried just about every popular brand out there—Yeti, Stanley, Hydro Flask, and others—and the Owala is the one that everyone in our family consistently reaches for.
I absolutely love the versatility of the lid. You can use the built-in straw when you want to sip, or easily flip it open and drink straight from the opening. Having both options in one bottle is incredibly convenient, especially when you're on the go.
The color combinations are also so fun! There are so many options to choose from, and the colors and designs make the bottles feel a little more personal and fun to use.
Durability is another huge selling point. These bottles get used constantly and have been dropped and knocked around, yet they hold up extremely well. They seem much less prone to denting than some of the other brands we've tried, which is especially important when they're being used by kids.
And, of course, they keep drinks really cold! We can fill them with ice and water, and they stay cold for hours. The lid also seals extremely well—we have never had an issue with them leaking in a bag.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Kelly", "review_title": "My Favorite Water Bottle", "review_text": "I’ve tried many water bottles over the years, and there are a few qualities I always look for. This bottle delivers on every single one.
#1 – Easy to clean. Bottles with fold-up straws tend to trap moisture and get musty over time, and they’re especially hard to clean where the mouthpiece connects to the lid. This bottle avoids that completely. The straw mouthpiece is integrated into the wide-mouthed spout under the lid, so there aren’t all those little crevices that are so difficult to clean.
#2 – Keeps water cold for a long time. This one does an excellent job of keeping my water cold for hours.
#3 – A carry handle that doesn’t get in the way. I LOVE the carry loop on this cup. It folds down over the lid when you’re not using it, so it doesn’t stick out or get in the way.
#4 – A practical size. The opening is large enough to fit my 2” x 2” ice cubes, but the cup itself is still narrow enough to fit in a standard cup holder.
Overall, this checks every box I look for in a water bottle. I’ve tried a lot of them over the years, and this is easily one of my favorites.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Bubbles", "review_title": "Hiding that lipstick in style!", "review_text": "I freaking love this thing. I may not follow trends, but I didn't want my fiancé's cup to put mine to absolute shame!

This enables me to pour my water into her bowl on the fly, without having to open my bottle past what I would do to drink from it. Quick and easy. That right there was the selling point for me. I don't chug my water but if I did, the chug hole does works fine.
The straw portion is ready to sip from, and it doesn't stick up tall like other water bottle straws. It's JUST tall enough to get the job done. (Because that happens.)", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "PowersofCali", "review_title": "Love the straw + chug option!", "review_text": "I got this Owala for my son and really like it so far! The bottle itself feels sturdy and good quality, and the lid closes securely and has a handle that makes it easy to carry. The colors are also really fun and vibrant.
My only concern is the coating on the outside. It feels like it may be somewhat easy to scratch, especially since this is going to be used by a kid and tossed into bags, taken to school, etc. We’ll see how it holds up over time!
Overall, though, I’m really happy with it.
I’ll update my review once I find out how sturdy it is.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jennifer", "review_title": "My New Favorite Water Bottle!", "review_text": "I absolutely love this Owala FreeSip water bottle! The FreeSip design is my favorite part because I can either sip through the built-in straw or tilt the bottle back when I want a bigger drink.

I colori sono fantastici!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Christian", "review_title": "La meilleure bouteille d'eau, tout simplement incassable et ultra-stylée !", "review_text": "Si vous hésitez encore, foncez les yeux fermés ! Je suis complètement sous le charme de ma nouvelle bouteille Owala.
Les couleurs : La palette de couleurs (ce mélange de rose et de touches orangées/corail) est juste magnifique en vrai, encore plus belle que sur les photos ! Le fini mat est très agréable en main.
L'isolation thermique : La capacité à garder l'eau glacée est tout simplement impressionnante. Même après des heures ou une longue journée, l'eau reste fraîche comme au premier instant grâce à l'isolation sous vide en acier inoxydable.
Pratique & Capacité : Sa grande contenance en ml est parfaite pour rester bien hydraté(e) toute la journée sans devoir passer son temps à la remplir.
Le fameux couvercle FreeSip : C'est là que la magie Owala opère ! La possibilité de boire soit à la paille intégrée (en restant droit), soit en la penchant comme une bouteille classique est une invention géniale. Le bouton poussoir avec le loquet de sécurité étanche évite absolument toutes les fuites dans le sac.", "review_rating": ""}]

I've considered stuffing something in there while I'm not wearing them to stretch the toe space out a little, or maybe even trying to operate on the shoes, but I think I'm just going to go ahead and buy a different pair. [{"reviewer_name": "MD", "review_title": "Love the Skechers!!!", "review_text": "For many years I faithfully wore the Nike Air Walk and then, low and behold, they stopped making them! They were one of very few "wide" shoes that Nike made -- plus they were all leather, very light, provided great support and were super comfortable. So, once they were discontinued, I was on the search for a replacement....
I didn't think of Skechers much as a "serious" brand, mostly because I didn't know much about them, but it turns out they do sell some wide fitment shoes, and these, for me, are an absolute great fit! I tried a pair, a few years back, and have faithfully replaced them every time, having once again found a pair of shoes I really love.
They are very similar to the Air Walks, in comfort and durability, although, sadly, they don't last as long as the Nike's did. Then again, they are about half the price! So, I don't feel too bad having to replace these more often. I'd say a pair lasts six to eight months, where the Nike's used to last more than a year, but, as I say, these are a lot more affordable to replace, so I guess it kind of works out, cost wise.
For me, the most important thing is having a pair of shoes that are comfortable, versatile and look good enough to wear to work with good Levi's and a sport shirt, yet can also be used for walks or even light hikes. Since they are all white I have the same problem I had with the white Air Walks, which is that they tend to get dirty kind of quickly, but, like the Air Walks, they also clean up beautifully with some shoe cleaner and a bit of Sneaker whitener, so they tend to look great until they simply wear out -- in my case it is usually the side that eventually blows out -- which was the same on the Air Walks, but just didn't happen as quickly. Even so, six to eight months of life is pretty good to get out of them, considering I wear these pretty often throughout the average week.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "R.E.", "review_title": "Quality for the dollars .", "review_text": "Quality for the Price . Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Hugo Buy That", "review_title": "Caramel is the best value you could ever get in a Ukulele!! WOW", "review_text": "I am new to the world of Ukelele, but I have been playing guitar for more than 30 years.

It has a pickup, onboard tuner and comes with many accessories and a nice pouch to carry them in. Kudos to the folks at Caramel for making it possible to have such a nice instrument at an incredible price. I hope more and more Ukulele lovers and those interested in learning to play this wonderful instrument will discover you as well. I'm going to give the Caramel Baritone a try next.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Nathan", "review_title": "Good sound, greater value!", "review_text": "For what I spent on this ukulele, the overall rate would have been a 5. Here is why the purchase received only 4 Stars. A very small thing I experienced with the uke was the fret board and saddle were very dusty or grey. A little lemon oil helped fix things up with the fretboard and the saddle. That was the only thing. Very minor. With that said, the fretboard and the fret wires were very clean. No sharp frets! It was really in great condition. This is a solid acacia wood ukulele and the sound is a bit quieter than some of my other ukes, but it is still a great ukulele. The pickup and tuner work great, cable is fine, the strap (not my style) but appreciated. The bag could be better. Use your savings and purchase a new case. This is a great starter ukulele or if you have been playing awhile it would be a good pick if you just wanted something different, at a great price.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Nash", "review_title": "Caramel CT204 all solid acacia", "review_text": "This is a very nice looking ukulele. The solid wood grain matches up really well. It has a good tone and intonation up the neck. The only thing that I changed was the string height which was a little high for me. Removed the saddle and sanded down so it is 2.5mm at the 12th fret now. Yes the nut and bridge saddle are bone which is really nice. The onboard electronics work good especially the tuner that I enjoy and is spot on. Very happy with purchase.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "JJeff", "review_title": "Great Uke for the Money", "review_text": "As most reviewers have said, this ukulele is a great value for the money. To get a solid wood ukulele for $119 is unheard of. I'm a uke nerd and have at least a dozen ukuleles from inexpensive to insanely expensive. I was impressed with the quality of the build for the money. The accessories are a nice touch, especially if you're new to ukes. The tone is fantastic and the acacia wood is beautiful. It plays so nicely and the neck is nice and wide for big fingers. Very much plays like a nylon string classical guitar. It came already mostly in tune and with the built in tuner was easy to get and keep in tune. I have three ukuleles and this one is now my go to. Next Ukulele will be a Caramel baritone to complete my collection.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Moon", "review_title": "Incredible value for money.", "review_text": "I've had a solid acacia ukulele for years and I bought this one for my husband's birthday after hearing some very good things about it. Description: About this item                     A unique mini 6-string nylon guitar that is sized like a baritone ukulele (17" scale) and plays like a guitar     The guitalele's tuning is pitched up to "A" (or up to a 4th) at A/D/G/C/E/A.     Nylon Strings     Comes with a soft case bag                 ›  See more product details
Category: Musical Instruments,Instrument Accessories,General Accessories
Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "Eli Thomas", "review_title": "Great little guitar that can play your favorite Uke songs too!", "review_text": "I've been playing this little gem for a week now as a replacement for my full size acoustic that is in dire need of a neck reset. It sits next to my office chair where I can pick it up and play any time. So far it has done a pretty good job of staying in tune with only the usual nylon string settling in. Tone is interesting with a neat, plucky sound and, being tuned to A, it shares the same finger positions on the 4 treble strings as a ukulele. In fact, it is a good sounding baritone ukulele but could be a little bit challenging for some due to closer string spacing compared to a uke. Action is fine and I am in no hurry to change the setup. factory strings seem OK and i will play on them until they wear out. Yamaha states that low or standard tension classical strings can be used and Savarez, D'Addario and DR are recommended brands. No need for special guilele strings.
The finish is very satin and may not be pleasing for those that enjoy glossy guitars though i think it's OK and seems tough enough. My GL1 came with a small blemish in the wood on the back which is an imperfection in the wood itself and not the finish. I would take 1/2 a star for the blemish but quality control is overall pretty good and the fret ends aren't noticeably sharp.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jon", "review_title": "A quality instrument from Yamaha", "review_text": "69 year old guitar hack here. Played electric, and some acoustic guitar in three bands way back in the 1970's. Played acoustic at a wedding. My neighbor bought a Yamaha GL-1 "guitalele" A few years ago, and told me recently that he loves it! A GL-1 is basically a very compact 6 string classical guitar, but, instead of being tuned Eadgbe, it is tuned 5 frets up on each string, so the low and high e's become a's. This means that all the chord shapes I know on a regular guitar can be played in the same positions, but the name of the chord will be different. Example, an e major chord shape on a guitar, will really be an a major on the Yamaha. If I am just playing by myself for myself, there is no problem. If I was to play along with a regular guitar, we would have to work out what key to play in. Also, if I sing and play, then depending on what key I play in, I would have to sing in higher notes.
This thing came quicky to me in Hawaii, and it is in perfect condition! Since it had nylon/classical type strings, it is going to take much longer for the strings to settle down and stop sretching. Way longer than my steel stringers. So, don't write a review after a few days complaining about this. All classical style nylon string guitars do this! Pick it up,tune it, play it, and keep tuning it. The tuners on mine seem just fine. It is a total blast for me to play. It sounds great, especially for the small body size. It has very good volume and sustain too. A bit stingy on the fret markers, both on the fingerboard and side of the neck. If you have big fingers, some chording might be a bit crowded. It doesn't have a truss rod. But, many classical guitars and many other guitaleles don't have them either. I have yet to read a review, or watch a video review, where the owner had a neck warp. In short, I should have bought one of these long ago.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Trevor", "review_title": "I take mine everywhere", "review_text": "I love this thing. I tied a strap to it with some shoe strings, I slap it on my back, get on my bike. I take it with me when I go hiking, to school, to the beach, or anywhere really. The tuning on it is ADGCEA which would be equal to as if you had a capo on a regular guitar's 5th fret, which means that you can play the same chord shapes as a regular guitar, the notes will just be higher.
As far as quality goes, I'm pretty happy with it. Some people said the strings that they got were no good, but I've had mine for about 3 months now and I have no complaints. The strings are very sensitive though. They bend very easily, so sometimes the chords played sound good and other times they might sound a little off. I see as a very delicate instrument.. when I press down my fingers for chords I press them straight down and make sure I'm not bending them. A;so, because they bend easily, it can go out of tune pretty easily too. I tune mine often, to make sure they are good to go. I have always tuned my normal guitars by ear, however I find that it is harder to do with the guitarlele, so I use a tuner usually.
Visually I have no complaints, the wood and finish are nice, the neck has good action and feel, although a small part of me wishes that they had some artwork around the soundhole. As for sound quality, I love it.. the higher strings/notes do stand out more in a way, and definitely have the ukulele sound, but if you play gently enough it creates a nice balance. The resonance is beautiful. It has a very warm, mellow sound. It's pretty loud for it's size too. And it is so versatile, you can play Spanish style chords like Em and Am which sounds awesome (Onda Vaga uses a uke, perfect example, youtube them), .. you can emulate a mandolin to an extent.. I'm not saying it sounds exactly like a mandolin since it obviously can't replicate the resonant-sound of the double layered strings, but it does have the high notes from the strings that at least sound somewhat similar to a mandolin, if you want to cover a song with one. Or you can just play regular songs, normal chord shapes, even powerchords sound good.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Doug", "review_title": "Positive review for serious 6-string players", "review_text": "I'm a 6-string (steel) acoustic fingerstyle/jazz player who was looking to goof around with something small and inexpensive. Wanted to leave a review for the like-minded, or everyone who actually wants to try digging some arpeggios and modes into one of these little things and playing some standards and fingerstyle tunes on a park bench or lawn chair. I've owned some nice instruments and play for hours a day, so the GL1 isn't my first rodeo.
First of all, the build quality is great. Importantly, the tuners are rock solid. Period. Intonation was surprisingly accurate for a $100 instrument - just a tiny, tiny bit sharp at the twelfth fret harmonic, but not noticeable when chording or playing melodies. The frets are perfect - no rough edges (see pictures). The instrument sounds clear and warm and lively. The strings it came with were fine - not rusty or anything - nice and shiny and obviously brand new.
The action out of the box (as pictures show) was pretty high. This is not a criticism of Yamaha or the shipper or anything - one usually has to set up one's own instruments. I'm not great at it, but I know the basics. I took the saddle out and sanded it way down and used some small files on the nut and now it's great. No problem. If you get one and want to do more than gripping open chords, plan on an easy half an hour of set up. Seriously - easy.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Linguo the Grammar Robot", "review_title": "decent, doesn't need to be tuned up a full 4th to sound OK", "review_text": "Mahalo used to make a similar product for less than half the price, so this guy seems a little overpriced to me – but since the Mahalo seems to be discontinued, there's no real competitor, and this hardly breaks the bank. It has entirely acceptable playability, sound, intontation, etc. I especially like to play it like a mandolin, flat-picking single lines, but of course it can play full-chord accompaniments, sounding just like a ukulele but lower. Travels fine, though one thing to note about the classic camp-singalong use is that the nylon strings are suuuuuper sensitive to temperature changes, so it's a bit frustrating playing it outdoors in chilly air next to a hot campfire
– you might need to invest in a steel-string alternative if you can't abide that.
You *can* tune it to standard guitar tuning (E2, A2, D3, ...), which is useful if you want to use it for, say, composing on the go and not get confused about which key you're in – but down there the strings sound like garbage and don't stay in tune. The recommended tuning is up a 4th, which I find a bit high, since you can't even play G2 (de facto a lot of things you play on guitars tend to be in keys like G, D, C ...). One solution is to use the recommended tuning but with "drop G" (lowest string = G2), which sounds fine. But you also can just tune the whole thing a major 3rd higher than a guitar (major 2nd lower than the recommended tuning), rather than a 4th (so: G2, C3, F3 ....) which IMHO sounds just as good and stays in tune just as well. (I just personally keep getting confused by the mental arithmetic that requires – what you expect to be a G major chord is actually Bb major ... etc.)", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Sean Snyder", "review_title": "Best Guitar Ever", "review_text": "This is THE starter guitar. Can be tuned to E-Standard with high tension strings (I love D'addario xtc46ff).
Every school across the country should have a set of these in their music room. Anyone who hates the bulk of a full size guitar, the early pain of metal strings, or the poor quality of cheap guitars, this is the answer.
The finish is not perfect, but the intonation is great. The lack of a truss rod means the neck is a tad thick for its size, however, this (thick neck) is an advantage for adult hands and reduces the neck dive you'd see in small guitars like this.
If you are having trouble with tuning, ensure the saddle is in the properly centered as it's held down by the strings in its slot and not actually attached to the guitar which allows you to upgrade or modify it in the future if you see fit. The strings are tied on, but the bridge will be fine with ball-ends, at least in E-Standard; they may leave indents, but I never lost confidence in the structure. The tuning machines take a light touch but are certainly functional and precise.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Monsterz", "review_title": "Well built and fun to play...", "review_text": "From what I can see, the bracing and kerfed lining is top notch. It has a bright tone which is nice. Upgraded to a bone nut and saddle which slightly improved overall tone. Action was a bit high at first so I slid out the saddle and sanded off about 1.8mm and later matched it to the new bone saddle and as for the nut, the stock one was slightly larger so had to buy one that wasn't fitted having to shape it to match.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Tom and Laurie", "review_title": "Here is the "real deal" review on this Guitalele", "review_text": "I've been playing, and writing music since 1984. I play a myriad of instruments and currently, I write and record commercially licensed music under BMI, Inc.
My Wife bought this instrument for me for a holiday gift, but I wanted to check it out before it gets wrapped.. just in case of damage. I am glad that I did. I also know how to setup and do maintenance on both electronic and acoustic instruments.
The good things about this instrument:
This instrument sounds really good, as it seems to be structurally sound. I do not see any cracks in the body or missing glue around the neck joint.
The strings are nice wrapped around to tuning pags.
The open faced tuners and gears seem to be of a higher quality than others that I have seen.
The bad things about this instrument:
The bridge saddle is WAY too high. I have no issues in regards to setting up a bridge saddle, but I expected Yamaha to be a "bit more" on the quality control side of things and at least have the saddle to a more "normal" height.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Albin Gierun", "review_title": "albin", "review_text": "Jag är väldigt nöjd!", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Vadzim Veleshka", "review_title": "Good quality and sound", "review_text": "Bought this guitalele and my expectations were justified.
It very comfortable small guitar for travel and training for me.
Sound very good: include all frets and play chords.
My variant has few scratches but for me it is not a problem and I think in common quality is good.
Also it has good price.
When I use it tune it to E (recommended A) and it’s sound good, string tension also normal with it.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Joel De la O", "review_title": "Excelente producto, lo recomiendo, buen sonido y cómodo.", "review_text": "Excelente producto, lo recomiendo, buen sonido y cómodo.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Mr. R. Dyer", "review_title": "A nice little guitar for the price", "review_text": "At this price level I had low expectations, but having respect for the Yamaha brand I took a chance and ordered the guitar, half expecting to send it back it it proved a disappointment.
It didn’t disappoint at all. As an experienced player of various full size acoustic guitars I must admit this little guitar is surprisingly well made and pleasant to play for such an economy price.
TBH I didn’t buy it for myself, it was supposed to be an alternative instrument for my Ukelele playing partner to progress to. She didn’t like it, because two extra strings aid a step to far for her. Ah we’ll never mind I tried.
Also I hope to use it to teach guitar to my 8 year old grandchild but haven’t introduced it to him yet. The body size is ideal for him, and the classical type nylon strings should be easier for him. However the neck width is about the same as a full size guitar and flat rather than radiused, which is not ideal for small hands. Also due to the necessarily short neck the tuning cannot be standard EADGBE like a full size so that’s an obstacle to learning the fretboard for later progression to a full size guitar when he’s older.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Fran Pérez Bauer", "review_title": "Mucho mejor de lo que me esperaba", "review_text": "La verdad es que había leído mucho de este producto antes de comprarlo y, una vez lo he recibido, me ha sorprendido gratamente.
Las calidades de la madera son muy muy buenas, la acción de las cuerdas es correcta y el sonido acorde a la dimensión de la caja del instrumento. Llevo años tocando la guitarra y quería ésta para estar en casa tranquilo en el sofá. La afinación en La no es un problema. La puedes afinar con un afinador de click en modo cromático. Mantiene la afinación muy bien desde el principio y las cuerdas venían nuevas, para nada oxidadas y no se estropean con los trastes como decían algunos. La funda es mucho mejor de lo que yo esperaba con un ligero grosor y un asa.
El problema que dice la gente de que la afinación es diferente no es ningún problema. Puedes tocar las mismas canciones pero suenan un poco más agudas, pero ningún problema. Antes de comprar el guitalele prueba con tu guitarra con una cejilla en el quinto traste y así te haces una idea de cómo suena el guitalele.

[{"reviewer_name": "Jon", "review_title": "My take on this 30" classical guitar", "review_text": "I have been playing the heck out of this 1/4 size classical nylon guitar and it's time for my review. I am no beginner. I call myself a guitar hack, as my technical knowledge of music theory is um, spotty. I am a full sized 71 year old adult 5'8" with average sized hands. I enjoy playing the smaller sized guitars and never expected this little guy to boom out like a 41" dreadnot guitar. It has a 20" scale and is 30" end to end.
It arrived quickly and I saw no visible damage. As for tuning it? I need to say we live on the big island Puna District. We leave our windows open always. The climate, humidity, etc make it impossible for any hollow body acoustic to stay in tune overnight. Ever. Tune it in the early day, and it will go sharp overnight. Having said that, the tuners are just okay. They do the job. The guitar has a decent finish. I am going to add fret markers on the side of the neck just like on my steel string acoustics. Classical guitars have few fret markers, and I need the full set. It comes with a bare minimum gig bag with no real padding and a storage pocket. Spare set of strings, A capo, and a strap. Has a strap pin in the end of the body and none at the top, but the strap has a string to tie that end onto the neck. No tuner came with it. Too bad because I have bought four Pyle acoustics and they came with great rechargeable tuners that I love. The neck seems straight and does not have a truss rod. Many classical guitars, even full sized ones like Yamaha do not have truss rods. This one has no "kerfing" inside. My Pyle 34" steel string acoustic has full kerfing. This 30" is tuned to standard guitar tuning, EADGBE. I'm quite sure, with the right strings, one could tune it down five frets to A and call it a guitelele, like my Yamaha GL-1. I plan to leave it standard tuning. It developed a bit of a fret buzz caused by the 3rd fret. When pressing down the D string the second fret it would buzz. The harder you picked that string, the worse it was. I agonized whether I should send it back or not for a couple weeks. Then, after a particularly hot dry spell here, the buzzing quite. I have played this every day. I like to grab my guitar whenever I want and I may pick it up and play 10-15 times a day. I have grown to really love this handy little classical and enjoy the nylon strings and sound it gives me is very nice! I am going to install a piezo pickup inside the body and will have to drill a small hole for the input jack. I could see myself playing one or two of my original songs at an open mic night using one of my amps. I'm a blues oriented player. I like I play slide, and I often use a slide with this guitar. I tune the high E sting down 2 frets to a D, as it really gives a fuller sound with a slide. I love this little bugger and would buy it again. Title: Enya NOVA GO SP1 Carbon Fiber 35-Inch Smart Acoustic-Electric Travel Guitar
Description: About this item                     WHY CARBON FIBER - Nova Go SP1 is made of carbon fiber composite material, which means it's impervious to temperature and humidity change. Taking it on travels, to chill on a beach with the hot bright sun up above, or to a hiking trip deep in a mountain, or even further to shoot some beautiful Instagram posts in a snow land, this Nova Go SP1 carbon fiber acoustic-electric guitar would stay stable, with no warp nor cracks. That's the definite edge of carbon fiber guitars.     WHERE THINGS GET INTERESTING - The absolute differentiator of this guitar is that it’s equipped with the SP1 pickup system. It gets you reverb, delay, and fusion effects on your bare guitar, unplugged. No pedals nor amps are needed. There’s a little speaker inside the body of the guitar, which produces these effects sound, and it can be also used for music playback via Bluetooth.     A PRODUCTIVITY WORKHORSE - SP1 pickup system not only allows you to have tons of fun unplugged. But if you plug it into an amp or PA, this Nova Go SP1 carbon fiber acoustic-electric guitar becomes a workhorse for you to gig with. What’s more, SP1 comes with USB On-The-Go connectivity. You can plug it directly into your phone or PC to record any creative ideas without needing an audio interface.     SOLID BUILD & EASY TO PLAY - The body of this Nova Go SP1 carbon fiber acoustic-electric Guitarra is 1/2 sized (35 in.), molded all in one piece, meaning that the bridge is a cohesive part of the top, not glued upon like traditional acoustic guitars. It would never snap or fall off. Meanwhile, we've put a truss rod into the neck, giving your more adjustability for the string action, even though the factory setup is already optimum. Also, the Zero Fret feature is added for smoother tuning.     PRACTICAL ACCESSORIES - This Nova Go SP1 acoustic-electric carbon fiber guitar comes with a gig bag, and the packaging is colorful and delicately designed. You can send it straight as a gift to someone you love or care about. A hexagon wrench is also included for you to adjust the string action. A USB Type-C cable is there to charge the pickup system, system update, and digital output. We’ve also included an instrument cable in the package.                 ›  See more product details

Reviews:
[{"reviewer_name": "A Discerning Buyer", "review_title": "The Best Amp I own", "review_text": "This is the best amp I have owned. It sounds glorious and looks beautiful. I have an old VOX DA5 which has no app and sounds anemic in large spaces but sounds very good in small spaces. I also have a Spark 2 which is very good and has many decent tones, especially with AI engine, but doesn't come even close to THR30ii. While this one is almost twice the price of Spark 2, I would recommend it over spark 2 any day. What THR cannot easily do that Spark 2 can is to create tones by just telling it - "give me a Ken Burrell tone from Midnight blue" gives something that is close enough. And despite not having an AI capability like Spark 2 has, I prefer this amp for its tone and sound. The feature I have used is to download tones (I think there are 40 or so tones) and save them on the amp. Those tones are all better sounding than Spark 2 tones. Also, the bluetooth audio capability in this is far superior to Spark 2 which sometimes distorts sound. I suspect that as I use Spark 2 in a big city where airwaves might be saturated with wifi and bluetooth signals I have experienced some connection issues on Spark 2. Overall, I would highly recommend this amp.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Truman B.", "review_title": "Everything I needed in an amp.", "review_text": "I've gotten to the point in life to where ease factors into my guitar playing time. It takes me 5 seconds to turn this on and get great tone, the fact it's battery powered means I can go where my family is not. The wireless dongle you buy separately makes the unit completely wireless and is worth the 100 dollars. Then there is the tone, this thing sounds incredible and is very easy to tweak. Then, when you add the wireless capability for both streaming via Bluetooth and then using the Line 6 G10t for wireless guitar with it, just leaves all the others in the dust!
The new app!
The Yamaha app looks just like the knobs on the top of the amp for the interface. It allows you to adjust it in real time to tweak, then if you want to save it - you can save it to one of the three banks of five patches. Very simple and straightforward to use.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Matt Pedro", "review_title": "I love this amp!", "review_text": "This is the perfect little home practice amp, especially if you get the wireless bug for your guitar. It is a bit expensive, considering that for the same money, you could buy a big, powerfull amp that you could play gigs with, but as convenient as this little amp is, I dont have a single regret about spending the money to buy it, and if I were ever so inclined, the line-outs on it could be used to plug into something big enough for a gig setting.", "review_rating": ""}, {"reviewer_name": "Jean L.", "review_title": "Wireless amp!", "review_text": "Good sounding amp. [{"reviewer_name": "A Discerning Buyer", "review_title": "The Best Amp I own", "review_text": "This is the best amp I have owned. It sounds glorious and looks beautiful. I have an old VOX DA5 which has no app and sounds anemic in large spaces but sounds very good in small spaces. I also have a Spark 2 which is very good and has many decent tones, especially with AI engine, but doesn't come even close to THR30ii. While this one is almost twice the price of Spark 2, I would recommend it over spark 2 any day. What THR cannot easily do that Spark 2 can is to create tones by just telling it - "give me a Ken Burrell tone from Midnight blue" gives something that is close enough. And despite not having an AI capability like Spark 2 has, I prefer this amp for its tone and sound. The feature I have used is to download tones (I think there are 40 or so tones) and save them on the amp. Those tones are all better sounding than Spark 2 tones. Also, the bluetooth audio capability in this is far superior to Spark 2 which sometimes distorts sound. I suspect that as I use Spark 2 in a big city where airwaves might be saturated with wifi and bluetooth signals I have experienced some connection issues on Spark 2. I use THR30ii in a place where there is zero bluetooth and wifi density and that is why I have never experienced any connection problems.
